title: Local Protocol Emulator
content: Develop Paxeer X applications against real native protocol transitions, local signing identities and verifiable receipts. Develop Paxeer X applications against real native protocol transitions, local signing identities and verifiable receipts.

title: What the emulator provides
content: The emulator runs a local gateway around the native core transition engine. It provides deterministic development workflows for accounts, payments, canonical activities and Programs, with a sequencer identity that clients explicitly trust. Local prefunding supports repeatable scenarios without moving production value. Surface Purpose GET /healthz Check local readiness. GET /v1/sequencer Read the advertised native network ID and sequencer public key. POST /__emulator/accounts/prefund Establish local development funding through emulator account tooling. GET /v1/state , GET /v1/protocol/account-state/head Inspect emulator state and the current account-state head. GET /v1/dids/{did}/sequence Read an identity sequence. POST /__emulator/time/set , POST /__emulator/time/advance Set or advance local protocol time for deterministic scenarios. POST /__emulator/faults Inject a fault for failure-path testing. GET / PUT /__emulator/snapshot Export or import an emulator snapshot. /v1/settle Retired: returns HTTP 410. Native activity and receipt workflows Exercise signing, state transitions and independently verifiable outcomes. Programs lifecycle and calls Develop deployment, discovery, simulation and execution journeys.

title: Provision a sequencer identity
content: layerx --json emulator provision Provisioning generates a sequencer seed from operating-system randomness and publishes its public trust anchor. It creates emulator/sequencer.seed and emulator/sequencer.anchor under the CLI profile directory using owner-only storage and atomic identity publication. Retain the paths returned by the command. The seed is secret; the anchor is the public verification identity. Existing files cause sequencer_seed_exists or sequencer_trust_anchor_exists . Use layerx emulator provision --force only when deliberately replacing the local identity, then rebind clients to the new anchor.

title: Start the gateway
content: layerx emulator up --listen 127.0.0.1:9402 --network-id 402 --sequencer-seed-file <provisioned-seed-path> Run the gateway in a dedicated terminal. The listener must be loopback because emulator control routes provide local development authority. Network ID 402 is the local default, distinct from Paxeer X EVM chain ID 125. Network ID zero is reserved. Option Use --sequencer-seed-file Required provisioned signing seed. --listen Choose an IP socket address on loopback. --network-id Bind activities and client handshake to a local native network. --protocol-version Select the supported protocol version for a compatibility scenario. --time-ms Choose the local protocol time in milliseconds for deterministic scenarios. --prefund Repeat a DID, public key and amount tuple for initial local account funding.

title: Bind the CLI to that identity
content: layerx environment use emulator --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9402 --network-id 402 --sequencer-trust-anchor-file <provisioned-anchor-path> layerx --json environment current Supply endpoint, network ID and one trust-anchor input together. The CLI waits for the listener and reads /v1/sequencer , then checks the network and public identity before accepting the profile. A profile can also use --sequencer-trust-anchor <hex> in place of the file. Subsequent selection uses layerx environment use emulator .

title: Diagnose handshake failures
content: Code Resolution environment_input_missing Provide the complete endpoint, network and anchor set. sequencer_identity_unavailable Start the listener and confirm the endpoint and identity route. network_id_mismatch Match client configuration to the running emulator network. sequencer_trust_anchor_mismatch Use the public anchor corresponding to the running sequencer seed. sequencer_trust_anchor_unreadable , sequencer_trust_anchor_malformed Correct the anchor path or public-key encoding.

title: Create development accounts
content: layerx key create alice layerx key default alice layerx account create --key alice --initial-amount 1000000 layerx key create bob layerx account create --key bob --initial-amount 0 layerx account get --did <alice-did> Key creation stores secret material in the selected credential store. Account creation in the emulator uses its prefunding route. Read public DIDs and account identifiers from the returned metadata instead of inventing bindings. The wallet convenience flow layerx wallet create <name> also registers a local identity and main account.

title: Prefund at startup
content: layerx emulator up --sequencer-seed-file <seed-path> --prefund '<did>,<64-hex-public-key>,1000000' Prefunding binds the supplied DID and 32-byte public key to the local account setup. The amount accepts a decimal low component or an explicit high:low pair. Keep the signing key, public binding and DID consistent across setup and activity construction.

title: Exercise payments and receipts
content: layerx --json payment test --from <alice-account> --to <bob-account> --currency <asset-id> --amount 1000 --idempotency-key emulator-payment-0001 layerx --json receipt get <0x-prefixed-transaction-hash> Retain the quote, commit outcome, transaction hash and canonical receipt. receipt get fetches by 0x-prefixed transaction hash. Reuse the stable idempotency key for the same payment after an uncertain response. Independently verify receipt bytes with layerx receipt verify , supplying the batch ID, asset, previous and resulting state roots and trusted sequencer public key. A journey response alone does not replace receipt verification.

title: Develop deterministic Programs
content: layerx new local-program layerx program build --manifest-path local-program/Cargo.toml layerx program discover <program-id> layerx program interface get <program-id> Use deploy and upgrade to exercise lifecycle authorization, simulate to obtain non-commit evidence, and call to obtain receipt-bound execution. Preserve current sequences, state roots, fuel limits, validity windows and interface digests. Simulation establishes committed: false ; execution verifies the returned activity, ABI, sequencer identity and terminal payload before typed success.

title: Move the application to a hosted profile
content: Keep emulator prefunding and local sequencer keys in the development environment. Bind a hosted profile with its own HTTPS endpoint, native network ID and trusted sequencer identity, then establish hosted identity and gateway credentials. A2A installation uses a hosted beta or production profile. MCP installation instead follows its enrolled daemon binding. Continue with the CLI reference , platform API , A2A agents and Programs .

title: Engine
content: Paxeer's EVM execution engine, transaction processing, and state transition management. Paxeer's EVM execution engine, transaction processing, and state transition management. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/engine/

title: Overview
content: The engine package provides EVM transaction execution for Paxeer. It wraps go-ethereum's EVM with Paxeer-specific precompiles, state management, and fee handling. The engine sits between the consensus layer (which orders transactions) and the EVM module (which manages on-chain state).

title: Executor
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/engine/executor/ The executor is the core EVM execution wrapper. It provides two entry points:

title: Executor Types
content: The Executor struct in engine/executor/executor.go supports two backends: Geth Executor: Uses go-ethereum's native EVM interpreter Evmone Executor: Uses the evmone C++ VM via EVMC bindings for performance // From engine/executor/executor.go type Executor struct { evm *vm.EVM } func NewGethExecutor(blockCtx vm.BlockContext, stateDB vm.StateDB, chainConfig *params.ChainConfig, config vm.Config, customPrecompiles map[common.Address]vm.PrecompiledContract) *Executor func NewEvmoneExecutor(evmoneVM *evmc.VM, blockCtx vm.BlockContext, stateDB vm.StateDB, chainConfig *params.ChainConfig, config vm.Config, customPrecompiles map[common.Address]vm.PrecompiledContract) *Executor

title: Transaction Execution
content: The executor provides two execution modes:

title: Standard Execution
content: func (e *Executor) ExecuteTransaction(tx *types.Transaction, sender common.Address, baseFee *big.Int, gasPool *core.GasPool) (*core.ExecutionResult, error) Standard execution charges gas fees from the sender, executes the transaction, and refunds unused gas. This path is used for direct EVM transaction submission.

title: Fee-Already-Charged Execution
content: func (e *Executor) ExecuteTransactionFeeCharged(tx *types.Transaction, sender common.Address, baseFee *big.Int, gasPool *core.GasPool) (*core.ExecutionResult, error) This mode assumes fees were already charged before execution. It skips fee deduction and refund. This is the mode the node Giga execution path uses for MsgEVMTransaction transactions.

title: Internal Components
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/engine/executor/internal/ Internal execution utilities: Host context ( host_context.go ): EVMC host context for evmone integration Interpreter ( interpreter.go ): EVM opcode interpreter wrapper Message ( message.go ): internal execution message handling

title: Precompiles
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/precompiles/ ; engine/executor/precompiles/failfast.go Paxeer-specific precompiled contracts live in the top-level precompiles/ package and are registered with the executor at initialization. The executor passes the customPrecompiles map to the EVM, which routes calls to the registered precompile addresses. The engine/executor/precompiles/ directory itself contains only the fail-fast wrapper ( failfast.go ) and its tests. See Precompiles documentation for the full list of Paxeer precompiles (bank, staking, oracle, pointer, etc.).

title: Dependencies (xbank, xevm)
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/engine/deps/ The engine depends on Cosmos SDK modules via thin wrappers in engine/deps/ :

title: xbank
content: engine/deps/xbank/ wraps the SDK bank module for balance operations: Send: Transfer tokens between accounts View: Query balances and supply Deferred Cache: Batch balance updates before commit

title: xevm
content: engine/deps/xevm/ wraps the EVM module keeper: State: EVM storage access (accounts, code, storage slots) Code: Contract bytecode storage and retrieval Receipt: Transaction receipt generation Address: Cosmos ↔ EVM address association Nonce: Account nonce management Fee: Gas price and fee collection Coinbase: Block reward recipient Precompile: Precompile address registration

title: Configuration
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/engine/executor/config/ The Giga executor configuration carries two flags, both defaulting to true : giga_executor.enabled : whether the Giga executor is used giga_executor.occ_enabled : whether optimistic concurrency control (OCC) is used with the Giga executor # app.toml [giga_executor] enabled = true occ_enabled = true Chain configuration (chain ID 125, fork activation) and the custom precompile address map are supplied to the executor constructors by the caller. They are not fields of this executor config.

title: Testing
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/engine/tests/ The engine includes comprehensive test suites: State Tests: state_test.go runs Ethereum state transition tests Harness: tests/harness/ provides test fixtures and builders Giga Test: giga_test.go for large-scale execution

title: Chain ID
content: The chain configuration maps the Cosmos identifier hyperpax_125-1 to EVM chain ID 125 . Transactions on that network must use chain ID 125 for EIP-155 replay protection. Unknown Cosmos identifiers use the separate development fallback chain ID and must not be treated as Paxeer mainnet.

title: Utilities
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/engine/executor/utils/ The utils package ( errors.go ) defines the Giga abort sentinel ( giga_fallback_to_v2 ) and ShouldExecutionAbort , which reports whether an error should abort Giga execution and fall back to the standard (V2) execution path.

title: Integration with EVM Module
content: EVM transactions arrive as MsgEVMTransaction messages. On the Giga execution path, the node application ( node/app.go ) constructs a geth executor with NewGethExecutor and calls ExecuteTransactionFeeCharged , because fees have already been charged before execution. The flow is: Consensus orders transactions in a block Block processing routes MsgEVMTransaction to the EVM execution path Ante processing validates the transaction and charges fees The Giga path constructs the executor and calls ExecuteTransactionFeeCharged The executor runs EVM bytecode against the state DB The EVM module generates the receipt and emits events See EVM Module documentation for the full message handling flow.

title: Next Steps

title: Escrow and Conditional Payments
content: Reserve funds, capture milestone payments, refund unused balances, and resolve disputes through native Paxeer X escrow. Reserve funds, capture milestone payments, refund unused balances, and resolve disputes through native Paxeer X escrow.

title: Payment Guarantees for Agent Commerce
content: Escrow separates a payment commitment from its final distribution. A buyer or agent funds a dedicated escrow account, a named beneficiary captures funds under the agreement, and a named arbiter resolves disputes. Marketplaces, service purchases, procurement, and milestone contracts use the same protocol lifecycle. The escrow module stores the agreement terms and lifecycle. Every movement of value uses the shared 402LXP transfer mechanism, including funding, beneficiary payments, refunds, and dispute splits. The account namespace is agent:<did>:escrow:<id> .

title: Define an Escrow
content: Field Purpose Escrow ID and account Identify the hold and its isolated funds. Owner Funds the hold and receives unused funds. Beneficiary Receives captured payments. Arbiter Authorizes the distribution of disputed funds. Asset and amount Specify the asset and positive funding amount in integer base units. Expiry Absolute batch timestamp deadline in milliseconds; zero means no expiry. Dispute window Absolute final timestamp for opening a dispute; zero disables dispute opening. Terms hash and agreement reference Bind the hold to the agreed conditions and reference record. The terms hash commits to the agreement. Applications verify delivery, evidence, or milestones against that agreement before requesting an authorized capture; hashing terms does not itself evaluate a real-world condition.

title: Lifecycle and Actions
content: Action Result State Open Move the owner's funds into escrow. OPEN Partial capture Pay a positive amount strictly below the remaining balance. PARTIALLY_CAPTURED Capture Pay the entire remaining balance to the beneficiary. CAPTURED Release Return the remaining balance to the owner. RELEASED Timeout Return an expired active hold's remaining balance to the owner. TIMED_OUT Open dispute Freeze ordinary capture and refund paths. DISPUTED Resolve dispute Distribute the remaining funds according to the arbiter's split. RESOLVED Capture pays the beneficiary. Release refunds the owner. Keep these meanings visible in application buttons and transaction previews.

title: Authority and Deadlines
content: The beneficiary or an owner principal acting through a delegated capability authorizes capture. The owner authorizes release. Either owner or beneficiary can open a dispute while the hold is active and the dispute deadline has not passed. Only the designated arbiter resolves the dispute. Captures fail at or after a nonzero expiry, even before a timeout sweep changes the recorded state. Batch maintenance processes due escrow deadlines using the batch timestamp, with a sweep capacity of 24 ( LX_ESCROW_SWEEP_CAPACITY ). Disputed holds do not follow the ordinary timeout refund path; they require resolution. The dispute deadline is inclusive: a dispute opens when the batch timestamp equals dispute_window , and the window is closed only when the timestamp is greater than it. A zero dispute window disables dispute opening.

title: Milestone Payment Workflow
content: Agree on the asset, owner, beneficiary, arbiter, deadlines, and delivery conditions. Open and fund the escrow for 1,000 base units. After the first milestone, partially capture 300 units. The beneficiary receives 300 and 700 remain locked. On completion, capture the remaining 700. Alternatively, release the unused 700 to the owner. If a dispute is opened before the deadline, submit evidence to the arbiter and resolve the remaining balance.

title: Dispute Split Example
content: A resolution specifies the beneficiary share in basis points from 0 to 10,000. With 700 units remaining and a 6,000 basis-point award, the beneficiary receives 420 and the owner receives 280. Earlier captures remain paid. The beneficiary amount rounds down to an integer base unit; the owner receives the remainder, preserving the complete escrow balance. beneficiary = floor(remaining_balance × beneficiary_basis_points / 10000) owner = remaining_balance - beneficiary

title: Protocol Reference
content: Escrow is module 2 . Activity payloads use fixed-width IDs and integer amounts; they are protocol activities rather than EVM contract method names. Activity Type Payload bytes LX_ESCROW_OPEN 0x00020001 288 LX_ESCROW_CAPTURE 0x00020002 80 LX_ESCROW_PARTIAL_CAPTURE 0x00020003 80 LX_ESCROW_RELEASE 0x00020004 64 LX_ESCROW_TIMEOUT 0x00020005 64 LX_ESCROW_DISPUTE_OPEN 0x00020006 32 LX_ESCROW_DISPUTE_RESOLVE 0x00020007 68

title: Retries and Failure Handling
content: Capture, release, timeout, and resolution carry a nonzero idempotency key. Preserve that key when retrying the same operation. Keys bind to the escrow and operation context; reusing one for a different payment is rejected. Track the returned receipt and final state before advancing a business workflow. Handle expired holds, disputed holds, unauthorized capture, and capture amounts above the remaining balance as distinct failures. A partial capture cannot equal the entire balance: use full capture instead. Out-of-range dispute splits are rejected.

title: EVM Module
content: Native EVM execution, address association, receipts, pointers, and precompile integration on chain ID 125. Native EVM execution, address association, receipts, pointers, and precompile integration on chain ID 125. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/

title: Overview
content: The EVM module ( modules/evm/ ) provides full Ethereum Virtual Machine execution on Paxeer. It runs as a Cosmos SDK module and integrates with the execution engine to process EVM transactions with chain ID 125 . The module handles: EVM Transaction Processing: Execute Ethereum-format transactions Address Association: Map Cosmos bech32 addresses to EVM hex addresses Receipt Generation: Create transaction receipts with logs and status Pointers: Link ERC-20 tokens to native Cosmos denoms Precompiles: Expose Cosmos modules via EVM precompiled contracts

title: Message Types
content: The EVM module handles MsgEVMTransaction , which wraps a standard Ethereum transaction: Legacy transactions (type 0) EIP-2930 access list transactions (type 1) EIP-1559 dynamic fee transactions (type 2) EIP-4844 blob transactions (type 3), accepted from Cancun EIP-7702 set-code transactions (type 4), accepted from Prague Cancun and Prague both activate at time 0 in the chain configuration, so all five types are accepted. MsgEVMTransaction also has an associate-transaction variant ( AssociateTx , reported by IsAssociateTx ) used for address association. Transactions are submitted via the JSON-RPC eth_sendRawTransaction endpoint or the Cosmos SDK MsgEVMTransaction message. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/ante/preprocess.go , modules/evm/types/codec.go , modules/evm/types/message_evm_transaction.go , modules/evm/types/config.go

title: Address Association
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/address.go Paxeer addresses exist in two formats: Cosmos: pax1... (bech32) EVM: 0x... (hex, 20 bytes) The EVM module maintains a bidirectional mapping between these formats. When a Cosmos account sends an EVM transaction, the module associates its pax1... address with the derived 0x... address. This allows: Cosmos accounts to interact with EVM contracts EVM accounts to interact with native Cosmos denominations Unified balance queries across both address formats

title: State Management
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/state.go The EVM module stores: Accounts: Nonce, balance (via bank module) Code: Contract bytecode ( keeper/code.go ) Storage: Contract storage slots ( keeper/state.go ) Receipts: Transaction receipts and logs ( keeper/receipt.go ) EVM state is stored in the module's KVStore. Account balances are managed by the bank module to maintain consistency with native token operations.

title: Transaction Execution Flow
content: When an EVM transaction is submitted: RPC receives eth_sendRawTransaction or SDK receives MsgEVMTransaction Ante decorators under modules/evm/ante/ validate signatures, nonces, and transaction fees Msg server routes to EVM module Execution runs through the engine executor ; on the node Giga path this is ExecuteTransactionFeeCharged , with fees already charged Executor runs EVM bytecode against state DB Module generates receipt ( keeper/receipt.go ) with logs, gas used, status Module emits events for indexing

title: Receipts
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/receipt.go Transaction receipts include: Status: 1 (success) or 0 (revert) Gas Used: Total gas consumed Logs: Event logs emitted during execution Contract Address: For contract creation transactions Bloom Filter: For efficient log filtering Execution stages receipts in a transient store and flushes them to the configured receipt store. GetReceipt delegates to that store; JSON-RPC exposes them through eth_getTransactionReceipt .

title: Pointers
content: Pointers are a Paxeer-specific feature that links ERC-20 token contracts to native Cosmos denoms. A pointer allows: ERC-20 transfer to move native tokens via bank module Native token transfers to appear as ERC-20 events Unified balance view across EVM and Cosmos APIs Pointer contracts are deployed via the pointer precompile .

title: Precompile Integration
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/precompile.go , Paxeer-X-Network/precompiles/ The EVM module registers custom precompiled contracts that expose Cosmos SDK modules to EVM callers. Paxeer-specific addresses are registered by the precompile package, including bank at 0x1001 and address conversion at 0x1004 . Standard Ethereum precompiles occupy a separate address range. See Precompiles documentation for the full list of Paxeer precompiles (bank, staking, oracle, IBC, etc.).

title: Fee Collection
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/fee.go , Paxeer-X-Network/precompiles/feetoken/feetoken.go EVM transaction fees are: Charged in PAX (native gas token) by default. An account can select an allowed alternative fee denom, such as SID, through the fee-token precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001018 . See Sidiora Reported using receipt gas usage and the effective gas price; estimation and charge settlement depend on the configured execution path Sent to the fee collector module Distributed to validators and stakers EIP-1559 dynamic fees are supported with baseFee and priority fees.

title: Coinbase
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/coinbase.go , keeper.go The EVM block context sets COINBASE to the fee collector module’s associated EVM address through GetFeeCollectorAddress .

title: Chain ID
content: Paxeer uses EVM chain ID 125 . This must match the chainId field in EIP-155 transaction signatures for replay protection. The Cosmos chain identifier is hyperpax_125-1 .

title: Configuration
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/types/params.go , types/config.go , keeper/params.go EVM module parameters include: Native units: PAX is the display currency; the implementation retains uhpx as its Cosmos base denomination and converts it to 18-decimal EVM units Fee bounds: Minimum and maximum fees per gas, target block gas, and dynamic adjustment parameters Storage gas: The default SSTORE set cost is 20,000 gas. Query the network’s EVM parameters when calculating costs for a deployment Chain Config: Fork activation times, including Cancun and Prague, and a configurable SSTORE cost

title: Genesis
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/genesis.go Genesis state for the EVM module includes: Module parameters Pre-deployed contract code and storage Address associations

title: Logging
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/log.go EVM event logs are emitted during transaction execution via the LOG0 , LOG1 , LOG2 , LOG3 , LOG4 opcodes. Logs are included in receipts and indexed for querying via eth_getLogs .

title: Deferred Operations
content: Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/evm/keeper/deferred.go Some EVM operations (like balance updates from precompiles) are deferred and batched for commit. This avoids redundant state writes during execution and improves performance.
