content: Use the JSON-RPC API Explore Paxeer precompiles Deploy contracts Previous Engine Next Storage

title: Fees and payment costs
content: Understand Paxeer X EVM gas, kernel execution fees, program occupancy, merchant pricing, spending ceilings and fee estimation. Understand Paxeer X EVM gas, kernel execution fees, program occupancy, merchant pricing, spending ceilings and fee estimation.

title: Identify the charge you are approving
content: Cost What it pays for Where to inspect it EVM gas EVM transaction execution, measured in gas and priced in the native gas token Transaction fee fields, current EVM parameters, gas estimate, execution receipt Native protocol fee Canonical activity admission and execution under the committed kernel fee schedule Fee estimate, signed fee_limit , canonical receipt Programs CALL fee Program execution under its versioned execution budget and fee schedule Program-specific estimate, authorized budget, CALL outcome Programs occupancy Namespace bytes that persist across protocol batches Occupancy receipt and batch settlement evidence Service or merchant price The resource, cart, subscription, or metered usage being purchased Accepted quote, x402 requirement, order digest, payment receipt Provider or conversion cost Charges attached to the selected external payment mechanism or rail The provider's terms and the accepted route quote A purchase amount and its network execution cost are separate terms. A merchant cart total is the sum of catalog prices and quantities; it does not define the protocol schedule. There is no universal merchant processing or ramp percentage to apply across every route. Review the specific quote and provider terms for the mechanism you select.

title: EVM gas
content: EVM transactions use Ethereum-style gas accounting. Dynamic-fee transactions carry maximum fee and priority fee fields; execution receipts report gas used and effective gas price. Query the current network settings when preparing a transaction rather than assuming fixed base-fee bounds. Use the EVM RPC and wallet fee controls for an EVM transfer or contract call. Native LayerX activity fee estimates apply to canonical activities rather than arbitrary EVM transactions. A workflow spanning both execution planes should expose the costs and evidence of its individual legs.

title: The native committed schedule
content: Native activity fees are deterministic functions of committed schedule bytes and execution meters. Parameters include base_fee , per_activity_type_unit , per_encoded_byte , per_execution_unit , per_storage_unit , multiplier_basis_points , Asset prices, and module prices. Schedule version Pricing capabilities Canonical encoding 1 Base and resource coefficients 86 bytes 2 Coefficients plus ten named Asset prices 87 + 16 × 10 bytes 3 Eleven Asset prices, adding the withdrawal slot Version 2 plus 8 bytes 4 Version 3 pricing plus seven named module prices Version 3 head plus a module-count byte and 16 × 7 price bytes Schedule versions select an encoding and pricing contract; they are distinct from an individual estimate's observed state. The withdrawal price slot is encoded as an unsigned 64-bit value even though other price slots use unsigned 128-bit values. An available schedule slot does not by itself determine which activity encodings a particular submission interface accepts.

title: How the fee is calculated
content: For a Programs CALL carrying an exact program fee, use the declared exact fee units under the applicable program fee schedule. Otherwise begin with base_fee . For an Asset activity under schedule version 2 or later, add its named flat Asset price. For other activity types, add per_activity_type_unit × activity_type . Under version 4, add the named module price for escrow, budget, stream, service, perpetuals, governance, or bridge activities. Add the encoded-byte, execution-unit, and storage-unit coefficients multiplied by their corresponding meters. Multiply the total by multiplier_basis_points , divide by 10,000, and round upward. ordinary_fee = ceil( (base_fee + activity_component + applicable_module_price + per_encoded_byte * canonical_encoded_bytes + per_execution_unit * execution_units + per_storage_unit * storage_units) * multiplier_basis_points / 10000 ) The exact Programs fee path is valid for Programs module 9, CALL ordinal 3, with a nonzero program fee schedule version. Unknown Asset ordinals fail as LXP_ERR_UNKNOWN_ACTIVITY ; unsupported schedule versions fail as LXP_ERR_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED . Integer arithmetic and canonical encodings keep independent execution and replay calculations consistent.

title: Asset and module prices
content: Asset operation Parameter Ordinal Register fee.asset.register 1 Pause / unpause fee.asset.pause / fee.asset.unpause 2 / 3 Open account fee.asset.account_open 4 Send / receive fee.asset.send / fee.asset.receive 5 / 6 Issue / revoke grant fee.asset.grant_issue / fee.asset.grant_revoke 7 / 8 Mint / burn fee.asset.mint / fee.asset.burn 10 / 11 Withdrawal price slot fee.asset.withdraw 9; schedule version 3 or later Version 4 module parameters are fee.module.escrow , fee.module.budget , fee.module.stream , fee.module.service , fee.module.perps , fee.module.governance , and fee.module.bridge . Programs uses its own exact CALL pricing path rather than a slot in this seven-module table.

title: Estimate before signing
content: There is no public lx_estimateFee JSON-RPC method in this checkout. The hosted gateway refuses every lx_* method name with JSON-RPC -32601 ( Method not found ). Do not present an lx_estimateFee request, or response fields such as observed_head_sequence , state_root , or verification: "authenticated_committed_snapshot" , as a public estimation contract. The hosted core fee estimate that does exist prices an EVM transaction: it computes gas_limit × max_fee_per_gas and returns only fee (decimal string), parameter_version: 0 , an empty canonical_schedule , and canonical_bytes . For native activities, price the exact canonical bytes against the committed schedule described above and set the signed fee_limit from that calculation. An estimate reserves no balance, locks no schedule, and proves no execution. When the schedule needs execution or storage meters that estimation cannot establish, the estimator refuses instead of treating the missing meters as zero. LNI fee_estimate and session_fee_state expose the committed schedule projection with the same non-reservation semantics.

title: Set and fund the fee ceiling
content: Prepare the exact canonical activity and estimate its fee. Choose a maximum in integer base units and disclose that fee_limit with the other payment terms. Ensure the actor's spendable fee balance covers the full limit, even when the estimate is lower. Sign and submit the approved bytes, preserving their activity identifier and idempotency key. Verify the final receipt, charged fee, result code, and requested commitment. Outcome Sequence and fee behavior Module effects Admission refused No global sequence, no consumed account sequence, no fee None Insufficient spendable balance for the limit LXP_ERR_FEE_UNPAYABLE ; refused before sequence assignment None Admitted execution succeeds Sequence consumed and computed fee charged within the limit Committed Admitted execution fails Sequence consumed; fee charged within the limit; failure receipt emitted Rolled back Computed fee exceeds the signed limit LXP_ERR_FEE_LIMIT ; charge capped at the limit Rolled back Protocol fee charges settle as 402LXP transfer legs with reason LXP_REASON_PROTOCOL_FEE to treasury account system:fees . Replay verifies the recorded charge, actor debit, treasury credit, schedule version, and resulting state. A failed payment can therefore have a fee-bearing receipt even when its requested transfer did not apply.

title: Programs occupancy and persistent storage
content: Occupancy charges for namespace bytes held across protocol batches. Its time unit is the batch number, not elapsed wall-clock time. The CALL flow prices its execution budget and carves authorized occupancy out of the signed fee limit. Due maintenance transfers settle as ordinary 402LXP legs. Occupancy is a separate batch settlement. A CALL that writes persistent storage is not fully settled until occupancy settlement for its containing batch completes. Program outcomes carry occupancy byte-batches, fee units, Asset identifier, evidence digest, and transfer root. Preserve the outcome and batch evidence when reconciling persistent storage costs; simulation alone does not perform batch occupancy settlement.

title: Merchant, metered, and subscription pricing
content: A merchant quote binds cart lines, integer totals, Asset, recipient, scheme, network, and timeout into a request digest. One cart uses one payment Asset and recipient. Catalog changes create new quote digests. In x402, accept the offered requirement without editing its amount or recipient, and distinguish that resource price from the network fee needed to settle it. Metered and subscription grants authorize bounded future draws with explicit purpose, expiry, and billing windows. Each draw or renewal remains a separately authorized receive and settlement. Price a complete workflow by its actual activities and storage obligations, rather than assuming that an initial grant covers every future network charge.

title: Governance and parameter changes
content: Governance controls fee.base , fee.activity , fee.byte , fee.exec , fee.storage , fee.multiplier_bps , and fee.encoding , together with the named Asset and module prices. Committed schedule bytes are stored under fee.schedule ; version 4 also uses fee.module-prices . Read the active committed schedule when estimating instead of copying fixed prices into application code.

title: Related guides
content: Payments and settlement First payment walkthrough EVM execution and gas Programs and occupancy Public payment API Governance

title: Finality & Commitment
content: Follow an activity from execution into a sealed batch, and request the evidence your application needs. Follow an activity from execution into a sealed batch, and request the evidence your application needs.

title: One history, increasing assurance
content: Paxeer X combines the fast LayerX activity path with Paxeer custody. Activities are ordered into sealed batches and replicas preserve the history for replay. The layerx-merge upgrade ( v7.0 ) retired the separate guarantor and checkpoint settlement plane: checkpoint submission to the Paxeer anchor returns a module-retired error, so applications must not require anchor registration as a live step. See Checkpoints . Stage Name Evidence and responsibility L0 Accepted The activity is ordered into the current batch and issued a state-root-bound receipt. L1 Sealed Batch ordering is fixed by the signed canonical header. Replicas retain sealed bytes. L2 Distributed The sealed batch and availability bundle are retrievable for independent replay. Earlier designs added bonded guarantor attestation and Paxeer checkpoint registration as further stages. That plane is retired. A receipt proves execution at its declared evidence level; it does not by itself prove settlement. Before using evidence to release value, apply the configured settlement and withdrawal rules for the relevant network.

title: Public commitment levels
content: Activity submission and payment middleware expose three exact commitment names. These are evidence requirements rather than interchangeable progress labels. They do not replace the lifecycle stages. Commitment Required evidence Application decision executed A verified canonical receipt for the submitted activity Inspect the authenticated outcome and its payment or program effects. batched Executed evidence plus an authenticated receipt proof naming the same activity and carrying byte-identical canonical receipt bytes Require signed-batch inclusion before releasing a resource. finalised Batched evidence plus finalised checkpoint evidence whose canonical header exactly equals the proof's signed batch header Require the checkpoint evidence bound to that exact batch. batch_evidence carries the authenticated receipt proof and checkpoint_evidence carries the checkpoint. A different checkpoint or a newer head cannot substitute for the exact required header. Admission acknowledgements, queue entries, activity IDs and HTTP 202 responses do not establish execution.

title: Use the exact wire vocabulary
content: The spelling is finalised , alongside executed and batched . Do not substitute other spellings or progress labels.

title: Recover a pending commitment
content: When a bounded wait cannot establish the requested evidence, the gateway returns an error rather than silently returning a weaker success. Recover the existing outcome instead of submitting a duplicate: Keep the original signed activity and activity ID. Read lx_getActivityStatus and lx_getReceipt to recover the existing outcome. Retrieve the required authenticated receipt and batch evidence. Verify exact activity, canonical receipt and signed-header bindings before satisfying your release policy. Creating another activity to escape an unknown result can duplicate the economic action.

title: Payment release policies
content: An x402 offer's LayerX terms under extra.layerx carry the payer account reference and currency code; the offer model has no LayerX commitment field. Choose the evidence your release policy requires at the application layer and verify it before releasing the resource. A successful settlement reference is lxp:<receipt_digest> . Validate the receipt, payment facts, configured authority and commitment evidence together. The reference or an HTTP success is insufficient on its own.

title: Replay covers the whole economic system
content: Replay covers payments, program calls, program-owned transfers and storage occupancy settlement from the same ordered history. Program monetary effects are explicit transfer sets applied through the kernel's single module-to-ledger entry, while occupancy charges remain replay-checkable batch evidence. Deterministic execution excludes local clocks, floating point and unstable iteration from consensus decisions.

title: Checkpoint finalisation checks (retired submission)
content: Checkpoint submission is retired and unconditionally returns a module-retired error. For historical checkpoints, the anchor keeper's finalisable check covers checkpoint status, the declared threshold, the bonded guarantor count, open challenges, the challenge window, and that the batch is exactly the latest finalised batch plus one. Do not build new flows on checkpoint registration.

title: Liveness and exits
content: If the ordinary activity path stalls, the last accepted history remains the replay anchor. Custody release on Paxeer remains governed by its applicable evidence, timing, limit, and eligibility rules; see Custody . Continue with Receipts & Proofs , Data Availability and Consensus .

title: Build with Foundry
content: Create, test, and deploy a Solidity counter with Forge, then read its state through the Paxeer EVM using Cast. Create, test, and deploy a Solidity counter with Forge, then read its state through the Paxeer EVM using Cast. Use this guide for a new Solidity project. Forge compiles and tests contracts; Cast reads chain data and sends signed transactions. The examples target Paxeer chain ID 125 (Cosmos chain hyperpax_125-1 ), whose native gas token is PAX. Other networks map differently — for example pacific-1 is 1329 and an unmapped local chain defaults to 713714 — so substitute your endpoint's actual chain ID where 125 appears below.

title: Set up the project
content: Install Forge and Cast using the Foundry installation instructions , then create a project. Keep the generated project files; add the named files below alongside the scaffold. forge init paxeer-counter cd paxeer-counter forge --version cast --version Use this foundry.toml for the example. It matches the in-tree toolchain: solc 0.8.27 with the Prague EVM target, which the chain enables from genesis along with Cancun. The repository's own foundry.paxeer.toml pins solc 0.8.27 without an explicit EVM version or optimizer run count; the run count below is an example choice, so record whatever you deploy with. [profile.default] src = "src" out = "out" libs = ["lib"] solc_version = "0.8.27" evm_version = "prague" optimizer = true optimizer_runs = 200 [rpc_endpoints] paxeer = "${PAXEER_RPC_URL}"

title: Write the contract
content: Create src/PaxeerCounter.sol . Anyone can update this demonstration counter; it is useful for checking storage, events, and frontend reads. // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT pragma solidity 0.8.27; contract PaxeerCounter { uint256 public number; event NumberChanged(address indexed caller, uint256 number); function setNumber(uint256 next) external { number = next; emit NumberChanged(msg.sender, next); } function increment() external { number += 1; emit NumberChanged(msg.sender, number); } }

title: Test local behavior
content: Create test/PaxeerCounter.t.sol . These tests run the contract locally in Forge, using an isolated test environment. // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT pragma solidity 0.8.27; import {Test} from "forge-std/Test.sol"; import {PaxeerCounter} from "../src/PaxeerCounter.sol"; contract PaxeerCounterTest is Test { PaxeerCounter private counter; function setUp() public { counter = new PaxeerCounter(); } function test_Increment() public { counter.increment(); assertEq(counter.number(), 1); } function testFuzz_SetNumber(uint256 next) public { counter.setNumber(next); assertEq(counter.number(), next); } } forge build forge test --match-contract PaxeerCounterTest -vv forge test --match-contract PaxeerCounterTest --gas-report The expected result is two passing tests, including the generated fuzz cases. Use the gas report to compare the cost of individual contract calls. Measure network throughput separately with a Paxeer development cluster.

title: Connect and rehearse deployment
content: Set PAXEER_RPC_URL to your EVM HTTP endpoint. This is different from a Cosmos RPC endpoint. Confirm its chain ID before selecting a signer. Import a development account into Foundry’s encrypted keystore when prompted. : "${PAXEER_RPC_URL:?Set your Paxeer EVM RPC URL}" test "$(cast chain-id --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL")" = 125 || { echo "Expected Paxeer chain ID 125" >&2; exit 1; } cast wallet import paxeer-dev --interactive forge create src/PaxeerCounter.sol:PaxeerCounter --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" --account paxeer-dev Run forge create first without --broadcast to rehearse, then review the destination chain, sender, and estimated cost before broadcasting. The signer needs PAX for an actual Paxeer deployment. For a local development network, use its actual chain ID and local funds.

title: Publish and read the result
content: The next command broadcasts a contract-creation transaction. Save its address and transaction hash from the output. forge create src/PaxeerCounter.sol:PaxeerCounter --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" --account paxeer-dev --broadcast # Set CONTRACT_ADDRESS and TX_HASH from the deployment output. cast receipt "$TX_HASH" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" cast code "$CONTRACT_ADDRESS" --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" cast call "$CONTRACT_ADDRESS" 'number()(uint256)' --rpc-url "$PAXEER_RPC_URL" Confirm a successful receipt, nonempty deployed bytecode, and an initial counter value of zero. The contract ABI is in out/PaxeerCounter.sol/PaxeerCounter.json . Use that artifact in your frontend ; keep the compiler version and optimizer settings with your deployment record. Reference: Foundry deployment and verification . For explorer verification, select a verifier that supports your Paxeer endpoint and submit the same compiler settings used for deployment. Paxeer source: Paxeer-X-Network/ — contracts/hardhat.config.js (Solidity 0.8.27, Prague), foundry.paxeer.toml (solc 0.8.27), modules/evm/config/config.go (ChainIDMapping), and rpc/send.go (SendRawTransaction). Previous Contracts Next Build with Hardhat

title: Funding and money movement
content: Move balances, fund agents, and connect external payment rails on the merged network. Former custody-boundary deposit, withdraw, and exit journeys are retired. Move balances, fund agents, and connect external payment rails on the merged network. Former custody-boundary deposit, withdraw, and exit journeys are retired.

title: Understand the boundary
content: Current money movement on the merged network is the internal move journey: fund, allocate, return, or transfer between LayerX accounts, including the EVM intent path. The former custody-boundary journeys — deposit, withdraw, exit, and wallet-binding — are retired kinds. They are retained only for decoding stored history and cannot start new journeys. Retained history of those kinds reads as closed , cannot resume signing or execution, and does not assert a successful movement. Journey Status Authorization and evidence Move Current Quote, commit, execution receipt Deposit Retired — history only Formerly wallet transaction and custody proof Withdraw Retired — history only Formerly withdrawal authorization and claim signature Exit Retired — history only Formerly eligibility, explicit confirmation, wallet claim The settlement_domain field is likewise retired; internal moves do not select a settlement domain. Money-moving mutations require an Idempotency-Key . Retain the key when retrying the same intended operation, and reconcile its journey before starting another movement.

title: Retired custody-boundary journeys
content: POST /v1/deposits (and its /confirm step), POST /v1/withdrawals (and its /claim step), POST /v1/exit , and GET /v1/exit/eligibility remain in the Human API schema as retired operations. Do not build new deposit, withdrawal, or exit flows on them. The on-chain custody path they relied on is also retired: the custody keeper refuses deposits and the custody precompile reverts. New integrations fund and move balances with the move flow below, on accounts that already hold spendable balances on the merged network.

title: Move money and fund an agent
content: Quote the source, destination, and amount first. The resolver selects fund , allocate , return , or transfer from the account relationship. Users choose what they intend to move; they do not choose a lower-level mechanism to bypass those relationships. POST /v1/moves/quote { "source": "acct_01j2gxq0aab1c2d3e4f5g6h7j8", "destination": "acct_01j2gxq0aak9m0n1p2q3r4s5t6", "money": { "amount": "500000", "currency": "LXP" } } POST /v1/moves Idempotency-Key: <unique-key-for-this-move> { "quote_id": "<quote_id-from-response>" } These request fields follow the Human API golden wire example. Amount is an integer string in the asset's precision, not a floating-point number. Obtain the quote ID from the response; the placeholder is not a real quote. Quote field What to review money and mechanism The exact amount, currency, and resolved movement fee_estimate and fee_ceiling Expected charge and maximum disclosed charge arrival_estimate and expires_at Expected timing and quote validity irreversibility_copy_key Any irreversible-action disclosure Commit returns a journey. A refused movement reports the refusing authority, explanatory copy, remaining money, and optional change path. Agent funding uses this same quote-and-commit surface. Reclaim uses POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/reclaim with money and returns a move with return semantics.

title: Spending and fee budgets
content: Agent monthly limits govern spending. Native fee budgets independently constrain per-activity fees, aggregate fees, and period fees. Read GET /v1/sessions/fee-policy for the native fee asset, currency, and decimals. Present the principal movement and the execution fee separately so an agent's funding amount is not confused with its ability to pay fees.

title: Verification levels
content: Human verification advances through three current rungs as evidence arrives: submitted ( unverified ), receipted ( receipt-verified ), and committed ( checkpoint-finalised ). checkpoint-finalised is the retained label for committed and is the current top rung. paxeer-finalised and settlement-anchored are retired decoding values; they do not define additional current rungs, so do not wait for them or present them as a stronger finality state.

title: Card, bank, and real-time payment rails
content: The fiat interop adapter connects provider callbacks for card, bank, and real-time payments. Provider evidence distinguishes authorised, clearing, settled, reversed, and chargeback events. Credit and corrective movements require accepted provider evidence and a receipt-gated LayerX result. Rail Provider callback route Card POST /v1/http/fiat/card/callbacks Bank POST /v1/http/fiat/bank/callbacks Real-time payment POST /v1/http/fiat/rtp/callbacks These are provider integration endpoints, not consumer deposit or card-entry endpoints. Callbacks carry token references only; PAN-shaped input is refused. A provider's authorisation is distinct from settlement, and reversal or chargeback is represented as its own verified event.

title: Independent market-maker ramps
content: Market-maker ramps let ordinary LayerX principals offer external conversion through quote terms and receipt-gated orders. Their toolkit compiles payer grant draws and operator sends, verifies order receipts, and journals orders. External custody is explicitly labelled so users can distinguish a ramp operator's custody from the Human account custody boundary. This ramp role is separate from the fiat callback adapter.

title: Reconcile the result
content: Read balances through GET /v1/account/balance , journey status through GET /v1/journeys/{journey_id} , and proof material through GET /v1/evidence/{evidence_id} . Journey states preserve still-checking, refused, and waiting-for-you alongside completion. The API response envelope is { ok, result?, error?, trace } ; retain trace and evidence references for support. See the Human interface for passkeys, wallet binding, approvals, and agent controls, and interop for external system boundaries.

title: Governance
content: Ordered authority changes, versioned parameters, staged rollouts, and controlled settlement upgrades across Paxeer X. Ordered authority changes, versioned parameters, staged rollouts, and controlled settlement upgrades across Paxeer X. Paxeer X governance operates across two boundaries: the Layer X activity log governs protocol execution, while Paxeer settlement contracts enforce their own authorized roles and delayed calls. A governance decision is evidence with an actor, scope, ordering position, and activation condition.

title: Governance in the activity log
content: Module 7 processes governance activities through the same envelope, authority, ordering, fee, and receipt rules as other activities. Identity creation, key rotation, recovery changes, session grants, revocation, and delegated capability issuance therefore remain part of replayable history. Only the following Module-7 ordinals were verified in monorepo source ( modules/lxphost tests). Meanings for other ordinals ( 0x00070002 , 0x00070003 , 0x00070006 , 0x00070009 ) were not verified and are not listed. Activity Purpose (as used in source) 0x00070001 Register / create-or-onboard identity ( registerType ). 0x00070005 Session-authority activity (used with fee-record loading in host tests). 0x00070008 Grant ( grantType ). Governance activity types are specific operations. Parameter proposals and emergency-state operations use the governance interfaces; applications must not manufacture an activity ordinal for a library operation. See Identity and authority for account delegation.

title: Parameter proposals and activation
content: On the Cosmos side, modules/layerxgov handles proposals and pause scopes (including ErrPausedScope ), separate from activity-log governance. Parameter-proposal field sets, any minimum activation delay, and staged-rollout scopes (All/Module/Market/Account set) were not verified in source and are not specified here. Before submitting a proposal, read the current value, bounds, and version from the deployed module, retain the proposal identifier and receipt, and verify the enacted value after activation.

title: Emergency controls
content: Governance records emergency halt and resume events with an ordered sequence. A pause identifies a module, market, or network scope, a trigger commitment, exit conditions, and entry epoch. Module enablement is also an ordered governance action. These interfaces require governance authorization and do not create an operator shortcut outside the log. When responding to an incident, retain the triggering evidence, select the narrowest applicable scope, order the halt, and inspect the resulting emergency state. Resume against the recorded exit conditions through a subsequent ordered action. Applications continue to distinguish execution availability from the availability of existing receipts and proofs.

title: Settlement roles and timelocks
content: Role Authority Proposer Schedules an allowed target and function selector with a sufficient delay. Executor Executes the exact scheduled operation after readiness and before grace-period expiry. Guardian Cancels a pending, incomplete operation. Timelock itself Changes roles, minimum delay, and call permissions through authorized self-calls. The operation identifier commits to the chain, timelock address, target, value, calldata hash, salt, and nonce. Scheduling and execution both enforce call permissions and value limits. Completion prevents operation replay; target failure reverts execution. Read the deployed contract's minDelay , delayFloor , and gracePeriod rather than assuming one universal waiting period.

title: Upgrades respect component boundaries
content: Layer X settlement components expose their role, static configuration hash, release version, and storage-layout version. The component base disables UUPS upgrades. The Sidiora proxy governance timelock provides a separate constrained upgrade path for its proxy targets. A proxy upgrade therefore follows that target's governance contract, while protocol parameter changes follow their own versioned activity rules. Before execution, compare the scheduled target, implementation, calldata, configuration commitments, and activation dependencies. After execution, retain the operation event and verify the target's resulting version and state.

title: Continue
content: Read Guarantors for membership and bonds, Security and trust boundaries for verification responsibilities, and Finality for checkpoint settlement.

title: Guarantors
content: Independent batch replay, bonded attestations, checkpoint certificates, and settlement accountability. Independent batch replay, bonded attestations, checkpoint certificates, and settlement accountability. Guarantors connect Layer X execution to Paxeer settlement. Each guarantor retrieves sealed batch data, independently executes it, compares the committed results, and signs an attestation only after verification. The certificate aggregates the required eligible attestations into evidence that the settlement registry can check.

title: Replay before signing
content: Pin the network, sequencer identity and key, and authorized batch range. Retrieve the signed candidate header and its availability chunks. Verify request correlation, chunk indices, hashes, Merkle proofs, the terminating response, and the reconstructed availability root. Load the verified genesis and registration state, validate actor signatures and authority, and replay the kernel and Programs runtime. Compare receipts, state diffs, recovery metadata, and committed roots before retaining or signing evidence. The producer verifies receipt signatures with the sequencer public key; it does not need the sequencer private key. Deterministic program calls, program-owned transfers, and storage-occupancy charges participate in the same replay. Replay failure stops attestation production.

title: Data availability is part of verification
content: Candidate retrieval is bounded, and reconstruction must reproduce the signed header's availability root before signing. A missing terminator, unavailable data, or a root mismatch is a refusal to sign. Specific chunk-count, chunk-size, and availability-class limits were not verified against a live producer in the monorepo (the former C/Python guarantor paths are retired) and are not specified here.

title: Attestations and certificates
content: Guarantors exchange canonical attestations through authenticated peer connections. An incoming attestation must pass signature and recovery verification, bonded-membership checks, and checkpoint-identifier recomputation from a locally verified header. The certificate assembler sorts guarantor identifiers and requires the configured threshold. Evidence Meaning Signed batch header Sequencer commitment to batch ordering and roots. Guarantor attestation A bonded signer's statement about a verified checkpoint. Checkpoint certificate Canonical aggregation of the required eligible attestations. Settlement registration The registry accepts the certificate under the deployed domain and contract rules. Checkpoint-certificate and guarantor-attestation signatures use distinct domain separators: LXP/v2/checkpoint-certificate and LXP/v2/guarantor-attestation , each followed by a null byte. Certificates carry an empty validity-proof field. An attestation is bonded re-execution evidence, not a zero-knowledge validity proof.

title: Bonded membership
content: The live implementation is the Go Cosmos module modules/layerxanchor , not a GuarantorBond contract; no GuarantorBond.sol exists in the monorepo. The module records guarantors with a signer and bond, and eligibility is narrow: a guarantor is eligible when its status is active and its bond is at least the module's MinBond parameter (default 1000000 in the bond denomination). Depositing tokens alone does not create membership authority. Older descriptions of a minimum bond computed as custodied value times a basis-point requirement, epoch/jail/ejection/unresolved-slashing eligibility checks, and a minimum one-day unbonding delay describe the retired contract narrative and were not found in the live module. Unbonding delay, equivocation/slashing paths, and peer-transport (mTLS) details were not verified in a live replacement producer and are not specified here.

title: Settlement confirmation
content: The submitter validates the deployed chain and registry binding, encodes the certificate, and submits a settlement transaction. Registration is confirmed against successful receipt status, transaction identity, the canonical block, and every checkpoint-registration event field. An existing registration is accepted only when it records the exact certificate. The node independently verifies the finality bundle returned to it. The producer then compares the node's stored finality evidence with the submitted bundle. These checks connect locally verified execution, the registered certificate, and the evidence applications subsequently consume.

title: Operator responsibilities
content: Maintain a distinct signing identity, exclusive persistent-state ownership, durable availability data, and retained attestations. Reuse stored attestations for a previously signed batch rather than generating replacement signatures. Peer-transport details were not verified in a live producer and are not specified here. Organizational and infrastructure independence require separate operator arrangements; two different keys alone do not establish that independence. Replay supports the direct-owner authority path and explicitly refuses unsupported oracle inputs or incomplete rotated-signer history. Treat these refusals as verification boundaries. A guarantor must obtain sufficient replay evidence before attesting.

title: Continue
content: See Finality , Governance , and Security and trust boundaries .

title: Build with Hardhat
content: Configure Hardhat 3 for Paxeer, test a Solidity contract locally, and keep repeatable deployments with Hardhat Ignition. Configure Hardhat 3 for Paxeer, test a Solidity contract locally, and keep repeatable deployments with Hardhat Ignition. Hardhat brings Solidity compilation, tests, and deployment records into a TypeScript project. This walkthrough creates a new Hardhat 3 project with its Mocha/Ethers toolbox and an explicit HTTP network for Paxeer chain ID 125 (Cosmos chain hyperpax_125-1 ; local or unmapped chains report other IDs, defaulting to 713714). It is separate from the repository's in-tree contract project, which remains Hardhat 2 with a CommonJS config — see the note under Configure the network.

title: Create a Hardhat 3 project
content: Use a Node.js version supported by Hardhat 3 . Run the initializer and choose the TypeScript project with Mocha and Ethers.js; install the dependencies it proposes. mkdir paxeer-hardhat cd paxeer-hardhat npx hardhat@3 --init npx hardhat --version The scaffold includes ESM configuration, a TypeScript configuration, and the toolbox plugins. Retain its lockfile so another developer uses the same toolchain.

title: Configure the network
content: In hardhat.config.ts , preserve any scaffold settings your project needs and use this network configuration. The compiler settings match the in-tree project (solc 0.8.27, Prague, which the chain enables from genesis); only the Hardhat 3 config shape is new. import { configVariable, defineConfig } from "hardhat/config"; import hardhatToolboxMochaEthers from "@nomicfoundation/hardhat-toolbox-mocha-ethers"; export default defineConfig({ plugins: [hardhatToolboxMochaEthers], solidity: { version: "0.8.27", settings: { evmVersion: "prague", optimizer: { enabled: true, runs: 1000 }, }, }, networks: { local: { type: "edr-simulated", chainType: "l1" }, paxeer: { type: "http", chainType: "l1", chainId: 125, url: configVariable("PAXEER_RPC_URL"), accounts: [configVariable("PAXEER_PRIVATE_KEY")], }, }, }); For reference, the in-tree project at contracts/ uses Hardhat 2 ( hardhat ^2.20.1 , toolbox ^4.0.0 ) with sources in ./src and a paxlocal network read from PAXEER_LOCAL_EVM_RPC_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8545 ). Use that project as-is for chain contracts; use this guide only for a new standalone project. Store your EVM endpoint and deployment key through the keystore plugin included in the toolbox. configVariable also resolves environment variables for CI and other automation. npx hardhat keystore set PAXEER_RPC_URL npx hardhat keystore set PAXEER_PRIVATE_KEY

title: Add and test the contract
content: Create contracts/PaxeerCounter.sol . This is the same small contract used by the Foundry guide. // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT pragma solidity 0.8.27; contract PaxeerCounter { uint256 public number; event NumberChanged(address indexed caller, uint256 number); function setNumber(uint256 next) external { number = next; emit NumberChanged(msg.sender, next); } function increment() external { number += 1; emit NumberChanged(msg.sender, number); } } Create contracts/PaxeerCounter.t.sol . A failed require fails the test; this test deploys and exercises the contract within the simulated EVM. // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT pragma solidity 0.8.27; import {PaxeerCounter} from "./PaxeerCounter.sol"; contract PaxeerCounterTest { function testIncrement() public { PaxeerCounter counter = new PaxeerCounter(); counter.increment(); require(counter.number() == 1, "increment did not persist"); } function testSetNumber(uint256 next) public { PaxeerCounter counter = new PaxeerCounter(); counter.setNumber(next); require(counter.number() == next, "value did not persist"); } } npx hardhat build npx hardhat test solidity Hardhat treats the parameterized test as a fuzz test. Keep existing scaffold contracts compatible with your chosen compiler or remove the unused scaffold examples when you make the project your own.

title: Describe the deployment
content: Create ignition/modules/PaxeerCounter.ts . Ignition records the deployment and can resume its own deployment plan when invoked again. import { buildModule } from "@nomicfoundation/hardhat-ignition/modules"; export default buildModule("PaxeerCounterModule", (m) => { const counter = m.contract("PaxeerCounter"); return { counter }; }); Exercise the deployment against the simulated network first. The simulated network uses local accounts and state. npx hardhat ignition deploy ignition/modules/PaxeerCounter.ts --network local

title: Deploy to your Paxeer endpoint
content: This command broadcasts using the configured signer and spends PAX for gas. Hardhat checks the endpoint against the configured chain ID. Review the deployment confirmation and retain the resulting address and transaction record. npx hardhat ignition deploy ignition/modules/PaxeerCounter.ts --network paxeer Keep ignition/deployments/chain-125/ , your source revision, and compiler configuration together. Read the receipt and deployed contract through the querying guide . For application tokens, configure the ERC-20 symbol and decimals independently of native PAX. For token contracts, the standard library package is @openzeppelin/contracts . Use a release compatible with your Solidity version; resolve imports such as @openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol against that installed package. References: Hardhat network configuration , Solidity tests , and Ignition deployments . Paxeer source: Paxeer-X-Network/ — contracts/hardhat.config.js and contracts/package.json (in-tree Hardhat 2, solc 0.8.27/Prague/1000), modules/evm/config/config.go (ChainIDMapping), and rpc/send.go (SendRawTransaction). This guide configures a new Hardhat 3 project. Previous Build with Foundry Next Build a Frontend

title: Human interface
content: Manage your Paxeer X identity, balances, agents, approvals, and recovery through evidence-backed journeys. Manage your Paxeer X identity, balances, agents, approvals, and recovery through evidence-backed journeys.

title: A human control plane for Paxeer X
content: The Human interface brings the LayerX execution system into an account experience: sign in with a passkey, add funds, create agents, authorize sensitive work, and follow every movement through receipts. Home combines your balance, managed agents, pending approvals, and recent activity. Human is custodial by default. Account authentication and protocol authority have separate roles. This separation lets you manage agents without exposing protocol signing keys to the browser. On the merged network, money moves through move journeys; the former wallet-binding, deposit, withdraw, and exit journey kinds are retired and remain readable only as closed history. Identity Purpose Authority Application identity Passkey authentication and device sessions Opens the Human account experience Protocol identity LayerX DID and account operations Custody service holds the primary signing key

title: Onboard and secure an account
content: Create an account with an email and display name. Register a passkey using the browser credential ceremony. Follow the protocol identity and recovery stages. Open the account when its protocol identity has a verified LayerX receipt. Onboarding progresses through creating the account, adding the passkey, setting up the protocol identity, and putting recovery in place. Resume continues the existing journey. A local progress indicator alone does not activate an account. Action Human API Create account POST /v1/accounts Register passkey POST /v1/passkeys/registrations , then POST /v1/passkeys/registrations/{registration_id} Read or resume onboarding GET /v1/onboarding , POST /v1/onboarding/resume Sign in POST /v1/passkeys/assertions , finish the assertion, then POST /v1/sessions Inspect or refresh sessions GET /v1/sessions , POST /v1/sessions/refresh

title: Wallet binding is retired
content: The former wallet-binding flow ( POST /v1/wallet-binding/statement , POST and GET /v1/wallet-binding , and rebind) is retired. Every binding type and operation is marked retired, and stored wallet-binding journeys read back only as closed history; they cannot resume signing or execution. There is no wallet to connect and no binding state to poll. An owner EVM address is bound to the DID during registration instead; see identity .

title: Create and govern managed agents
content: An agent has a name, purpose, and monthly spending limit. Creation establishes the agent, its protection, and first funding. A separate native fee budget sets maximum fees per activity, total fees, period length, and maximum fees per period; a spending allowance and a fee allowance serve different purposes. On networks enforcing native fee authority version 2, the finite native_fee_budget must be supplied at creation: omitting it refuses creation, and changing or rotating a key never silently replenishes it. POST /v1/agents Idempotency-Key: 9f3c1e6a0b8d4f72a5c9e1d3b7a2c4e6 { "name": "Research Runner", "purpose": "Buys datasets and pays per-use research services", "monthly_limit": { "amount": "250000000", "currency": "LXP" }, "native_fee_budget": { "...": "finite fee budget, required on fee-authority-v2 networks" } } The example follows the Human API wire format. Amounts are integer strings; present human-readable values using the asset's declared precision. Creation returns an agent-create journey. Control Operation Result Browse agents GET /v1/agents ; GET /v1/agents/{agent_id} Agent details and status Pause or resume POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/pause or /resume Updated Agent Change monthly limit POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/limit Updated Agent Fund Move quote and commit Receipt-backed movement journey Reclaim funds POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/reclaim Move journey using return semantics Rotate or recover keys POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/rotate or /recover Key challenge Archive POST /v1/agents/{agent_id}/archive with confirm_name Agent retirement journey Owner key rotation adds a disclosure and step-up before starting the rotation window. Retirement stops work and closes the agent. Pause returns the current Agent directly; it does not create a separate journey response.

title: Review approvals before money moves
content: Held activities appear as waiting-for-you . Open the approval to inspect the amount, counterparty, asset, fees, expiry, remaining budget after approval, and supporting evidence. A step-up ceremony confirms the disclosed action before approval. Rejecting resolves the request without approving its movement. List pending requests with GET /v1/approvals . Read GET /v1/approvals/{approval_id} and review its facts. Begin step-up with POST /v1/step-up and finish it with POST /v1/step-up/{challenge_id} using the supplied confirmation digest. Submit step_up_evidence to POST /v1/approvals/{approval_id}/approve , or use /reject . Read the decision's money_moved and evidence instead of inferring success from the button press. At decision time money_moved is false; movement is established by the resulting journey and receipt. Approval states are pending, approved, rejected, expired, and defective. Expiry and defective evidence prevent a request from being treated as an approved payment.

title: Read progress and proof
content: Journeys expose stages, evidence references, timestamps, and refusals. States are getting-ready, sending, processing, done, done-finalised, still-checking, refused, waiting-for-you, closed, and awaiting-approval. Closed is how retired wallet-binding, deposit, withdraw, and exit history reads back; awaiting-approval marks a journey held for approval and is not receipt-backed completion. A refusal identifies who refused, explanatory copy, money left, and an optional path to change the request. Verification Meaning unverified Submitted; no stronger authenticated execution evidence is attached receipt-verified Receipted; the LayerX execution receipt is verified checkpoint-finalised Committed; inclusion in a committed block is verified The former paxeer-finalised label is retired and defines no further rung. Use GET /v1/journeys , GET /v1/journeys/{journey_id} , and GET /v1/evidence/{evidence_id} . Evidence material includes its class, verification, content type, and base64 bytes. Live updates use POST /v1/stream and GET /v1/stream/{cursor} . These Human verification labels are distinct from RPC commitment names.

title: Recovery, sessions, and support
content: Security settings manage passkeys, individual or all sessions, authenticator enrollment, backup-code rotation, and recovery evidence. Sensitive actions use a disclosure digest and step-up authorization. Revealed recovery evidence is a timed secret with a remask timestamp and copy policy. Protocol keys remain in custody; the single exception is the export-primary-key security action, the only route by which a DID primary key leaves the service. Activity search uses POST /v1/activity/query ; detail uses GET /v1/activity/{entry_id} . Support conversations accept deposit, withdrawal, agents, account, and report topics through POST /v1/support/conversations . Continue with funding, money movement, and withdrawals or explore agent capabilities .

title: Identity, Ownership and Credentials
content: Connect human ownership, agent identities, hosted sessions and scoped signing authority across Paxeer X. Connect human ownership, agent identities, hosted sessions and scoped signing authority across Paxeer X.

title: One owner, explicit authority
content: Paxeer X connects an owner to an agent DID, a signing authority, an account and a recovery policy. These bindings make responsibility explicit when an agent prepares an activity, requests approval, delegates work or spends from a budget. A hosted login authenticates a principal; an activity signature authorizes a particular protocol action. Identity surface What it establishes What to retain Human owner The owner DID, protected Ed25519 authority and recovery commitment. Public registration evidence and secure custody references. Native account The account bound to the owner through the EVM/DID binding. Account identity and the committed binding transaction. Hosted principal Tenant, subject, allowed signer keys, optional account and audiences. The principal record and tenant context. Hosted session Time-limited access to hosted services. Session ID, expiry and securely held token. Agent capability The activities, counterparties, assets and limits an agent may use. Capability scope, expiry and revocation state.

title: Register an owner
content: Registration, funding, and recovery are transactions on the merged network (EVM chain ID 125). The pre-merge custody-credit bootstrap through the 0x1013 precompile is retired and is not a prerequisite; see custody . Provision the owner DID and recovery policy through the identity flow, and generate and protect the owner signing key. Bind the DID to the owner EVM address: read layerXBindNonce(address) from the address precompile at 0x…1004 , have the Ed25519 DID key sign the bind message, and call bindLayerX(bytes32, bytes) from that address. The binding is one EVM address per DID and one DID per address. Verify the committed transaction and LayerXBound event, then query getUnifiedAccount(address) for the main account ID. A successful query alone is insufficient, because an unbound address returns zero fields. Register identity and recovery state through LayerXAuth at 0x…101C : recordLifecycle(bytes payload, bytes32 idempotencyKey) executes Governance module 7 for the bound caller. Identity registration is ordinal 1 ( 71 01 00 02 || did_id32 || primary_key32 ); the recovery commitment is ordinal 3, with an optional five-field form carrying delay bounds. Rotation (ordinal 2) is not exposed through recordLifecycle . Fund the intended account with the correct native asset, keeping EVM gas funding distinct from the kernel account balance. Retain the activity IDs and receipt evidence. An account name such as agent:<actor-DID>:main identifies the intended account. Its account ID is derived by the protocol account codec, not by interpreting the DID as an address. Session authorization uses the dedicated grantSession and revokeGrant methods rather than the lifecycle payload.

title: Key and account representations
content: The Human authority reference accepts a lowercase 64-character public-key hex string or did:layerx: followed by the same key hex. The owner actor is the exact generated DID. The recovery root is unpadded base64url of the registered 32-byte commitment. Preserve these values exactly; whitespace, uppercase key hex, 0x prefixes and DID fragments are refused.

title: Hosted principals and sessions
content: The hosted identity API uses HTTPS and service Bearer authentication. The Provisioning service manages principals and sessions; the Registrar service can also create principals but cannot manage sessions. Consumer services introspect a user session using their own service credential, keeping user tokens separate from service authority. Method and path Purpose POST /v1/principals Create or update a principal and its signer/account/audience bindings. POST /v1/sessions Mint a session for a known subject. DELETE /v1/sessions/{id} Revoke a session by its 16-byte hex identifier. POST /v1/sessions/introspect Check whether a presented token is active for the calling service. POST /v1/introspect Use the same introspection contract through its alternate path. POST /v1/publication-keys , /v1/signup , /v1/signup/verify Publication-key registration and the signup flow. POST /v1/starter-credits , /v1/starter-credits/settle Starter-credit issuance and settlement. GET /internal/v1/principal , GET /internal/readyz Internal principal lookup and readiness. POST /v1/principals Content-Type: application/json Authorization: Bearer <provisioning-service-token> { "tenant": "treasury", "sub": "agent:treasury-operator", "allowed_signer_public_keys": ["<32-byte-lowercase-public-key-hex>"], "account": "<registered-account>", "audiences": ["ramp"] } POST /v1/sessions {"tenant":"treasury","sub":"agent:treasury-operator","ttl_seconds":3600} Replace bracketed values with established public bindings. The session response contains session_id , tenant , sub , token , csrf_token and expires_at . Tokens use ses_{32hex-id}.{64hex-secret} . Keep token and CSRF material out of URLs, logs and public configuration.

title: Session bounds and introspection
content: The default lifetime is 86,400 seconds. A session may request 1 through 2,592,000 seconds, with at most 4,096 live unrevoked sessions per principal. Principal subjects contain 1–128 lowercase identifier bytes. Signer lists contain at most 128 unique lowercase 32-byte hex keys; audience lists contain at most 32 unique identifiers. Gateway introspection returns the active subject and allowed signer keys. Developer consumers (Webhooks and Dashboard) receive the active subject and CSRF token. Ramp introspection additionally requires an authorized audience and a stored account. Unknown, expired, revoked or secret-mismatched sessions return an inactive result.

title: Delegate without surrendering ownership
content: Agent sessions carry tenant, agent DID, authority reference, permitted activity types, expiry, client and policy version. Capabilities restrict activity types, counterparties, assets, amount ceilings, rate ceilings, purpose constraints and expiry. Every dimension is required; an empty permission set denies the corresponding action. Use capability.create to establish authority, capability.attenuate to narrow a grant, capability.list to inspect grants and capability.revoke to withdraw authority. Combine capability scope with a funded agent budget and approval policy for monetary operations.

title: Rotation, revocation and recovery
content: Session grants are authorized through grantSession(bytes, uint64, bytes32) and withdrawn through revokeGrant(bytes32, uint8, uint64) . The version-1 session payload carries the canonical grant, its expiry sequence, and a 32-byte action key. Key rotation is not exposed through recordLifecycle ; use the dedicated ABI methods and verify scope and revocation state before authorizing a spend. Recovery uses the registered guardian commitment and threshold from the ordinal-3 lifecycle payload. Keep recovery material exercisable and separate from the primary owner key, and maintain the registered delay policy alongside that commitment.

title: Respond to a compromised credential
content: Revoke the affected hosted session and withdraw its agent capability. Close or revoke budgets exposed to the compromised delegate. Rotate the signing authority through the registered owner policy, or use the guardian recovery process. Verify committed policy state and receipts before issuing replacement credentials.

title: Errors and operational checks
content: The HTTP API returns typed errors with a retry policy. Invalid arguments, missing credentials and unauthorized service operations require corrected input or authority. Session capacity returns 429 session_bound_reached ; unavailable durable storage returns 503 store_unavailable . Respect Retry-After where supplied. GET /livez checks service liveness; GET /readyz verifies writable durable storage. Principal records, session digests and revocation state survive restart through a snapshot and journal. Token secrets are not stored in plaintext. Technical references: docs/wiki/HumanOwnerRegistration.md ; services/platform/hosted/identity/src/main.rs ; services/agent/schema/agent-api/identity.kvx . Continue with agent budgets and approvals .

title: Installation & Build
content: Build the Paxeer X node, deterministic LayerX kernel, hosted services, agent tools and Programs from the unified monorepo. Build the Paxeer X node, deterministic LayerX kernel, hosted services, agent tools and Programs from the unified monorepo. Source: paxeer-monorepo/Makefile , chain.mk , and paxeer-monorepo/README.md

title: Build the complete network stack
content: The monorepo contains the Go chain node, the C17 kernel, Rust service workspaces, SDKs, and program tooling. The running network entry point is paxd . The kernel runs inside paxd . There is no standalone kernel daemon to build or run. That daemon is retired. Component Build surface Purpose Merged node make paxd-build build/paxd with linked native libraries and release version stamp Kernel library and tools make build Kernel archive, genesis builder, and module registry, without rebuilding the node Agent services make agent-build Agent runtime and its service boundaries Human services make human-build Human API, providers, owner and security components Platform services make platform-build-all Gateway, core boundary, registry, and hosted services Programs and porting make programs-build Programs workspace and porting kits These commands run from the repository root. Use the Rust toolchain and dependency locks declared by each workspace, and the C compiler and native dependencies declared by the kernel build. Program guests target WebAssembly; install the target required by the selected guest before compiling it. Installation provides binaries and images. Joining a network also requires its genesis, network identity, and role-specific credentials. Retain build provenance and artifact checksums with the deployment record. Continue with node startup and operator roles .

title: Prerequisites
content: Go: 1.25.8, as declared in go.mod , or the toolchain required by the selected revision Rust: 1.91.1, as declared in rust-toolchain.toml C compiler: C17 compiler for the kernel, via the root Makefile Make: Standard build tool Git: For cloning the repository Solidity: 0.8.27 with Foundry, for contract builds Native toolchain: GCC and the native libraries required by the selected build. Use LEDGER_ENABLED=false to disable the optional Ledger build tag.

title: Repository Location
content: Clone the unified Sidiora-Labs/paxeer-monorepo repository. Chain sources, kernel sources, workspaces, and build configurations share this repository root. The name Paxeer-X-Network survives only as the Go module path. git clone https://github.com/Sidiora-Labs/paxeer-monorepo.git cd paxeer-monorepo

title: Build the Chain Node
content: Build the merged node from the repository root. make paxd-build is the primary entry point. It builds build/liblayerx.a and programs/target/release/liblayerx_programs_sandbox.a before invoking chain.mk , and stamps the version from tools/release/version.json . make paxd-build # build/paxd, linked native libraries and release version stamp make paxeer-build make paxeer-lint make paxeer-test make paxeer-ci make paxeer-build and make -f chain.mk build also build the linked native prerequisites and produce build/paxd , using the chain makefile's version defaults. Root make build builds only the kernel archive, genesis builder, and module registry. It does not produce a kernel daemon. Select the chain explicitly with chain.mk : make -f chain.mk build make -f chain.mk install make -f chain.mk test make -f chain.mk ci

title: Build Output
content: build/paxd from make paxd-build , make paxeer-build , or make -f chain.mk build . $GOBIN/paxd when GOBIN is set, otherwise $(go env GOPATH)/bin/paxd , from make -f chain.mk install . make workspace-build combines the kernel, services, node, app and tooling targets, and the root Foundry tree; make monorepo-ci delegates to the workspace CI target.

title: Ledger Support
content: Ledger hardware wallet support is enabled by default in chain.mk . To build without ledger: make paxeer-build LEDGER_ENABLED=false

title: Mock Balances (Testing)
content: For testing with mock balances: make -f chain.mk install-mock-balances

title: Benchmark Build
content: For benchmark runs: make -f chain.mk install-bench

title: Version Information
content: The Makefile resolves version from Git tags or branch names. The chain version resolver retains its historical namespaced tag pattern: paxeer-network/vX.Y.Z Version information is embedded in the binary at build time via linker flags: Name : paxeer AppName : paxd Version : Resolved from tag/branch Commit : Git commit SHA Check version: paxd version

title: Static Linking
content: To build a statically-linked binary: make paxeer-build LINK_STATICALLY=true

title: Go Module
content: The repository root declares the chain Go module: module github.com/Sidiora-Labs/Paxeer-X-Network go 1.25.8 Note: The root go.mod and go.sum govern the chain Go dependencies. Rust components use their own workspace manifests and lockfiles.

title: Foundry (Contracts)
content: Chain contracts under contracts/src/ use foundry.paxeer.toml . Fetch the pinned dependencies and build from the repository root: bash contracts/bootstrap-libs.sh FOUNDRY_CONFIG=foundry.paxeer.toml forge build --offline --root . Kernel contracts also live under contracts/ , using repository-root foundry.toml and tests/solidity/ . See contracts/README.md and the contracts guide for the two project configurations.

title: Docker
content: Local Docker cluster targets are available. See Docker documentation for: make docker-cluster-start make run-local-node Compose configurations in docker/

title: Choose a Node Configuration
content: Use the local Docker configuration to try the built binary, or initialize a node with the genesis, peers, and mode for your chosen network. For an existing network, select the binary revision specified by its upgrade plan.

content: Run a node Configure paxd Use Docker for local testing Previous Network Parameters Next Run a Node

title: Interchain (IBC)
content: Connect Paxeer X to other chains through IBC packets, native token transfers, and the attested bridge. Connect Paxeer X to other chains through IBC packets, native token transfers, and the attested bridge. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/interchain/ , precompiles/ibc/ , and the IBC keeper and router wiring in node/app.go .

title: Cross-chain routes in Paxeer X
content: Paxeer X supports IBC transfers through its Cosmos protocol stack and attested external-chain transfers through the native bridge . IBC authenticates packets with light clients, connections, channel state, and packet proofs. The bridge authenticates external deposits with a configured attestor threshold and enforces registered chains, asset caps, nullifiers, and pause controls. The bridge precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001016 exposes bridgeIn , bridgeOut , chain and attestor queries, cap queries, replay status, and pause state. IBC transfers use 0x1009 . Choose the route supported by the destination and asset; an IBC channel identifier is separate from the bridge chain registry identifier. Record the source transaction, destination identifier, asset denomination, amount, and transfer status. Treat packet acknowledgement or timeout separately from bridge attestation and destination release. Continue with assets , settlement , and the unified network .

title: Protocol and implementation
content: The in-tree IBC implementation provides clients, connections, channels, packet commitments, and application routing. Relayers submit proofs and carry packets and acknowledgements between chains. A working transfer requires compatible live clients, an open channel, and relayer delivery. Query the target network for the port, channel, counterparty, and supported denomination before sending funds. Source directory Purpose interchain/modules/core/ Client, connection, channel, port, and commitment protocol logic. interchain/modules/apps/transfer/ ICS-20 fungible-token transfer messages, packets, and keeper. interchain/modules/apps/27-interchain-accounts/ Interchain-account implementation. interchain/modules/light-clients/ Tendermint ( 07-tendermint ), solo-machine ( 06-solomachine ), and localhost ( 09-localhost ) light-client code. precompiles/ibc/ EVM interface to native ICS-20 transfers.

title: Inspect clients and channels
content: Configure the CLI's Cosmos RPC endpoint for the Paxeer node being queried, then inspect its state: paxd query ibc client states paxd query ibc connection connections paxd query ibc channel channels Verify the channel's port, connection, remote chain, ordering, and open state. Channel identifiers such as channel-0 are local to a chain; they are not universal destinations.

title: Transfer through the CLI
content: This command template sends 1,000,000 uhpx , one PAX. Set IBC_CHANNEL to a verified channel and IBC_RECIPIENT to an address valid on its destination chain. paxd tx ibc-transfer transfer \ transfer "$IBC_CHANNEL" "$IBC_RECIPIENT" 1000000uhpx \ --from mykey --chain-id hyperpax_125-1 Use the actual bank denomination for other assets. An IBC voucher has its own denomination trace; do not substitute a display ticker for a bank denomination.

title: Transfer directly from the EVM
content: The precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001009 exposes two nonpayable transfer methods. Use the full precompiles/ibc/abi.json for client bindings. interface IBC { function transfer( string calldata toAddress, string calldata port, string calldata channel, string calldata denom, uint256 amount, uint64 revisionNumber, uint64 revisionHeight, uint64 timeoutTimestamp, string calldata memo ) external returns (bool success); function transferWithDefaultTimeout( string calldata toAddress, string calldata port, string calldata channel, string calldata denom, uint256 amount, string calldata memo ) external returns (bool success); } The immediate EVM caller must have a Paxeer address association and sufficient native-denomination balance. A wrapper uses the wrapper's associated account. amount is a bank base-unit integer, not payable EVM value; delegatecall and staticcall are rejected. The explicit method takes an absolute remote timeout height and timestamp. IBC timestamps use nanoseconds. The default-timeout method derives its timeout from the channel's connection and client state: the height is the client's latest height plus the relative default 0-1000 (revision 0, height 1000), and the timestamp is ten minutes in nanoseconds beyond the later of the client consensus timestamp and the current block time. It can fail when required channel or client state is absent. The ABI submits transfers; it does not expose channel enumeration or a general incoming-packet callback. Use the native query interfaces to inspect IBC state.

title: Track the whole transfer
content: A successful local transaction means the source-chain transfer was accepted. It does not mean the destination has already received the assets. Retain the source transaction and packet identifiers, then track relay, acknowledgement, or timeout/refund handling on both chains. Configure your relayer for both networks, check that its clients are current, and monitor packet delivery and acknowledgement processing.

title: Implementation references
content: precompiles/ibc/IBC.sol : exact public selectors. precompiles/ibc/ibc.go : associated sender, amount conversion, timeout derivation, and keeper invocation. interchain/modules/apps/transfer/ : packet lifecycle and native transfer behavior. Precompile reference and native query interfaces . Previous SDK Next Admin & HPX

title: Interoperability
content: Connect agent payments, commerce mandates, card and bank rails, and external chains to Paxeer X through evidence-backed adapters. Connect agent payments, commerce mandates, card and bank rails, and external chains to Paxeer X through evidence-backed adapters.

title: One execution ledger, many entry points
content: Interoperability adapters translate foreign protocols into evidence that LayerX execution can verify. They preserve the original protocol's authorization and settlement facts while routing state changes through a receipt-verified LayerX operation. Paxeer X retains custody and withdrawal guarantees. The interoperability gateway provides HTTP, MCP, and A2A ingress. Transport selects how a request arrives; the adapter selects how its evidence is validated. Applications keep the same operation identity and reconciliation process across these interfaces.

title: Connector catalogue
content: Adapter Application journey Evidence boundary x402 Buyer builds payment, seller offers a resource, facilitator verifies and settles Payment evidence plus verified LayerX receipt; HTTP, MCP, and A2A transports ap2 Verify an agent commerce mandate and execute within its authority Verified mandate and LayerX receipt ucp Complete a commerce checkout Checkout evidence and receipt-gated execution visa-tap Verify a trusted agent intent and execute its authorized action Trusted agent credential, canonical target, and policy checks fiat Process card, bank, and real-time-payment callbacks External settlement evidence and LayerX receipt migration-v2 Import verified account, asset, and history state Source-chain verification and migration rules

title: Gateway discovery and operation tracking
content: GET /v1/adapters exposes adapter metadata. Track an operation with GET /v1/operations/{id} , where id is exactly 64 hexadecimal characters. The service also exposes GET /livez and GET /readyz for process and readiness checks. These are gateway paths relative to the configured gateway origin. # Use the gateway origin assigned to your environment. curl "$INTEROP_GATEWAY/v1/adapters" curl "$INTEROP_GATEWAY/v1/operations/$OPERATION_ID" Build the request body from the selected adapter's schema. Preserve operation identifiers and evidence digests through retries. A successful HTTP exchange reports the gateway exchange; the operation's receipt-backed outcome establishes the state change.

title: Evidence policies
content: Policy Required basis layerx-receipt A verified LayerX execution receipt verified-mandate+layerx-receipt Accepted mandate authority and a verified execution receipt trusted-agent-credential Agent credential accepted by the configured trust policy external-settlement+layerx-receipt External rail settlement evidence paired with a verified execution receipt

title: x402 over HTTP, MCP, and A2A
content: x402 supports buyer, seller, and facilitator roles. The same route family accepts http , mcp , or a2a as its transport segment. Capability discovery comes before constructing a payment, so clients can select the supported scheme and network. Method Path Purpose GET /v1/{transport}/x402/supported Discover payment support GET /v1/{transport}/x402/facilitator/supported Discover facilitator support POST /v1/{transport}/x402/buyer/build Build buyer evidence POST /v1/{transport}/x402/seller/offer Produce a seller offer POST /v1/{transport}/x402/verify Verify payment evidence POST /v1/{transport}/x402/settle Settle through LayerX execution Verification also has the /facilitator/verify variant; settlement has /seller/settle and /facilitator/settle variants beneath the same x402 prefix. Commitment extras and metered or subscription grant draws let applications bind payments to a resource and consume an authorized allowance over time.

title: Paid resource workflow
content: The seller publishes an offer identifying the resource and payment terms. The buyer discovers support and builds evidence for the selected terms. The seller or facilitator verifies the evidence before accepting the purchase. Settlement submits the LayerX operation and verifies its receipt. The application associates resource delivery with the accepted payment operation and retains its evidence for reconciliation.

title: Agent commerce and fiat rails
content: Method HTTP route Action POST /v1/http/ap2/mandates/verify Verify mandate POST /v1/http/ap2/execute Execute authorized mandate POST /v1/http/ucp/checkouts/complete Complete checkout POST /v1/http/visa-tap/intents/verify Verify trusted-agent intent POST /v1/http/visa-tap/intents/execute Execute accepted intent POST /v1/http/fiat/card/callbacks Accept card-rail evidence POST /v1/http/fiat/bank/callbacks Accept bank-rail evidence POST /v1/http/fiat/rtp/callbacks Accept real-time-payment evidence Unlike x402, these adapters are HTTP-only: there is no MCP or A2A variant of the routes above. Mandate verification establishes what an agent may do before execution changes state. TAP policy binds the trusted agent and canonical request target, with clock-skew limits owned by the service. Fiat callbacks bind external settlement to the LayerX operation; repeating a provider notification must reconcile the original operation rather than credit it twice.

title: Migration imports
content: The hosted migration adapter is migration-v2 . It is served under /v2 , not the /v1 adapter prefix, and every route is a POST. Other methods, a /v1 prefix, or a trailing slash are unknown routes. Method Route Action POST /v2/migration/accounts Import accounts POST /v2/migration/assets Import assets POST /v2/migration/history Import history POST /v2/migration/history/read Read imported history

title: Portable receipts and mirrors
content: Portable receipt verification checks LayerX evidence without requiring a live node connection. Ethereum and Solana mirrors publish batch archives and commitments so independent consumers can verify committed LayerX evidence; see Ethereum & Solana Mirrors . Mirrors carry verification data; custody remains on Paxeer X. Choose migration for a source-state transition, a mirror for independent archive verification, and the bridge for a custody-backed asset transfer. Preserve the source chain identity and proof material in each case.

title: Admission and receipts
content: Adapters ultimately submit operations to LayerX execution. An admission acknowledgement precedes execution and publication, so it does not by itself establish a state change. Receipt lookup is the step that establishes the operation's outcome. Integrations keep gateway exchange, admission, execution receipt, and settlement evidence as separate records, keyed by the operation identifier.

title: Continue building
content: Explore bridging and custody , execution and settlement architecture , and native chain APIs to connect protocol evidence to chain state.

title: Unsupported JSON-RPC Methods
content: Ethereum JSON-RPC methods that are explicitly unsupported on Paxeer EVM. Ethereum JSON-RPC methods that are explicitly unsupported on Paxeer EVM. Source: rpc/info.go , rpc/filter.go , rpc/tracers.go , rpc/state.go and rpc/tx.go in the Paxeer node source.

title: Overview
content: Some Ethereum JSON-RPC methods are registered on Paxeer's EVM endpoint but return a JSON-RPC error instead of a result. This gives clients and tools a stable, documented failure (code -32000 ) rather than "method not found" ( -32601 ).

title: Explicitly Unsupported Methods
content: Method Typical Error Message Reason eth_blobBaseFee "blobs not supported on this chain" EIP-4844 blob transactions not supported eth_newPendingTransactionFilter "eth_newPendingTransactionFilter is not supported on Pax EVM RPC" Only on nodes without a receipt-log feed; sequencer and standby nodes serve it (see below) debug_getRawBlock "debug_getRawBlock is not supported on Pax EVM RPC" Raw RLP block payloads not served debug_getRawHeader "debug_getRawHeader is not supported on Pax EVM RPC" Raw RLP header payloads not served debug_getRawReceipts "debug_getRawReceipts is not supported on Pax EVM RPC" Raw RLP receipt payloads not served

title: Now implemented
content: Two methods that previously returned this error are implemented. eth_syncing returns false when consensus reports the node caught up, and otherwise a progress object with startingBlock , currentBlock and highestBlock . debug_getRawTransaction returns the raw transaction bytes for a hash, or a transaction not found error. Only debug_getRawHeader , debug_getRawBlock and debug_getRawReceipts remain explicitly unsupported.

title: Error Response Format
content: Unsupported methods return a standard JSON-RPC error: { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1, "error": { "code": -32000, "message": "blobs not supported on this chain" } }

title: eth_syncing
content: eth_syncing is implemented from the consensus status: false when the node is caught up, otherwise startingBlock (earliest held block), currentBlock and highestBlock .

title: eth_newPendingTransactionFilter
content: On sequencer and standby nodes, which hold the receipt-log feed, this filter is served: each poll returns the hashes of transactions receipted since the last poll, in sequence order. Full-transaction mode ( fullTx: true ) is refused — the filter serves transaction hashes only. On every other node the call returns the -32000 unsupported error. Independently, the node tracks pending nonces, and eth_getTransactionCount(address, "pending") uses the local pending nonce or forwards the request to the appropriate EVM proxy.

title: debug_getRaw* Methods
content: Raw RLP-encoded headers, blocks and receipt lists are not served on this RPC surface; use the standard eth_* endpoints, which return structured JSON. Raw transaction bytes are the exception: debug_getRawTransaction is implemented and returns them by hash.

title: eth_blobBaseFee
content: The current implementation rejects EIP-4844 blob transactions in transaction admission. The blob fee RPC returns the explicit unsupported error shown above.

title: Broader Compatibility Notes
content: Beyond explicitly unsupported methods, Paxeer's RPC diverges from Ethereum in several conceptual areas:

title: Block Tags and Pending Nonces
content: Block-number helpers resolve latest , safe , finalized and pending to the latest height; endpoint watermarks can further limit the readable state. Pending nonce queries have a separate path.
