Do not assume pending and latest return the same nonce. A BFT commit provides finality under the consensus protocol’s assumptions. RPC freshness and finality are separate properties.

title: Storage Proofs Use a Different Format
content: eth_getProof is implemented by StateAPI.GetProof . Its result contains address , hexValues and storageProof . Storage proofs contain IAVL proof operations rather than Ethereum Merkle Patricia trie proofs. The response excludes Ethereum per-account proof fields because the store has no Ethereum per-account root. Ethereum proof verifiers cannot consume this response unchanged. The requested height must be readable and the configured store must support proof queries. Historical retention and endpoint availability still apply.

title: No Proof-of-Work
content: eth_mining and eth_hashrate have no implementation on any registered API, so they return method-not-found ( -32601 ), not the registered -32000 unsupported error. Do not branch on -32000 for them. Paxeer uses BFT consensus, not PoW See JSON-RPC API for full compatibility details.

title: Implementation Checks
content: The node repository contains focused checks for these RPC contracts: rpc/info_test.go rpc/state_test.go rpc/tracers_test.go rpc/filter_test.go For provider-specific method support, check the endpoint configuration and inspect the JSON-RPC result or error returned by each request. Previous JSON-RPC API Next REST & gRPC

title: JSON-RPC API
content: Paxeer's EVM JSON-RPC interface with standard Ethereum compatibility and Paxeer-specific enhancements. Paxeer's EVM JSON-RPC interface with standard Ethereum compatibility and Paxeer-specific enhancements. For complete read-only examples, follow Query the EVM or the Python Quickstart . Use Debug Transactions to work from a failed receipt to a reproducible diagnosis. Source: rpc/server.go (registration), tx.go (pending nonces), state.go (proofs), and subscribe.go (subscriptions) in the monorepo

title: Architecture Overview
content: Paxeer provides a comprehensive RPC interface that combines standard Ethereum JSON-RPC compatibility with Paxeer-specific enhancements. The API includes these namespaces:

title: Namespace Summary
content: Namespace Transaction Visibility Use Case eth_ EVM transactions only Pure EVM applications, Ethereum tooling compatibility pax_ EVM + Cosmos transactions (synthetic receipts) Full chain visibility, cross-chain event indexing pax2_ EVM + Cosmos + bank transfers Complete transaction view including native transfers debug_ EVM tracing and debugging Transaction replay, gas profiling, state inspection px_ Sequencer receipt keys px_getReceiptKeys for local receipt verification (HTTP only) echo_ , net_ , web3_ Liveness, network identity, client version Standard utility namespaces txpool_ Mempool inspection Pending/queued transaction views (HTTP only) Transport coverage differs. HTTP registers echo , eth , pax , pax2 , px , net , txpool , web3 and debug . WebSocket registers only echo , net , web3 and eth — there is no pax_ , pax2_ , debug_ , txpool_ or px_ on WebSocket connections.

title: eth_ Endpoints
content: The eth_ prefixed endpoints provide a pure EVM-compatible view: EVM-only: Only process and return EVM transactions Ethereum tooling: Use ethers.js, viem, web3.js, Hardhat, and Foundry with the method-specific differences below Transaction view: EVM transactions and their emitted logs Method contracts: Standard request shapes with documented Paxeer differences

title: Key eth_ Methods
content: eth_blockNumber eth_getBlockByNumber , eth_getBlockByHash eth_getTransactionByHash eth_getTransactionReceipt eth_getLogs eth_call , eth_estimateGas eth_sendRawTransaction eth_getBalance , eth_getCode

title: pax_ Endpoints
content: The pax_ prefixed endpoints provide an enhanced view that includes both EVM and relevant Cosmos transactions: Synthetic transactions: Cosmos events (CW20, CW721) exposed as EVM logs Full visibility: See both EVM and Cosmos activity Cross-chain events: Index pointer contracts and token transfers Trace filtering: Variants to exclude pre-state check failures

title: Synthetic Transaction Endpoints
content: These endpoints bridge Cosmos and EVM by exposing Cosmos-native events as EVM-compatible logs: pax_getLogs — Enhanced eth_getLogs with synthetic logs pax_getFilterLogs — Enhanced eth_getFilterLogs with synthetic logs pax_getBlockByNumber , pax_getBlockByHash — Include synthetic transactions pax_getBlockReceipts — Include receipts for synthetic transactions Receipt lookup: Use eth_getTransactionReceipt with the synthetic transaction hash.

title: Trace Failure Filtering
content: A block can contain transactions that fail before EVM execution, including nonce or balance checks. Use the following endpoints when you need a view that excludes those failures: pax_traceBlockByNumberExcludeTraceFail pax_traceBlockByHashExcludeTraceFail pax_getTransactionReceiptExcludeTraceFail pax_getBlockByNumberExcludeTraceFail pax_getBlockByHashExcludeTraceFail

title: pax2_ Endpoints (Bank Transfers)
content: The pax2_ namespace exposes the same block shape as pax_ but includes bank transfers in block payloads: Seven methods: block, block receipts, transaction counts, ExcludeTraceFail variants No pax2_ transaction or filter API HTTP only (not WebSocket)

title: Legacy API Gating
content: Both pax_* and pax2_* are legacy APIs gated by [evm].enabled_legacy_pax_apis in app.toml : Deprecated: Scheduled for removal Allow list: Only methods in the config array are enabled Default config: Three pax_* address/Cosmos helpers pre-filled ( pax_getPaxAddress , pax_getEVMAddress , pax_getCosmosTx ) Disabled response: JSON-RPC error -32601 , message explains deprecation Coverage: rpc/pax_legacy_test.go

title: Transaction Index Mismatches
content: Important: Transaction indices differ between eth_ and pax_ endpoints.

title: Example
content: Consider a block with: EVM Transaction 1 Cosmos Transaction 1 EVM Transaction 2

title: eth_getBlockReceipts
content: Returns only EVM transactions with sequential indices: EVM Transaction 1 (tx index: 0) EVM Transaction 2 (tx index: 1)

title: pax_getBlockReceipts
content: Returns all transactions (EVM + Cosmos) with sequential indices: EVM Transaction 1 (tx index: 0) Cosmos Transaction 1 (tx index: 1) EVM Transaction 2 (tx index: 2)

title: Receipts and Logs
content: EVM-originating: Synthetic events included in both eth_getLogs and eth_getTransactionReceipt Cosmos-originating: Synthetic events not in eth_ methods; use pax_getLogs and pax_getBlockReceipts logIndex values: Strictly increasing and consistent within each namespace

title: Best Practice
content: Use the same endpoint consistently within your application Account for index differences when switching endpoints Prefer transaction hashes over indices (hashes are consistent across endpoints)

title: debug_ Endpoints
content: Use debug_trace* methods to inspect historical execution: Inspect failed call frames and returned error data Compare gas consumption across calls and opcodes Review the state accesses and changes exposed by the selected tracer

title: Key debug_ Methods
content: debug_traceBlockByNumber , debug_traceBlockByHash debug_traceTransaction debug_traceCall

title: Paxeer RPC Distinctions
content: Paxeer's RPC deviates from Ethereum in several areas:

title: Block Tags and Pending Nonces
content: Committed-state reads resolve supported latest, safe, and finalized tags through the RPC publication watermarks Pending account nonces have a separate path: eth_getTransactionCount(address, "pending") uses the mempool’s next nonce or a configured proxy Track submitted hashes and use the pending nonce when coordinating multiple transactions from one account

title: No Uncle Blocks
content: Paxeer finalizes blocks through BFT consensus and does not produce Ethereum uncle blocks The uncle endpoints are registered on HTTP and WebSocket and answer with the empty result: eth_getUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex and eth_getUncleByBlockHashAndIndex return null , and eth_getUncleCountByBlockNumber / eth_getUncleCountByBlockHash return 0x0 for known blocks

title: Storage Proof Format
content: eth_getProof is implemented for proof-capable stores The result contains address , hexValues , and IAVL storageProof operations; it is not Ethereum’s Merkle Patricia account-proof shape Use an IAVL proof verifier and an endpoint retaining proof-capable state at the requested height

title: No Proof-of-Work
content: eth_mining and eth_hashrate are not registered on any API, so they return method-not-found ( -32601 ) rather than the explicit -32000 unsupported error Paxeer uses BFT consensus, not PoW

title: No Blobs
content: EIP-4844 blob transactions not supported eth_blobBaseFee returns error -32000 : "blobs not supported on this chain" See Unsupported Methods for the complete list.

title: Consistent Historical Reads
content: Pin related reads to one block number and retain its block hash with indexed data. Use a provider with the historical state your application needs, and keep the same namespace when reading blocks, receipts, and logs.

title: WebSocket Support
content: Paxeer RPC supports WebSocket for: eth_subscribe for newHeads and logs Pending-transaction subscriptions are not implemented by SubscriptionAPI eth_unsubscribe Legacy pax2_* endpoints are HTTP-only, as are pax_ , debug_ , txpool_ and px_ . WebSocket serves the echo , net , web3 and eth namespaces. Previous WASM Runtime Next Unsupported Methods

title: Launchpad
content: Create fixed-supply instruments, open virtual-reserve markets, trade with explicit limits, and direct accumulated fees. Create fixed-supply instruments, open virtual-reserve markets, trade with explicit limits, and direct accumulated fees.

title: From issuance to an active market
content: Paxeer X Launchpad deploys a CREATE2 SidioraERC20 token, creates its SidioraPool, mints an NFT fee right, and opens a virtual-reserve curve in one market-creation workflow. The market's native denomination is launchpad/ followed by the pool address hex. Human and agent-controlled businesses can issue instruments while trading agents buy and sell those instruments through explicit transaction permissions. The instrument represents the issuer's declared terms. Creating a market does not establish equity, revenue rights, or a legal claim automatically. Keep the business identity, creator account, token address, and instrument description visible in your application. Choose a name, symbol, fee strategy, and optical address (zero address when unused); fund the creator with the configured quote asset and transaction gas. Submit createMarket(name, symbol, feeStrategy, optical) to the Launchpad precompile; it returns (token, pool, nftId) . A permit variant, createMarketWithPermit , takes the same arguments plus permit parameters. Read the confirmed MarketCreated event and retain the token address, pool address, NFT id, and native denomination. Inspect reserves and a fresh buy or sell quote before signing an order. Operate fee distribution and market pause controls under the appropriate authority.

title: Creation and supply
content: The creation fee is paid in the configured quote token. Launchpad deploys the token with its fixed supply, binds it to the pool with bindPool , and transfers the supply to the pool. Market indices start at one and increase per market; the denomination is launchpad/<pool hex> , not a numbered subdenomination. The creator begins as guardian and fee-rights holder, and the fee right is represented by the minted NFT ( nftId ). Names contain at most 64 bytes and symbols at most 16. Both are nonblank UTF-8 without surrounding whitespace or control characters. Market supply and initial reserve settings come from protocol parameters rather than a per-call supply argument.

title: Curve reserves and executable prices
content: A market tracks virtual quote reserve, real quote balance, and token reserve. Effective quote reserve is the sum of virtual and real quote reserves. Virtual liquidity shapes the pricing curve; it is not a funded quote balance that can be withdrawn. Sells remain constrained by real quote liquidity. The market record includes total supply, cumulative volume, creation time, accumulated fees, pause state, and an eight-slot price-snapshot ring. Use getPoolPrice(pool) for a reference price, getPoolStats(pool) for reserves, volume, current fee, and market cap, and quoteExactInput(pool, amountIn, isBuy) for an amount-specific estimate returning amount out, fee amount, and price impact. quoteMultihop quotes token-to-token routes through the quote asset.

title: Trade with slippage and expiry limits
content: The precompile is 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001017 . buy(pool, usdlAmountIn, minTokensOut, deadline) and sell(pool, tokenAmountIn, minUsdlOut, deadline) are keyed by pool address and take no recipient argument; output goes to the caller. Permit variants ( buyWithPermit , sellWithPermit ) and the multihop swapTokenForToken(tokenIn, tokenOut, amountIn, minAmountOut, deadline) are also exposed. Both calls are nonpayable: EVM native value is not the quote payment. // launchpad is an ethers Contract using the Launchpad ABI and signer. // pool and quoteIn come from the selected market and user input. const quote = await launchpad.quoteExactInput(pool, quoteIn, true) const minOut = quote.amountOut * 9900n / 10000n // 1% tolerance const deadline = BigInt(Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) + 120) const tx = await launchpad.buy(pool, quoteIn, minOut, deadline) await tx.wait() This template assumes the connected account has the required quote balance (and allowance, or a permit) and gas. The pool address identifies the market; do not substitute the token or quote asset address. A stale quote does not reserve liquidity. The signed minimum output and deadline protect execution when reserves or fees change.

title: Buy and sell fee behavior
content: Fees are charged in the input asset. On a buy, the protocol share of quote fees goes to the treasury and the remainder accumulates for the market's fee-rights holder. On a sell, token fees remain in the token reserve. Dynamic fees use market age and volatility, clamped to configured bounds; a quote supplies the effective rate for that trade.

title: Choose where accumulated fees go
content: Value Strategy Execution 0 Claim claimFees(nftId) pays accumulated quote fees to the fee-rights holder; the accumulator-level claim(pool, recipient) pays a chosen recipient. 1 Burn executeBurn(nftId) sends accumulated quote fees to the dead account. 2 Airdrop executeAirdrop(nftId) opens a holder distribution epoch. 3 LP rewards executeLpRewards(nftId) adds accumulated quote fees to real curve reserves. The fee-rights holder changes strategy with setFeeStrategy(nftId, newStrategy) and executes the selected strategy. Fee functions on this surface are keyed by nftId ; accumulator-level functions are keyed by pool (for example getAccumulatedFees(pool) ). Burn here directs quote fees to the dead account; it does not burn the launched token's fixed supply. LP rewards reinforce the market's quote backing rather than issuing a separate LP token.

title: Holder airdrop epochs
content: Each airdrop fixes its distribution amount, holder history, supply, payout denomination, and block height. Entitlement is the integer floor of epoch amount multiplied by the holder's boundary balance divided by boundary supply. Later transfers do not rewrite the historical entitlement. A holder claims the current epoch through claimAirdrop(nftId) (or the accumulator-level claimAirdrop(pool, holder) ); each holder claims an epoch once. Use claimAirdropEpoch(nftId, epoch) to claim a specified opened epoch.

title: Permissions and market controls
content: Actor Authority Creator Funds creation and starts as guardian and fee-rights holder. Guardian Pauses and unpauses market trading. Fee-rights holder Changes fee strategy and executes fee disposition. Trader Spends its own input balance and selects minimum output and deadline; output is paid to the caller. Token holder Claims eligible airdrop entitlement. Governance authority Updates protocol parameters through the governance-authorized parameter message. Paused markets reject swaps. Orders also reject expired deadlines, zero input, insufficient balances or real liquidity, and output below the signed minimum. These are transaction conditions your interface should explain before prompting for a signature.

title: Read markets and track receipts
content: getAllPools(offset, limit) paginates discovery; getPoolCount() returns the total; getPoolsByCreator(creator) groups issuance by creator; and getPoolByToken(token) , getNftIdByPool(pool) , and getPoolMetadata(pool) resolve one market. getPoolStats , getPoolPrice , and getMarketCap support trading views. Markets exist in Generation 1 and Generation 2 SidioraPool forms; new markets are created as Generation 2. Index MarketCreated , Swap , FeeFlow , FeeDistributed , FeeStrategyChanged , PoolRegistered , PoolStateUpdated , and TokenDeployed . Reconcile event observations against the confirmed market record and balances before showing a completed issuance, trade, or claim.

title: Protocol settings
content: The default quote token is the USDL ERC-20 at 0x85FcD13735F4309833A503EE804ea32395851479 . Reference defaults set virtual quote reserve to 10000000000 , token supply (virtual token default) to 1000000000000000 base units, and creation fee to 1000000 quote base units. Fee bounds start at 10–300 basis points with a base of 30, and the protocol receives 1000 basis points of buy fees. Governance can update these values; read current settings (for example creationFee() , baseFeeBps() , virtualUsdlDefault() ) before presenting a launch cost or fee estimate. Continue with asset registration and supply , exchange trading , precompile integration , and SDKs .

title: LayerX Kernel
content: The deterministic C17 execution core of Paxeer X: one signed activity, one canonical history, and one reproducible result. The deterministic C17 execution core of Paxeer X: one signed activity, one canonical history, and one reproducible result. The LayerX kernel executes agent activity across payments, escrow, budgets, streams, services, trading, governance, assets, bridges, and programs. It resolves authority, applies state transitions, produces receipts, and binds each result to the next state root. Paxeer provides the EVM settlement and custody layer; ordinary LayerX operations run through the activity protocol without requiring a separate Paxeer transaction.

title: Three execution invariants
content: Invariant Meaning for applications One canonical history Global sequences order admitted activities. State roots chain per activity. The append-only log is authoritative; query indexes can be rebuilt. One financial doorway Modules do not write balances directly. Economic modules and programs propose validated transfer sets, and the only module-to-ledger entry is lxp_kernel_apply_transfer_set , preserving a common accounting boundary. One reproducible result Independent replay produces identical receipts and roots from the same ordered input, parameter versions, and batch time.

title: Canonical activities
content: Each state-changing action uses a signed lxp_activity envelope. The canonical binary encoding uses fixed-width big-endian integers, explicit fields, and no floating point or maps. A valid decode must re-encode to the same bytes; extra trailing bytes are rejected. Field Purpose protocol_version , network_id Select the enabled protocol rules and prevent cross-network replay. Protocol 1 is legacy, 2 adds occupancy, and 3 adds state commitment. activity_type The high 16 bits identify the module; the low 16 identify the operation ordinal. actor_did , authority Identify the principal and primary key, session, or capability grant authorizing the action. account_sequence Must exactly match the actor’s next sequence; gaps and stale sequences are refused. timestamp_bound Bounds validity using the sealed batch timestamp. idempotency_key Binds the retry identity of the activity. Retain the exact signed bytes and key for recovery; do not assume re-executing a duplicate returns the original receipt — recover the outcome through receipt and status reads. fee_limit Caps the deterministic execution fee the actor authorizes. payload , payload_hash , signature Bind the operation body and its Ed25519 authorization to the canonical signing preimage.

title: From admission to state transition
content: Decode and check the envelope, including protocol version, network, payload binding, and module enablement. Resolve the actor and authority, verify the signature, and enforce the exact account sequence. Evaluate timestamp bounds against batch time. Compute the fee against the active schedule and the activity’s fee limit. Open the state journal; dispatch module validation and execution. Commit successful module effects or roll them back on execution refusal. Apply required fee and sequence bookkeeping and produce a receipt chained to the resulting state root.

title: Admission refusal and execution failure
content: Malformed envelopes, wrong-network requests, and payload-hash mismatches fail admission without consuming the account sequence or charging an execution fee. A terminal rejection still occupies its global sequence, but it does not consume the actor’s account sequence and no fee is charged. Module effects roll back, while protocol bookkeeping persists. Applications must inspect the receipt’s result code before treating an action as successful.

title: Identity is part of execution
content: Agent DIDs are native accounts. The kernel enforces primary and session keys, scoped grants, rotation, recovery, revocation, and expiry. Delegation can narrow authority without widening it. See Identity and delegated authority for the identity lifecycle.

title: Determinism across machines
content: Consensus execution uses C17 and deterministic protocol types. It excludes floating point, local wall-clock reads, unstable database iteration, and pointer-derived hashing. Time-dependent rules—including grant expiry, escrow deadlines, stream accrual, funding intervals, and governance activation—read the committed batch timestamp. Oracle observations arrive as signed ordered activities; execution never fetches an external HTTP response.

title: Programs share the accounting boundary
content: Module 0x09 executes deterministic WASM programs under the invoking activity’s authority. Program-owned accounts derive from public program identifiers and seeds. Derivation alone grants no debit authority. Nested spending grants narrow the permitted source, destination, asset, and amount. Program monetary effects pass through the same transfer-set entry as other modules, and persisted namespace occupancy is metered and settled as replayable transfer legs.

title: Receipts and replay
content: A lxp_receipt binds the activity identifier, global sequence, previous and resulting state roots, activity root, result code, effects, fee charged, batch identifier, and module and parameter versions. Program outcomes additionally bind terminal results, runtime and ABI versions, resource metering, transfer evidence, and call-graph commitments. Clients supply activities; the protocol produces receipt evidence. Replicas replay the append-only history using its committed parameters. A root or receipt disagreement stops acceptance of that replay. Portable layerx-receipt-proof-v2 evidence lets a verifier authenticate a receipt against independently trusted batch facts. A receipt proves execution at its declared evidence level; it does not by itself prove settlement.

title: Native integration surfaces
content: The native interface exposes lxp_kernel_execute_activity and lxp_kernel_dispatch . Prepared-batch APIs separate preparation, commit, and publication; batch-boundary and publication-digest interfaces bind the records being published. Protocol-3 batch maintenance runs escrow deadlines, budget rollover, service defaults, and occupancy finalization within the batch journal. There is no lxp_kernel_replay entry point in the native interface.

title: Application workflow
content: Build the canonical activity using the correct network, authority, next sequence, fee limit, and validity bounds. Sign once and retain the exact bytes and idempotency key for retry and recovery. Submit with the evidence level required by the business operation. Verify receipt identity, result, fees, effects, and state-root binding. Require matching batch evidence before releasing a resource that needs settled assurance.

title: Continue reading
content: Sequencing, checkpoints, and finality Programmable execution Identity and delegated authority Payments and accounting Receipt verification

title: Payment mandates and trusted agents
content: Authorize direct and autonomous purchases with signed AP2 mandates, exact asset bindings, and trusted-agent request verification. Authorize direct and autonomous purchases with signed AP2 mandates, exact asset bindings, and trusted-agent request verification.

title: Separate the agent, the authorization, and the payment
content: Paxeer X verifies who presents a commerce request, what the payer authorizes, and what payment executes. Visa Trusted Agent Protocol supplies signed agent credentials and intent tags. AP2 supplies signed mandate constraints and checkout bindings. The LayerX payment plane executes the resulting typed intent and returns settlement evidence. Each step retains its own verification boundary.

title: AP2 v1 mandate verification
content: The AP2 adapter verifies SD-JWT and JOSE mandate material and evaluates its constraints before preparing payment. Direct mode handles direct authorization; autonomous mode evaluates delegated purchasing authorization, including the applicable line-item constraints. Verification binds payment and checkout identities, merchant details, amount, currency, payment instrument, audience, nonce, and validity conditions. Verification input Purpose now and clock_skew_seconds Evaluate validity windows with an explicit clock and permitted skew. expected_audience Require the mandate to target the expected audience. expected_nonce Bind verification to the expected authorization context. currency_minor_exponent Interpret the payment currency at its correct minor-unit precision. usage Evaluate an open mandate against durable prior-use facts.

title: Bounded autonomous authorization
content: For an open payment mandate, retain a usage record with its exact mandate reference, frequency, previous occurrence count, amount already spent in minor units, and next eligible execution time. The reference is the AP2 sd_hash of that specific mandate, preventing usage facts from being applied to a different authorization. Supply these facts explicitly when verifying the next purchase. The verification context requires a positive timestamp, nonempty audience and nonce, a currency minor exponent no greater than 18, and clock skew no greater than 3,600 seconds. These are verifier input bounds enforced before constraint evaluation; the mandate still has to pass its signed constraints. The adapter profile is AP2 v1 ( ap2-v1-signature-constraint-receipt-verified ).

title: Bind authorization to actual settlement
content: A verified mandate becomes an authorized payment only after its merchant and currency match the configured LayerX asset binding. The binding identifies the asset, payer and payee receipt accounts, minor-unit exponent, and atomic units per currency minor unit. Amount conversion uses checked multiplication and rejects overflow or a zero result. asset atomic amount = mandate minor units × atomic units per minor unit idempotency identity = principal + stable payment reference request binding = mandate material + currency + asset + payer account + payee account + amount + execution time The idempotency identity remains stable across retries of the same principal and payment reference. The request digest commits to the authorization material and settlement binding, preserving the relationship between the requested purchase and the executed payment.

title: Verify and execute
content: HTTP route Operation POST /v1/http/ap2/mandates/verify Verify signed mandate material and its constraint context. POST /v1/http/ap2/execute Map the authorized purchase to typed payment execution and signed evidence. POST /v1/http/visa-tap/intents/verify Verify a trusted-agent request. POST /v1/http/visa-tap/intents/execute Hand the trusted commerce intent to the LayerX authority path. Resolve the signing keys and verify the signed AP2 mandate pair against the explicit verification context. Evaluate merchant, amount, checkout, and autonomous-use constraints. Apply the configured asset and receipt-account binding. Execute through the LayerX intent plane using the derived idempotency identity and request digest. Verify execution evidence and sign the AP2 payment and checkout receipt evidence.

title: Visa Trusted Agent Protocol
content: The TAP adapter verifies RFC 9421-style sig2 request signatures against a trusted-agent registry. The agent-browser-auth tag identifies browsing intent and agent-payer-auth identifies payment intent. Verification checks the validity window, registered key status, signature algorithm, signed request target, cryptographic signature, and nonce uniqueness.

title: Replay protection and credential binding
content: A nonce window consumes the nonce together with its key identifier and expiry. A verified credential can be associated with a LayerX agent through the credential-binding store. That association records identity context; payment authority still passes through the typed intent authority path. A valid agent signature does not by itself supply the payer's mandate or authorize an arbitrary transfer. Maintain the registry's key status and validity information, use canonical authority and path representations for signature verification, and preserve nonce state across the merchant request lifecycle. Browse and pay operations retain distinct intent tags so an operation is evaluated in its declared context.

title: Portable purchase evidence
content: AP2 execution returns signed evidence containing portable LayerX receipt evidence. Payment and checkout receipt references preserve the exact verified authorization bindings. The portable mandate-pair format carries the external evidence needed by Ap2ExternalMandateVerifier , allowing verification to travel with the purchase evidence. Retain the signed mandate pair, canonical execution receipt, authorized batch, merchant checkout identity, and mandate usage facts as the appropriate records for the transaction. Keep raw payment credentials out of operational logs. Use agent commerce to connect this authorization flow to merchant checkout, order reads, and paid-resource fulfillment.

title: Market Makers
content: Provide exchange liquidity and operate independent asset ramps with bound quotes, authorized payments, durable reconciliation, and receipt-gated settlement. Provide exchange liquidity and operate independent asset ramps with bound quotes, authorized payments, durable reconciliation, and receipt-gated settlement.

title: Two liquidity workflows
content: Paxeer X supports market makers as ordinary LayerX principals. On exchange books, a maker posts resting bids and asks and manages the inventory committed to those orders. An independent ramp operator quotes conversions between LayerX assets and an external payment or payout system. Exchange orders and ramp orders have distinct execution and custody models. Workflow Inventory Execution evidence Spot quoting Base or quote units escrowed for resting orders Matching result and asset settlement receipt On-ramp Operator LayerX assets and external funds External settlement followed by verified LayerX delivery Off-ramp Customer-authorized LayerX payment and operator external payout inventory Verified LayerX payment followed by external payout settlement

title: Quote exchange liquidity
content: Create separate order identifiers for each quote, size bids against quote-asset inventory and asks against base-asset inventory, and submit limit GTC orders to the spot book . Matching uses best price and time priority; fills execute at the resting order's price. Update exposure from verified fills and residual order state. Before repricing, cancel the old order and reconcile the result. Maintain separate records for free inventory, inventory reserved by resting quotes, and completed trades. Market halts stop new placement; an agent's quoting policy should inspect market state and stop replacement submissions while a market is halted.

title: Independent ramp custody
content: The ramp toolkit binds a customer, operator, quote, and authorization into one order. The operator controls off-platform funds and payout. Show the toolkit's custody disclosure wherever the customer reviews or tracks a ramp: External custody: this independent market maker controls the off-platform funds and payout. The LayerX receipt proves the LayerX payment leg. External payment settlement comes from the provider's evidence and remains a separate obligation. A complete ramp order reconciles both.

title: Bind the quote
content: Terms Purpose quote_id , direction, expiry Identify the offer, on-ramp or off-ramp flow, and validity window LayerX asset and amount Bind the exact on-platform inventory movement External currency and minor-unit amount Bind the external payment amount without floating-point ambiguity Rate numerator and denominator, fee, maximum slippage Make the conversion terms explicit Context, provider token, payout token Bind the intended payment context and provider operation RampOrder::bind validates the quote and customer/operator identities, matches the requested quote identifier, and computes an order digest. Customers and operators use the AgentMain account namespace. On-ramp orders use operator authorization; off-ramp orders require a payer grant. The digest commits to the quote, principals, operator signing-key handle, context, and authorization reference. RampOrder::bind(request, quote, customer, operator, now) -> order_digest On-ramp: external provider settles -> operator sends LayerX asset -> verify receipt Off-ramp: customer payer grant -> verify LayerX payment -> external provider settles This is the toolkit workflow, not an HTTP endpoint. Integrate through the toolkit's typed clients and your provider's actual contract.

title: Execute an on-ramp
content: Authenticate the customer and obtain a valid quote with exact LayerX and external amounts. Bind and journal the order, then complete the compliance decision and external collection workflow. Reconcile external provider settlement before preparing the LayerX delivery. Use compile_operator_send(order) , which takes only the bound order and returns a LedgerCall to LEDGER_ADDRESS carrying encode_pay_exact(..., order_digest) . It refuses orders that are not operator-funded on-ramps without a payer grant. Retain the canonical activity before submission. Resolve pending or unknown submissions by activity identifier. Verify the receipt against the authorized batch and bound order; mark the workflow done after verified delivery.

title: Execute an off-ramp
content: Bind the customer's quote and payer-grant identifier into the order. Use compile_customer_payment(order) to construct the authorized customer-to-operator payment: a budget spend to PAY_ADDRESS . compile_payer_grant_draw(order, _receiver_sequence) is a compatibility shim that delegates to it and never uses the retired ledger draw selector. Verify the LayerX payment receipt before initiating the provider payout. Reconcile the provider operation or authenticated callback and retain its evidence digest. Complete the order after the external payout settles. Surface refusal, reversal, or manual review as distinct outcomes.

title: Verify payment evidence
content: verify_order_receipt checks canonical receipt evidence against the authorized batch and the expected asset-module operation. It binds the activity identifier, sender, receiver, asset, amount, and context to the order. On success it returns a VerifiedLayerxLeg with tx_hash , receipt_digest , height , and rung , derived from the sequencer signature and log binding. A provider callback is verified against the bound order and provider public key before it changes the journal. Callback identifiers and provider sequence numbers support replay handling. Keep the order digest, activity identifier, receipt digest, and provider evidence digest together in the customer's operational record.

title: Durability and recovery
content: The journal uses the domain LXP/market-maker-ramp/journal/v2 ; LXP/market-maker-ramp/journal/v1 is retained only as the legacy domain for migration. Worker leases coordinate order progression. The engine records the canonical planned activity before broadcasting, so recovery can resolve its result without inventing a fresh payment. Unknown submission status remains unknown until reconciled. Customer status Operational meaning Pending A payment or payout is progressing Unknown Submission outcome requires lookup and reconciliation Refused A leg refuses; retain the refusal code Manual review The provider requires an operator decision Reversed The provider reports a reversal Done The direction-specific settlement gates are satisfied

title: Rebalance Paxeer inventory
content: InventoryRebalancer journals custody transfers under an idempotency key and reconciles the retained operation identifier and transaction hash. Reusing a key with different asset or amount terms returns a conflict. A finality tracker polls the Paxeer transaction and records block identity and confirmations; a broadcast hash alone does not release inventory for a completed strategy cycle.

title: Integration map
content: The toolkit lives at services/platform/ramps/toolkit and exposes clients , engine , evm , journal , and migration modules. Use QuoteTerms and RampOrder for order binding, the compilation helpers for authorized payment construction, verify_order_receipt for payment verification, and RampPresentation for customer-facing status. Continue with Spot Exchange , EVM Precompiles , and LayerX Modules . Protocol references: services/platform/ramps/toolkit/src/lib.rs , services/platform/ramps/toolkit/src/engine.rs , services/platform/ramps/toolkit/src/journal.rs , and include/layerx/lx_spot.h .

title: MCP tools
content: Connect assistants to verified Paxeer X state and policy-governed wallet and token operations through 22 scoped MCP tools. Connect assistants to verified Paxeer X state and policy-governed wallet and token operations through 22 scoped MCP tools.

title: One governed execution path
content: layerx-mcp exposes a 22-tool catalogue to MCP clients. Every invocation passes through layerx-agentd as a DaemonInvocation , with Policy, Capability, Budget, RateLimit, and Audit gates, except faucet.request , which has no daemon operation and executes directly against the node (below). The same authorization and submission rules apply when an assistant uses a tool as when an application calls the daemon. A read-only deployment exposes read tools and omits writes. Tool discovery is filtered to the scopes bound to the caller, so an unavailable scope does not appear as an actionable tool.

title: Tool catalog
content: Tool Kind Required scope Daemon operation Purpose tenant.readiness read read TenantReadiness Read daemon-local readiness; the evidence is explicitly unverified protocol state. balance.get read read:balance ReadBalance Read verified program-scoped balances from the daemon with their verification level and freshness. history.list read read:history ReadHistory Page verified account history from the daemon under an explicit item bound and stable cursor. receipt.get read read:receipt ProgramReceipt Read the canonical receipt the daemon holds for one activity. checkpoint.get read read:checkpoint ReadCheckpoint Read the finalised checkpoint certificate for one batch sequence through the daemon. proof.get read read:proof ReadProofBundle Read the proof bundle the daemon holds for one activity. availability.get read read:availability AvailabilityFetch Read verified availability chunks and attributed failures for one decimal batch number. wallet.accounts read read:wallet:accounts ReadAccount List the verified accounts the daemon observes for one program. wallet.balance read read:wallet:balance ReadBalance Read one verified account balance for one asset through the daemon. activity.prepare write write:prepare Prepare Prepare canonical activity bytes and their bound disclosure inside the daemon. activity.disclose write write:disclose Prepare Decode the bound disclosure of canonical activity bytes. activity.sign write write:sign Sign Sign a daemon preparation at the daemon's external signing boundary; no key material is read. activity.submit write write:submit Submit Submit an externally signed preparation through the ordinary daemon path. activity.track write write:track Track Resolve the daemon's current state for one submission. activity.wait write write:activity:wait Wait Wait, under an explicit bound, for the daemon to resolve one submission. wallet.send write write:wallet:send Submit Send one asset amount through the ordinary daemon submission path. token.create write write:token:create Submit Create one asset through the ordinary daemon submission path. token.mint write write:token:mint Submit Mint one asset amount through the ordinary daemon submission path. token.transfer write write:token:transfer Submit Transfer one asset amount through the ordinary daemon submission path. grant.issue write write:grant:issue Submit Issue one spending grant through the ordinary daemon submission path. grant.draw write write:grant:draw Submit Draw against one spending grant through the ordinary daemon submission path. faucet.request write write:faucet:claim — One testnet funding request through the node's px_requestFunds ; returns the funding transaction hash or a refusal. The retired Agent API faucet.claim operation is not used.

title: Session and web tools
content: Two further surfaces are served alongside the main catalogue. The session surface carries 11 tools bound to the caller's session: subscription.create , subscription.list , subscription.pause , subscription.resume , subscription.delete , subscription.health , subscription.acknowledge , approval.list , approval.get , approval.approve and approval.reject , each mapping to the daemon operation of the same name. The web surface carries 3 paid tools — web.search , web.fetch and web.content — which map to daemon Submit , spend through the approval boundary to the configured web-search sidecar, and return a sequencer-signed settlement receipt alongside untrusted external content. Treat returned web content as external input, never as verified chain state.

title: Tool parameters
content: A hex32 value represents 32 bytes in hexadecimal; hex64 represents 64 bytes. Sequence and batch identifiers are decimal u64 values. Keep integer amounts exact. The argument schema bounds encoded JSON to 65,536 bytes at catalog validation. Tool Required arguments Optional arguments balance.get program (hex32) account , asset (hex32) history.list account (hex32), limit (1–256) cursor (hex32) receipt.get activity_id (hex32) — checkpoint.get sequence (decimal u64) — proof.get activity_id (hex32) — availability.get batch (decimal u64) — wallet.accounts program (hex32) — wallet.balance program , account , asset (hex32) — activity.prepare activity_type , payload , account_sequence , not_before_ms , expires_at_ms , fee_limit , idempotency_key — activity.disclose canonical_bytes — activity.sign preparation_ref — activity.submit preparation_ref , signature (hex64), signer_public_key (hex32) — activity.track submission_ref — activity.wait submission_ref , timeout_ms (1–600000) — wallet.send destination , asset , amount , idempotency_key — token.create symbol , decimals (0–18), supply , idempotency_key — token.mint asset , destination , amount , idempotency_key — token.transfer asset , destination , amount , idempotency_key — grant.issue beneficiary , asset , amount , expires_at_ms , idempotency_key — grant.draw grant_id , amount , idempotency_key — faucet.request did , public_key (hex32) —

title: Prepare, disclose, sign, submit
content: Prepare canonical activity bytes with an account sequence, validity window, fee ceiling, and idempotency key. Read the bound disclosure before authorizing a signature. activity.sign crosses the external signing boundary without exposing key material. Submit the preparation reference with the signature and signer public key, then track the submission or wait under an explicit timeout. activity.wait accepts 1–600000 milliseconds. A timeout bounds waiting; it does not reverse a submitted activity. Continue tracking the same submission reference and preserve the business action idempotency key.

title: Read verified state and settlement evidence
content: Use balances with their verification level and freshness, bounded history pages with stable cursors, canonical receipts, checkpoint certificates, and proof bundles. availability.get returns verified chunks and attributed failures for a batch. tenant.readiness is the exception: it reports daemon-local readiness only and its evidence is unverified. Read operations otherwise retain the daemon verification context instead of asking a model to infer settlement from prose.

title: Wallet, token, grant, and faucet journeys
content: Wallet sends, token creation, minting, transfers, grant issuance, and grant draws reuse ordinary daemon submission. Token decimals are bounded to 0–18. A grant binds beneficiary, asset, amount, and expiry; a draw names the grant and amount. Faucet requests bind the DID and public key and execute as one px_requestFunds call against the node. Integrate tools alongside XDK and SDK quickstarts . Inspect Agent API for canonical write semantics and the agent daemon for its execution boundary.

title: Ethereum & Solana Mirrors
content: Publish Paxeer X batch archives to external chains and verify committed receipt evidence independently of a hosted gateway. Publish Paxeer X batch archives to external chains and verify committed receipt evidence independently of a hosted gateway.

title: External access to canonical evidence
content: The mirror system builds committed batch archives, publishes them to Ethereum or Solana, and retrieves them through independently configured chain sources. A consumer can then verify an archived receipt under its own sequencer key configuration without contacting the Paxeer X gateway. Mirror publication distributes evidence. Paxeer custody and settlement remain governed by their own checkpoint authority and contracts. An external chain's publication confirmation alone does not authorize a Paxeer withdrawal.

title: Publisher and verifier roles
content: Component Responsibility layerx-mirror-publisher Acquire committed node data, construct archives, publish to configured targets and track durable progress layerx-mirror-verify Read configured mirror sources and verify a committed archive or one archived receipt MirrorVerifier Admit a committed archive, return its committed coordinate, and verify a receipt by index under configured sequencer keys PublicationJournal and archive spool Preserve publication phases and exact archive material through restart

title: Trust configuration
content: The verifier configuration carries layerx_network_id , a receipt_keys list, and a sources list. Each receipt key pins sequencer_id_hex , public_key_hex , and the first_height / last_height window in which that key authorizes receipts. This trust material is configured independently of archive payloads; an archive cannot authorize its own signing key or extend its height window. A configuration with no receipt keys is refused. Source Identity pins Ethereum RPC quorum, chain ID, genesis hash, archive contract, archive code hash and publisher identity Solana RPC quorum, genesis hash, archive program, upgradeable loader, program-data account, program code hash and publisher identity Retain target-chain identity and canonical position with each observation. On Ethereum this includes the observed block and reference head; on Solana it includes the rooted slot and block hash.

title: Publish an archive
content: layerx-mirror-publisher /etc/layerx/mirror-publisher.json layerx-mirror-publisher --probe 127.0.0.1:<status-port> The second form probes the publisher's status listener for readiness instead of starting the service. Any other argument shape exits with a usage error. Read committed blocks from the configured Paxeer source, starting at the configured first height. Build and validate the archive, preserving its exact canonical bytes and content commitment. Persist publication intent, obtain target-chain signatures and broadcast. Observe configured chain confirmation or rooting, retrieve the published archive and verify the bytes. Advance the durable publication cursor only through the recorded publication workflow. Publisher configuration includes the state directory, first height, polling interval, checkpoint freshness budget in blocks, status listener address, and the Paxeer committed-source section. The Ethereum target is configured explicitly; the Solana section is optional and validated when present.

title: Recover publication safely
content: The publication journal distinguishes prepared, pre-broadcast failure, signed, broadcast-unknown, pending, finalized, and retrieved-verified states, alongside permanent refusal, reorganization, and expired broadcast. When broadcast status is unknown, resolve chain history before issuing a replacement nonce or blockhash. Readiness includes checkpoint freshness against the configured block budget. A healthy process and a completed historical publication do not by themselves establish that every target is current.

title: Read policies
content: Policy Behavior Use exact Read one source locator and commitment Audit a specific publication ordered-preference Use an explicit ordered candidate set Controlled source failover agreement Require a configured minimum agreement among candidates Cross-source corroboration A candidate identifies the configured source index and exact archive commitment. Source divergence, insufficient agreement, missing data, RPC divergence and rate limits remain distinct outcomes.

title: Verify from a mirror
content: Prepare a verifier configuration with your independent network and source pins, then supply a JSON request on standard input. A receipt request names the archived receipt by its index within the batch. Replace the commitment placeholder with the 32-byte archive commitment: { "batch_number": "12", "evidence": { "kind": "receipt", "index": 0 }, "policy": { "kind": "exact", "candidate": { "source": 0, "commitment_hex": "REPLACE_WITH_32_BYTE_ARCHIVE_COMMITMENT_HEX" } } } layerx-mirror-verify /etc/layerx/mirror-verifier.json < receipt-request.json The verifier fetches the archive from the pinned source, checks its commitment and batch, and verifies the sequencer signature over the archived receipt bytes against the receipt key whose height window covers the batch. It does not take receipt bytes from the caller: a request carrying fields such as canonical_hex is refused, because unknown request members are denied. There is no state-proof request in this command; the only other evidence kind is committed , which verifies the archive's committed coordinate without selecting a receipt. Batch numbers are nonzero canonical decimal strings without leading zeros. Receipt indices at or above 1,048,576 are out of bounds, and the request body is capped at 40 MiB.

title: Interpret the result
content: On success the verifier prints { "ok": true, "verification": { ... } } . The verification object contains level , evidenceDigest , sourceId , target , canonicalPosition , provenance , latestBatch , batchLag , failoverCount , agreeingSources , committedHeight , and committedBlockHash . Failures print ok: false with an error code. The only evidence level is Committed : the archive was admitted under the pinned source commitment and, for a receipt request, the receipt's sequencer signature verified. The report carries no checkpoint level and no signed-header digest. Freshness is reported separately through latestBatch and batchLag and can be unknown. Store the observation and trust configuration with the evidence so later readers can distinguish historical validity from current coverage.

title: Library verifier
content: In Rust, MirrorVerifier::from_committed_source or admit_committed admits archive bytes against an observation, refusing a mismatched source commitment or batch. committed() returns the committed height and block hash retained in the archive. committed_receipt(index, keys) verifies one archived receipt under the supplied sequencer height-range keys. Admission of a committed archive does not require a signed batch header, and this verifier surface does not establish native checkpoint assurance; applications requiring that assurance must obtain it through the checkpoint path, not from a mirror report or external-chain finality.

title: Archive retention and audit
content: Keep the archive commitment, canonical archive bytes, trusted sequencer key windows, target identity, canonical chain position and evidence verification result together. For settlement audits retain native certificates and independently authorized checkpoint policy as well. Continue with Relay & Archive Nodes for public history endpoints, Receipts & Proofs for portable verification, and Data Availability for authenticated replay bundles.

title: Epoch Module
content: Time-based hooks and epoch lifecycle management for coordinating periodic chain operations. Time-based hooks and epoch lifecycle management for coordinating periodic chain operations. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/epoch/

title: Overview
content: The epoch module manages fixed time periods (epochs) and triggers registered hooks when an epoch ends and the next begins. An epoch defaults to 60 seconds ( time.Minute in genesis). Hooks run during BeginBlock . In this codebase only one hook consumer is wired in node/app.go : the mint keeper. Validator-set updates, parameter activation, and periodic cleanup are not epoch-hook consumers here.

title: State
content: The epoch module maintains a single state object: > paxd q epoch epoch --output json { "epoch": { "genesis_time": "2023-04-27T19:08:11.958027Z", "epoch_duration": "60s", "current_epoch": "0", "current_epoch_start_time": "2023-04-27T19:08:11.958027Z", "current_epoch_height": "0" } } genesis_time: Chain genesis time (fixed) epoch_duration: Duration of each epoch (default 60s) current_epoch: Current epoch number (increments at each epoch boundary) current_epoch_start_time: Timestamp when the current epoch started current_epoch_height: Block height at which the current epoch started

title: Epoch Boundaries
content: Epochs are defined by wall-clock time, not block height. In BeginBlock ( modules/epoch/keeper/abci.go ) a new epoch begins only when the block time is strictly after the boundary: if ctx.BlockTime().Sub(lastEpoch.CurrentEpochStartTime) > lastEpoch.EpochDuration { // advance exactly one epoch } The comparison is strict ( > ), not ≥ . It is a single if , not a loop: at most one epoch advance per block, even after a long halt. The new start time is oldStart + epoch_duration , not the current block time, so the schedule does not drift to block time.

title: Hooks
content: Other modules implement the EpochHooks interface ( modules/epoch/types/hooks.go ): type EpochHooks interface { AfterEpochEnd(ctx sdk.Context, epoch Epoch) BeforeEpochStart(ctx sdk.Context, epoch Epoch) } At a boundary the keeper runs them in this order: AfterEpochEnd(ctx, lastEpoch) — for the epoch that is ending SetEpoch(newEpoch) — store the incremented epoch BeforeEpochStart(ctx, newEpoch) — for the epoch that is starting Emit the new_epoch event Each hook runs in a cached context ( ctx.CacheContext() ). Its writes are committed only if the hook completes; a hook panic is re-raised and aborts the block rather than advancing the epoch without the hook's state transition.

title: Example: Mint Module
content: The mint module ( modules/mint/keeper/hooks.go ) implements epoch hooks: BeforeEpochStart is a no-op and AfterEpochEnd performs the daily release check. It is the only hook registered in node/app.go : app.EpochKeeper = *epochmodulekeeper.NewKeeper( appCodec, keys[epochmoduletypes.StoreKey], keys[epochmoduletypes.MemStoreKey], app.GetSubspace(epochmoduletypes.ModuleName), ).SetHooks(epochmoduletypes.NewMultiEpochHooks( app.MintKeeper.Hooks()))

title: Events
content: The epoch module emits a new_epoch event at each epoch boundary: epoch_number: The new epoch's epoch number epoch_time: The new epoch's start time epoch_height: The block height at which the new epoch started

title: Messages
content: The epoch module does not expose any transactions. Its handler rejects every message as unrecognized. Only the module itself updates epoch state during BeginBlock .

title: Parameters
content: The epoch module has no runtime parameters: Params is empty and validation rejects any non-empty value. The epoch duration lives in the epoch genesis state.

title: Use Cases
content: Mint module: The only wired consumer; its AfterEpochEnd hook checks whether a daily release is due. See Mint module

title: Next Steps
content: Understand how the mint module uses epochs Review all Paxeer modules Previous Modules Overview Next Mint Module

title: Mint Module
content: Scheduled native token release: a fixed amount minted daily through the epoch hook, under governance-controlled schedules. Scheduled native token release: a fixed amount minted daily through the epoch hook, under governance-controlled schedules. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/mint/

title: Overview
content: The mint module creates new native tokens according to a predefined schedule: a total_mint_amount released between a start date and an end date. There is no block-by-block inflation rate. Minting is driven only by the epoch module's AfterEpochEnd hook and releases at most once per UTC date.

title: Minting Mechanism
content: On each epoch end, the hook ( modules/mint/keeper/hooks.go ) loads or updates the current minter from the release schedule, then computes today's release from the ending epoch's start time — not the current block time: coinsToMint := latestMinter.GetReleaseAmountToday(epoch.CurrentEpochStartTime.UTC()) GetReleaseAmountToday ( modules/mint/types/minter.go ) applies these rules, in order: Before the start date, or if a mint already happened on that UTC date ( last_mint_date matches): release 0 Past the end date, or with zero days left: release all of remaining_mint_amount Otherwise: release remaining_mint_amount / days_between(today, end_date) (integer division) If the amount is zero or nothing remains, the hook returns without minting. Otherwise it mints the coins ( MintCoins ), sends them to the fee_collector account ( AddCollectedFees ), and records the mint: remaining_mint_amount decreases and last_mint_amount , last_mint_date , and last_mint_height are updated. The distribution module then handles collected fees as usual.

title: Example
content: If total_mint_amount = 1,000,000 tokens and the period is 100 days: Initial daily mint: 1,000,000 / 100 = 10,000 tokens/day After 50 days: 500,000 remaining / 50 days = 10,000 tokens/day (unchanged if no downtime) If the chain was down for 1 day at day 50: 500,000 remaining / 49 days = 10,204 tokens/day (adjusted) If the chain is still down past the end date, the first epoch end after recovery releases the entire remainder at once (rule 2)

title: Minter
content: The minter stores current release state. Dates use the yyyy-mm-dd format: type Minter struct { StartDate string // The day where the mint begins EndDate string // The day where the mint ends Denom string // Must equal the bond denom (uhpx) TotalMintAmount uint64 // Total amount to be minted RemainingMintAmount uint64 // Remaining amount to be minted LastMintAmount uint64 // Last amount minted (usually from the day before) LastMintDate string // Last day minted LastMintHeight uint64 // The height of the last mint } The denom is not a free choice: validation requires both the minter denom and Params.MintDenom to equal the default bond denom, uhpx . Query the current minter and parameters: paxd q mint minter paxd q mint params

title: Params
content: Parameters define the release schedules the minter is derived from: type Params struct { MintDenom string // Type of coin to mint (must be uhpx) TokenReleaseSchedule []ScheduledTokenRelease // List of token release schedules } type ScheduledTokenRelease struct { StartDate string // The day where the mint begins EndDate string // The day where the mint ends TokenReleaseAmount uint64 // Total amount to be minted } Multiple release schedules can be defined, allowing sequential minting periods.

title: Epoch Hook
content: The mint module has no begin-block minting logic of its own. Its BeforeEpochStart hook is a no-op; all minting happens in AfterEpochEnd as described above. Because epochs default to 60s, the hook runs frequently, but the same-date check limits actual mints to one per UTC date. See the Epoch module for how boundaries are detected.

title: Update Minter Proposal
content: The minter can be replaced via governance to change the mint schedule. The proposal is stored verbatim after validation ( HandleUpdateMinterProposal calls ValidateMinter then SetMinter ), so every field must be set explicitly. In particular: remaining_mint_amount is not derived from total_mint_amount . Setting it to 0 means no ongoing release and no further mints last_mint_date must be a parseable yyyy-mm-dd date; an empty string fails validation. A fresh minter uses 0001-01-01 denom must be uhpx , and last_mint_amount must not exceed total_mint_amount - remaining_mint_amount { "title": "Update Minter", "description": "Adjust mint schedule", "minter": { "start_date": "2023-10-05", "end_date": "2023-11-22", "denom": "uhpx", "total_mint_amount": "100000", "remaining_mint_amount": "100000", "last_mint_amount": "0", "last_mint_date": "0001-01-01", "last_mint_height": "0" } } Submit the proposal: paxd tx gov submit-proposal update-minter ./minter_prop.json \ --deposit 20pax --from admin -b block -y \ --gas 200000 --fees 2000uhpx After the proposal passes, paxd q mint minter returns exactly the stored minter above until the next daily release updates it.

title: Update Params Proposal
content: Parameters can be updated to define new token release schedules: { "title": "Param Change Proposal", "description": "Update token release schedule", "changes": [ { "subspace": "mint", "key": "MintDenom", "value": "uhpx" }, { "subspace": "mint", "key": "TokenReleaseSchedule", "value": [ { "token_release_amount": 500, "start_date": "2023-10-01", "end_date": "2023-10-30" }, { "token_release_amount": 1000, "start_date": "2023-11-01", "end_date": "2023-11-30" } ] } ] } Submit: paxd tx gov submit-proposal param-change ./param_change_prop.json \ --from admin -b block -y --gas 200000 --fees 200000uhpx Note: Changes to total_mint_amount or remaining_mint_amount after the start date do not affect tokens already minted.

title: Mint Event
content: Emitted on each successful mint: mint_date: Date of the mint mint_epoch: Epoch number when the mint occurred amount: Amount minted

title: Metrics
content: Each successful mint records two gauges: the OpenTelemetry gauge mint_coins_minted{denom} and the legacy telemetry gauge pax/mint/coins (exported as pax_mint_coins{denom} ).

title: Oracle Module
content: Navigate the retired EVM Oracle API and the native interfaces for exchange rates, voting parameters, and price observations. Navigate the retired EVM Oracle API and the native interfaces for exchange rates, voting parameters, and price observations. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/precompiles/oracle/oracle.go , modules/oracle/ , node/wasmbinding/queries.go , and node/app.go .

title: EVM price queries are retired
content: The Oracle precompile remains registered at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001008 , but both getExchangeRates and getOracleTwaps revert with: oracle precompile is retired; oracle data queries are disabled For EVM applications, choose an active price-data integration for your network and configure its asset identifiers, units, and freshness checks.

title: Native Oracle interfaces
content: The native Oracle module handles validator voting, aggregation, and queries. It also provides the keeper used by CosmWasm Oracle query plugins. Component Function modules/oracle/handler.go Feed-consent delegation and aggregate exchange-rate vote messages. modules/oracle/abci.go MidBlocker : vote-period ballot aggregation, exchange-rate updates, and slash-window penalty processing. modules/oracle/keeper/ Stored rates, vote targets, validator voting state, parameters, and query services. modules/oracle/client/cli/query.go Native exchange-rate, actives, snapshot-history, TWAP, parameter, feeder, and vote-penalty queries. node/wasmbinding/queries.go HandleOracleQuery : native exchange_rates and oracle_twaps custom-query handlers. Query current vote targets and observations to identify the denominations available on your network. Check observation timestamps before using a rate in application logic.

title: Aggregation and parameters
content: Aggregation runs in the module's mid-blocker ( MidBlock in modules/oracle/module.go ), not in begin- or end-block. At the last block of each vote period it builds voting claims from bonded validators, organizes ballots by configured vote targets, applies threshold checks, and derives exchange rates through weighted-median processing ( WeightedMedianWithAssertion for the reference denom, Tally with the reward band for cross rates). At the last block of each slash window it runs SlashAndResetCounters over the miss/abstain counters. Vote-period, reward-band, and slash-window behavior is controlled by module parameters. Read the live parameters and vote targets before interpreting a network's observations or validator obligations. Do not infer a fixed voting period, reward band, slash rate, or required asset list from an example or another network's settings.

title: Native query commands
content: These eight commands are registered by the native module. Point the CLI at the Cosmos RPC endpoint for the node you are inspecting: paxd query oracle params paxd query oracle vote-targets paxd query oracle actives paxd query oracle exchange-rates paxd query oracle exchange-rates "$DENOM" paxd query oracle price-snapshot-history paxd query oracle twaps "$LOOKBACK_SECONDS" paxd query oracle feeder "$VALIDATOR_ADDRESS" paxd query oracle vote-penalty-counter "$VALIDATOR_ADDRESS" The optional denomination belongs to exchange-rates ; there is no separate singular exchange-rate command in this CLI. Validator operator addresses use the paxvaloper prefix.

title: CosmWasm query boundary
content: The oracle custom-query route still calls the native module handler. A CosmWasm custom querier payload for retained exchange rates has this shape: { "route": "oracle", "query_data": { "exchange_rates": {} } } Issue this query from a CosmWasm contract through WASM bindings . Check the returned denominations and observation freshness before using the results.

title: Related interfaces
