title: Paxeer X Modules
content: Native execution, markets, issuance, and data modules in modules/, including retired settlement-compatibility directories. Native execution, markets, issuance, and data modules in modules/ , including retired settlement-compatibility directories. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/README.md

title: Unified Paxeer X modules
content: Paxeer X combines EVM and Cosmos execution with the LayerX kernel. The chain modules below enforce the chain-side rules; the LayerX kernel is part of the same network, and a receipt is final when its block is committed. Addresses below are shortened; see precompiles for full addresses and upgrade gates. Module Role in Paxeer X EVM entry point lxphost Shared cgo host for kernel validation and execution; also backs the layerxprograms precompile 0x101D layerxledger Asset registration, derived accounts, transfers, and exact payments. The old payer-grant issue, revoke, and draw operations are retired 0x101A layerxauth Capability and session grants, revocation, and SDK authorization integration 0x101C layerxpay Escrows, budgets, streams, and service agreements, subject to configured family enablement and pause gates 0x101B layerxagent Scheduled EVM calls, job deposits, and bounded end-block execution. Agent-function precompiles occupy 0x0901 – 0x0908 ; the scheduler is at 0x0905 0x0901 – 0x0908 layerxchains Tenant-domain registry, funding, allowances, operator controls, and lifecycle. Sub-chains are database namespaces on the same network 0x101E sequencer On-chain leader list, receipt keys, and sequence state used by block proposal and receipt machinery — layerxgov Governance proposal content ( LayerXProposal ) that dispatches packaged parameter and admin messages through the SDK MsgServiceRouter Governance proposals perps Native perpetuals markets and synchronous trading: orders, positions, and margin 0x1015 spot Native spot markets, orders, stop orders, quoters, and vaults — pricefeed Validator-signed index and mark price observations with mid-block aggregation — layerxbridge Attested transfers between Paxeer and external chains: chain registry, attestor set, per-asset caps, and bridgeIn / bridgeOut 0x1016 launchpad Native bonding-curve markets over tokenfactory denoms 0x1017 xweb Attested web data for EVM contracts and kernel programs; governance controls the attestor set, threshold, and pause state 0x1019 Explore the unified network , asset model , settlement lifecycle , and bridge . modules/README.md describes module ownership.

title: Retired settlement compatibility
content: These directories retain legacy types, historical state handling, and retirement checks. They do not provide a separate execution or settlement domain: Module Status EVM entry point layerxcustody Legacy custody registry and retirement handling. Deposits, proof-carrying withdrawals, forced exits, and deposit-root publication are retired. Fund derived sub-accounts through native bank sends; use layerxbridge for outward transfers 0x1013 layerxanchor Retired checkpoint and bond machinery. Use committed blocks for finality and committed application state with per-key proofs for state verification 0x1014 layerxexchange Retired exchange-intent submission and proof-based settlement machinery. Use the native perps module at 0x1015 for orders, positions, and margin 0x1015 (superseded by perps )

title: Module Overview
content: Paxeer X-specific chain modules live under Paxeer-X-Network/modules/ . These extend the Cosmos SDK with functionality unique to Paxeer X’s EVM L1 design. The pages in this section document epoch , mint , oracle , store , and tokenfactory in detail; the modules above are documented in their own sections or in modules/README.md .

title: Module List
content: Module Purpose evm Native EVM execution, address association, receipts, pointers, and precompile integration epoch Time-based hooks and epoch lifecycle management mint Scheduled native-token minting, released daily through the epoch hook oracle Validator exchange-rate voting and weighted-median price aggregation (native interfaces; the EVM precompile is retired) store Single cached-context helper; not a registered chain module tokenfactory Creation and admin management of native token denominations by any sender

title: Framework Modules
content: Framework-provided modules (bank, staking, distribution, governance, etc.) remain under sdk/x/ . Interchain application modules live under interchain/modules/ .

title: EVM Module
content: The evm module is Paxeer X’s core EVM execution layer: EVM execution: Runs Ethereum transactions with full opcode compatibility Address association: Maps Cosmos addresses to EVM addresses Receipts: Generates EVM transaction receipts Pointers: Bridging between Cosmos and EVM state Precompiles: Integration with Paxeer X-specific precompiled contracts See EVM documentation for details.

title: Epoch Module
content: The epoch module provides time-based lifecycle hooks: Epoch boundaries: Fixed time periods (60s by default) checked in BeginBlock Hooks: Registered modules run AfterEpochEnd / BeforeEpochStart callbacks at each boundary. Only the mint keeper is wired in node/app.go See Epoch documentation for details.

title: Mint Module
content: The mint module manages native token issuance: Release schedule: A total_mint_amount released between a start and end date Minting trigger: Only the epoch AfterEpochEnd hook, which mints at most once per day (UTC date) Destination: Newly minted coins are sent to the fee_collector account See Mint documentation for details.

title: Oracle Module
content: The oracle module enables validator-based price feeds on native interfaces: Exchange rate voting: Validators submit price observations for configured vote targets Aggregation: Weighted-median computation in the mid-blocker at the last block of each vote period Penalties: Miss/abstain counters are processed at each slash window; this is not a check on whether a submitted price was "bad data" EVM access: The oracle precompile at 0x…1008 is retired and reverts; use native or CosmWasm queries See Oracle documentation for details.

title: Store Module
content: modules/store/ is a single helper file, not a registered module: GetCachedContext : Returns a context backed by a CacheMultiStore plus the cache itself. It has no keeper, types, queries, or messages See Store documentation for details.

title: Token Factory Module
content: The tokenfactory module enables native token creation: Native denominations: Create new token types as factory/{creator}/{subdenom} Creation: MsgCreateDenom has no permission gate; any sender can create a denom and becomes its admin Management: The admin can mint (to itself), burn (from itself), change admin, update the allow list, set metadata, and pause/unpause the denom See Token Factory documentation for details.

title: Module Integration
content: Modules are registered in the application through node/app.go : Module manager: Coordinates module initialization and upgrades Begin/end block: Modules register hooks for block lifecycle Message routing: Module-specific transactions routed to handlers Query routing: Module-specific queries routed to keepers Previous Storage Next Epoch Module

title: Store Module
content: A single cached-context helper in modules/store/ — not a registered chain module. A single cached-context helper in modules/store/ — not a registered chain module. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/store/handler.go

title: Overview
content: modules/store/ contains exactly one file, handler.go (11 lines), exporting one function. It has no module.go , keeper, types, genesis, messages, or queries, and it is not registered in node/app.go . modules/README.md lists it only as "module-level store integration helpers".

title: GetCachedContext
content: package store import ( sdk "github.com/Sidiora-Labs/Paxeer-X-Network/sdk/types" ) func GetCachedContext(ctx sdk.Context) (sdk.Context, sdk.CacheMultiStore) { ms := ctx.MultiStore() msCache := ms.CacheMultiStore() return ctx.WithMultiStore(msCache), msCache } GetCachedContext wraps the context's multistore in a CacheMultiStore and returns both the derived context and the cache. Writes made through the derived context stay in the cache until the caller writes the cache through; discarding the cache discards the writes. This is the standard SDK pattern for speculative execution.

title: What it is not
content: No key-formatting or prefix constants, iterator utilities, or codec helpers are defined here. Modules define their own prefixes and call the SDK KVStore and codec directly. No state-migration utilities or test helpers (in-memory stores, mock contexts, snapshots) live in this package. It is not a layer over PaxDB storage ; module keepers access state through the SDK multistore without going through this package.

title: Next Steps
content: Understand PaxDB storage architecture Review other Paxeer modules Previous Oracle Module Next Token Factory Module

title: Token Factory Module
content: Creation and admin management of native token denominations with creator-namespaced denoms. Creation and admin management of native token denominations with creator-namespaced denoms. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/modules/tokenfactory/

title: Overview
content: The tokenfactory module allows any account to create new native tokens: MsgCreateDenom has no permission gate, allow list of creators, or governance check. Tokens are namespaced by creator address as factory/{creator address}/{subdenom} , eliminating name collisions. A single account can create multiple denoms by providing unique subdenoms. The creator becomes the denom's admin. The admin can mint, burn, change admin, update the denom allow list, set bank metadata, and pause or unpause the denom — subject to the sender restrictions below.

title: Token Naming
content: Tokenfactory denoms follow the format: factory/{creator_address}/{subdenom} Example: factory/pax166vhptur29s3gw5qr6dm30s06gej6pr4zevkqk/ufoo Prefix: Always factory (7 bytes) Creator address: Bech32 address (max 75 bytes) Subdenom: User-defined (max 44 bytes) The full denom must also pass the SDK denom validation, [a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9/-]{2,127} ( sdk/types/coin.go ). That means a subdenom containing . is rejected, while - and / are allowed characters in the full denom. Total denom length must not exceed 128 bytes.

title: CreateDenom
content: Create a new denom. Field 3 carries an optional bank allow list for the new denom: message MsgCreateDenom { string sender = 1; string subdenom = 2; AllowList allow_list = 3; // bank AllowList type } CLI: paxd tx tokenfactory create-denom ufoo --from mylocalwallet State modifications: Set DenomMetadata via bank keeper Set AuthorityMetadata with sender as admin Add denom to CreatorPrefixStore Creation fails if the subdenom equals an existing native denom or the resulting denom already has bank metadata.

title: Mint
content: Mint tokens (admin only). The minted coins go to the sender — there is no recipient field: message MsgMint { string sender = 1; cosmos.base.v1beta1.Coin amount = 2; } CLI: paxd tx tokenfactory mint 100000000000factory/pax166vh.../ufoo --from mylocalwallet Checks: the denom was created via tokenfactory, the sender is the admin, and the denom is not paused. The amount is minted via the bank module to the sender's account; distributing it further is a separate bank send.

title: Burn
content: Burn tokens (admin only). The coins are burned from the sender's own balance — the admin cannot burn from another account: message MsgBurn { string sender = 1; cosmos.base.v1beta1.Coin amount = 2; } Checks: the denom was created via tokenfactory, the sender is the admin, the denom is not paused, and the sender holds the amount. The amount is sent from the sender to the module account and burned via the bank module.

title: ChangeAdmin
content: Transfer admin privileges: message MsgChangeAdmin { string sender = 1; string denom = 2; string newAdmin = 3; } The sender must be the current admin, and newAdmin must differ from the current admin. ValidateBasic requires newAdmin to be a valid, non-empty bech32 address, so admin cannot be renounced by setting it to "" through this message; an empty admin can only exist in stored or genesis authority metadata.

title: UpdateDenom
content: Replace the denom's bank allow list: message MsgUpdateDenom { string sender = 1; string denom = 2; AllowList allow_list = 3; // bank AllowList type } paxd tx tokenfactory update-denom <denom> --from mylocalwallet The allow list must be defined, contain only valid bech32 addresses, and not exceed the denom_allowlist_max_size parameter (default 2000 ).

title: SetDenomMetadata
content: Set the denom's bank metadata from a file: paxd tx tokenfactory set-denom-metadata <metadata-file> --from mylocalwallet

title: SetDenomPaused
content: Pause or unpause a denom: paxd tx tokenfactory set-denom-paused <denom> true --from mylocalwallet While a denom is paused, tokenfactory mint and burn reject with ErrDenomPaused .

title: Admin Capabilities
content: The admin can: Mint: Create new tokens of the denom, credited to the admin itself Burn: Destroy tokens from the admin's own balance Change Admin: Transfer admin rights to another address Update allow list / metadata / pause: Via MsgUpdateDenom , MsgSetDenomMetadata , and MsgSetDenomPaused There is no force-transfer message in this module: the admin cannot move or burn tokens held by other accounts. Ordinary transfers use the bank module and require the holder's signature. Admins can share privileges via the authz module without changing the master admin.

title: Queries
content: paxd query tokenfactory params paxd query tokenfactory denom-authority-metadata <denom> paxd query tokenfactory denom-paused <denom> paxd query tokenfactory denoms-from-creator pax166vhptur29s3gw5qr6dm30s06gej6pr4zevkqk paxd query tokenfactory denom-metadata <denom> paxd query tokenfactory denom-allow-list <denom> paxd query bank denom-metadata --denom factory/pax166vh.../ufoo

title: Parameters
content: denom_allowlist_max_size : Maximum addresses in a denom allow list. Default 2000 ; changeable by governance

title: Restrictions
content: To fit within the 128-byte Cosmos SDK denom limit: Max subdenom length: 44 characters Max creator address length: 75 characters (bech32 prefix ≤ 16 chars) Calculation: len("factory") + 2*len("/") + len(creator_address) + len(subdenom) ≤ 128 7 + 2 + 75 + 44 = 128

title: Use Cases
content: Wrapped assets: Mint tokens representing off-chain assets Synthetic tokens: Create tokens backed by other on-chain assets Protocol-managed denoms: Modules create denoms for internal accounting Governance tokens: DAOs issue native governance tokens

title: Integration with Bank Module
content: Tokenfactory denoms are native tokens, not ERC-20 contracts. They integrate with the bank module for: Balance queries Transfers via MsgSend IBC transfers Distribution to stakers

title: Network operations
content: Operate the hosted Paxeer X service graph, qualify journeys, preserve durable state, and recover across service boundaries. Operate the hosted Paxeer X service graph, qualify journeys, preserve durable state, and recover across service boundaries. The hosted platform connects identity, Human workflows, gateway admission, protocol execution, verified receipt authority, program registration, settlement, and outbound events. Each service has a specific authority and persistence boundary. Operating the network means keeping those boundaries consistent through startup, release changes, maintenance, and recovery. The concrete control implementation in the monorepo is the hosted testnet control service ( services/platform/hosted/testnet/ ); readiness, journeys, and parameters below describe that service, not a generic production control plane.

title: Service architecture
content: Service boundary Responsibility Operational evidence Gateway Public protocol API admission and routing. Readiness, activity responses, and receipt lookup. Identity and Human Identity sessions, human journeys, approvals, and account-facing workflows. Identity readiness and durable journey or approval state. Node and core Ordered execution, canonical receipts, and authorized administrative operations. Node history, roots, receipts, and core journals. Receipt authority and replica Verify receipt inclusion and derive authorized batch facts. Pinned identities, signed headers, inclusion evidence, and derived roots. Registry and builder Program artifacts, registration, and release material. Artifact commitments, registry records, and compatible release versions. Paxeer and guarantors Custody, independent replay, checkpoint registration, and finality evidence. Settlement receipts, checkpoint events, and matching node evidence. Internal signing and event sources Non-exporting signing APIs and verified journey, payment, approval, and program events. Durable journals, principal binding, and event sequences. Control Dependency status, package and wire gates, and journey admission. Readiness document and explicit failing dependencies. The gateway provides the public protocol entry point. Human APIs and administrative services remain separate service boundaries. Private-network control tooling manages disposable environments; its funding and reset endpoints are not public production account APIs. Production account funding follows the custody-credit workflow.

title: Startup and release lifecycle
content: Validate the selected network and custody profile, release images, genesis inputs, and retained-material inventory. Provision trust material and persistent stores before services that consume them start. Start the Paxeer and trusted execution boundaries, then bootstrap node genesis and settlement bindings. Publish the resulting settlement contract addresses and canonical module registry. Start control, gateway, registry, and outbound-delivery services after their dependencies exist. Require compatible package and wire versions, dependency readiness, and admitted application journeys. Complete a real journey through execution and evidence inspection before promoting the release. Registry preparation compares published module identifiers and activity ordinals with the node's advertised preparation surface. An observer node uses the same genesis with a separate process and data store. Genesis bytes, Comet chain identity, EVM chain identifier, and CA digest identify the intended settlement environment.

title: Package and protocol compatibility
content: The control release gate compares package semantic version and wire protocol version independently. A compatible package name does not override a wire-version mismatch. Global readiness includes the release gate; a journey can have healthy dependencies while the overall release remains degraded.

title: Health and journey admission
content: Control route Meaning GET /livez The control process answers requests. GET /readyz All declared dependencies, all journeys, and the release gate are ready; otherwise HTTP 503 includes the degraded document. GET /v1/status Summary state for control, gateway, core, and Paxeer components. GET /v1/parameters Testnet-specific parameters (network layerx-testnet , package and wire versions, monthly reset schedule). GET /v1/journeys/{journey} Admission for a named journey, including failing dependencies. These routes describe the control service inside the operator's configured environment. Configure the control origin explicitly; the paths are not a promise of a public control hostname. The control service declares exactly three journeys: funding , payment , and receipt-inspection . There is no programs journey. Journey Required dependencies funding Identity, faucet, Redis, core admin, core. payment Identity, gateway, core, receipt authority. receipt-inspection Gateway, receipt authority, core. An admitted journey returns HTTP 200 with admitted: true , ready: true , and an empty failing array. A degraded journey returns HTTP 503 with named failures. The global probe also includes Paxeer; a Paxeer dependency failure can degrade global readiness while an execution journey remains admitted.

title: Probe depth
content: Readiness probes establish only their declared dependency condition (connection-level checks such as HTTP readiness, TLS handshake, TCP connection, or Redis connectivity). A real payment, registry operation, or settled checkpoint supplies deeper application evidence. The exact probe depth per dependency was not verified against the testnet probe bodies and is not specified here.

title: Durability and recovery
content: Core operation journals, Human state, registry records, internal event journals, signing material, and node history are durable state with distinct ownership. Preserve the complete material set needed by each service. Replacing a container does not authorize generating a new identity or seal secret for an existing store.

title: Signing boundary
content: Internal signing uses non-exporting signing APIs: callers create key handles and sign through authenticated routes without receiving seed material. Detailed sealing parameters were not verified in source and are not specified here. The signing API does not export seeds. KMS readiness requires the exclusive store lock and a successful durable-write probe. Access to signing routes requires a verified client certificate and bearer identity.

title: Verified event sources
content: Journey, payment, approval, and program event sources bind provisioned principals to their upstream credentials. Payment facts come from a decoded protocol receipt. Exact per-principal sequence and idempotency rules were not verified in source and are not specified here. Internal journals append and synchronize records before reporting success, hold an exclusive lock, and replay in append order. A failed append marks the journal unavailable. Event-source readiness requires upstream readiness, principal binding, and a writable journal; this prevents an apparently healthy process from silently losing new events.

title: Maintenance and draining
content: Record the active release, network identity, latest verified batch and checkpoint, and outstanding operation identifiers. Remove the affected service from new ingress admission through the deployment's traffic controls. Reconcile accepted operations from their durable receipts and journals, preserving idempotency keys for retries. Preserve outstanding event delivery state, signing material, and persistent volumes before replacing a process. Restore the service with matching identity and release material, then inspect replay and readiness results. Readmit traffic after the relevant journey and its evidence checks pass. Draining is a deployment and reconciliation workflow. The control API exposes readiness and journey admission; it does not define a universal drain endpoint. A pending operation remains pending until its canonical receipt or durable outcome resolves it.

title: Disposable environment tooling
content: The repository provides these operator targets for an isolated hosted environment. Cluster creation and teardown change infrastructure; teardown deletes the disposable cluster, persistent volumes, and local generated material. make platform-test-tooling make platform-hosted-topology-check make platform-beta-cluster-up make platform-hosted-smoke # After the disposable environment is no longer needed: make platform-beta-cluster-down Hosted smoke consumes the environment generated by bring-up and requires complete inputs. Retained-material mode validates inventory completeness, ownership, permissions, profile selection, registry consistency, and the live KMS seal digest before reuse. Retaining material supports another startup against the existing environment; it does not preserve data through teardown.

title: Failure triage
content: Read the global readiness document, then the specific journey's failing dependency list. Check the named dependency at its own boundary and distinguish connection health from verified application results. For release failures, compare package and wire versions before changing traffic admission. For journal or seal failures, preserve the store and restore matching material before restarting consumers. For settlement failures, compare the intended domain, certificate, canonical transaction receipt, and registered checkpoint evidence. Continue with Node operators , Guarantors , Security and trust boundaries , and Governance .

title: Network Parameters
content: Chain identity, denominations, configurable defaults, and governance controls across Paxeer X. Chain identity, denominations, configurable defaults, and governance controls across Paxeer X.

title: Unified execution and application parameters
content: Paxeer X retains chain ID 125 while joining EVM and Cosmos accounts to LayerX identity and kernel execution in one node. The address precompile’s getUnifiedAccount returns the related EVM address, Cosmos address, DID public key, and LayerX main account identifier. See the network model . Parameter family Controlled behavior Bridge Chain registry, attestor threshold, per-asset caps, and pause state Launchpad Quote denomination, virtual reserves, creation fee, fee bounds, decay, volatility and concentration weights, and protocol fee share Fee tokens Approved fee denominations, rate age, spread limit, enablement, and distribution policy XWeb Attestors, signature threshold, request fee, delivery limits, and pause controls Tenant domains modules/layerxchains namespaces state within the shared network. Creating a domain does not require new node infrastructure. The pre-merge custody and anchor parameter families are not live governable families. layerxVerify ( 0x1012 ) and layerxCustody ( 0x1013 ) are retired at the merge. layerxAnchor ( 0x1014 ) rejects writes after the merge, and the retained anchor module refuses new checkpoint submissions. Guarantor threshold, bond, challenge, and unbonding parameters describe that retired protocol only. docs/system/chain-modules.md in the monorepo lists parameter fields and docs/system/governance.md lists proposal types. Query the target network’s active values for financial decisions. See native interfaces , asset units , and bridge controls .

title: Chain Identifiers
content: Use these identifiers when configuring a wallet or client. Confirm the connected node's chain ID before signing a transaction. Parameter Value EVM chain ID 125 / 0x7d Consensus chain ID hyperpax_125-1 Account prefix pax1… Validator operator prefix paxvaloper1… Binary / default home paxd / ~/.paxeer Go module github.com/Sidiora-Labs/Paxeer-X-Network Repository Sidiora-Labs/paxeer-monorepo . The Go module path retains the Paxeer-X-Network name. EVM_RPC_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8545 curl -sS "$EVM_RPC_URL" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_chainId","params":[]}' paxd status --node tcp://127.0.0.1:26657 Public node JSON-RPC uses the root URL https://api-mainnet-beta.paxeer.network or the numbered nodes https://api1.mainnet-beta.paxeer.network through https://api14.mainnet-beta.paxeer.network . Expected eth_chainId result is 0x7d . Public namespaces are debug , echo , eth , net , pax , test and txpool . Method availability depends on node configuration. Configure more than one node and compare eth_blockNumber when selecting one near the head. node.hyperpaxeer.com is only the hpx library mirror used by build and installation tooling, never a JSON-RPC endpoint. See Public RPC . Source: tools/hpx/publish.sh , node/params/config.go , node/const.go , rpc/info.go .

title: Native Denominations
content: The native asset pays EVM gas. Node parameters name its human unit hpx . Cosmos CLI and bank APIs use uhpx for base-unit amounts. EVM clients use 18-decimal native amounts. 1 hpx = 1,000,000 uhpx 1 uhpx = 1,000,000,000,000 EVM wei 1 hpx = 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 EVM wei Use uhpx amounts for Cosmos CLI transactions and 18-decimal native amounts for EVM transactions. Address association joins the supported wallet representations; see address precompiles . Source: node/params/config.go — UhpxExponent ; modules/evm/state/utils.go — UhpxToSweiMultiplier .

title: Query Current Parameters
content: Query the connected network for its active governance, staking, slashing, and consensus parameters. Cosmos queries use the consensus RPC endpoint; EVM requests use the EVM JSON-RPC endpoint. paxd query staking params --node tcp://127.0.0.1:26657 paxd query slashing params --node tcp://127.0.0.1:26657 paxd query gov params --node tcp://127.0.0.1:26657 curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:26657/consensus_params Default parameter Value Meaning Unbonding time 21 days Default staking unbonding duration Unbonding / redelegation entries 7 Limit for an individual delegation pair Standard governance period 2 days Default deposit and voting periods Expedited governance period 1 day Default expedited voting duration Governance minimum deposit 10,000,000 base units Query the active governance deposit requirement Expedited minimum deposit 20,000,000 base units Query the active governance deposit requirement Slashing fractions 0 by default Configured by chain governance Governance approval requires a yes-vote ratio strictly greater than the configured threshold after abstentions are excluded. Validator jailing and equivocation handling apply alongside the configured slashing fractions. Source: sdk/x/staking/types/params.go , sdk/x/gov/types/params.go , sdk/x/gov/keeper/tally.go , sdk/x/slashing/types/params.go .

title: Gas and Block Limits
content: Query eth_gasPrice , eth_feeHistory , and eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas for EVM fee information. The node also has local admission prices and simulation limits. Consensus block.max_bytes is a block limit; mempool.max-tx-bytes is a separate transaction limit. See JSON-RPC and Configuration for the distinct EVM, consensus, and node settings.

title: Performance and Endpoints
content: Track block interval using block timestamps, throughput using transactions per block, and RPC latency using request metrics. Record the node revision and workload when comparing measurements. Use the RPC endpoint supplied by your node operator. The HPX distribution and peer registry supplies chain metadata and peer information for its configured network. The hosted gateway px_ API is separate from public node JSON-RPC. Obtain its URL and credentials from the operator.

title: LayerX Integration
content: Paxeer chain parameters govern L1 transactions. For applications that also use LayerX activities and receipts, see Paxeer and LayerX for the integration architecture. Previous Paxeer and LayerX Next Installation & Build

title: Troubleshoot a Node
content: Diagnose Paxeer X sync stalls, peer failures, RPC errors, database locks, and AppHash mismatches before changing node state. Diagnose Paxeer X sync stalls, peer failures, RPC errors, database locks, and AppHash mismatches before changing node state. Collect a small set of evidence before changing configuration: the running binary, configured network, current height, peer count, and recent logs. This lets you distinguish a local service problem from a network-wide halt or an application-state mismatch.

title: Diagnose kernel and application dependencies
content: A healthy EVM RPC confirms one execution surface. Trace the affected Paxeer X operation across ingress, identity, kernel execution, receipt verification, checkpoint authority, and chain settlement. Keep the activity ID, receipt identity, batch number, checkpoint ID, and chain transaction hash correlated. Symptom Evidence to inspect Recovery direction Gateway rejects a request Public method, authentication, registry route, dependency readiness, and receipt verification error Correct the failing authorization or upstream dependency Node or hosted service fails startup Generated configuration, signed genesis, network identity, state-directory ownership and lock. The former layerxd --check-config path is retired Use the matching artifacts and one process per state directory Sequencer advances, replica lags Replica input history, retained logs, connectivity, receipt and root agreement Restore the replica path from its verified history Checkpoint awaits attestations Availability retrieval, replay errors, authorized sequencer range, guarantor membership and threshold Restore verification and attestor connectivity before publication Checkpoint registered, publication pending Publication authorization, owner signatures, registered certificate, and finality evidence Supply the required valid authorization through its protected signing path Human or agent operation stalls Identity, owner approval, provider readiness, key-management channel, and canonical receipt Repair the responsible service boundary and resume the recorded operation Relay/archive falls behind Relay/archive is retired (see relay/archive status ); for chain history lag, use the paxd sync checks below Diagnose the paxd node's sync state instead A failed guarantor replay stops signing; preserve that evidence and resolve the disagreement. A refused or invalid publication signature is different from a missing authorization that remains pending. Do not substitute a transaction receipt for proof of checkpoint finality or a completed withdrawal. Continue with settlement and operator responsibilities .

title: Confirm the process and endpoints
content: The following examples assume a Linux systemd service named paxd and default local ports. Substitute your service name and bound ports if they differ. paxd version --long systemctl status paxd --no-pager systemctl show paxd -p ExecStart -p User ss -lntp curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:26657/status | jq '.result | {node_info, sync_info}' curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:26657/net_info | jq '.result.n_peers' curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:8545 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_chainId","params":[]}' For the Paxeer X network documented here, compare the Cosmos network with hyperpax_125-1 and the EVM result with 0x7d . A local development cluster can use a different identifier. The binary found in your shell can differ from the absolute path in the service’s ExecStart .

title: Match the symptom to the next check
content: Symptom Inspect Next action Connection refused Service status and listening sockets Confirm process startup and the bound address before investigating peers Zero peers Network ID, configured peer IDs, DNS, and P2P connectivity Use peers supplied for that exact network and release Peers present, height stalled Earliest error before the stall, upgrade height, disk and memory pressure Compare the same height with a known-good node Cosmos status works, EVM RPC fails EVM enablement, port, and RPC namespace configuration Check application configuration Historical query fails Pruning and state retention at the requested height Use an archive-capable endpoint with that state

title: Capture a sync stall
content: Capture the height and latest block time twice, a short interval apart. Compare both samples with a known-good node on the same network. A changing height with increasing lag points toward throughput; an unchanged height with a repeating error points toward a specific blocker. curl --fail --silent --show-error http://127.0.0.1:26657/status | jq '.result.sync_info | {latest_block_height, latest_block_time, catching_up}' journalctl -u paxd --since '15 minutes ago' --no-pager -o short-iso df -h df -i free -h Check storage capacity and inode exhaustion separately. For slow disks, use the host’s I/O monitoring to compare read latency, write latency, and saturation with the stalled period. Avoid changing several performance settings at once; preserve one baseline to compare against.

title: Investigate AppHash mismatches
content: An AppHash mismatch means the node’s computed application state disagrees with the block header. Record the exact height, expected and actual hashes, binary revision, genesis identity, and snapshot provenance. Use the binary assigned to that network’s upgrade schedule at the failing height. journalctl -u paxd --since '1 hour ago' --no-pager | rg -n -i 'apphash|app hash|panic|corrupt|upgrade|handshake' # Set PAXEER_NODE_HOME to the data directory used by the service. sha256sum "${PAXEER_NODE_HOME:?Set the active node home}/config/genesis.json" Handshake errors can follow a state mismatch; start with the earliest application error rather than repeatedly rotating peers. Reconcile the release, upgrade schedule, and snapshot with a known-good operator before choosing recovery steps.

title: Handle database locks and recovery
content: A database lock often means another process still holds the same data directory. Inspect the service and process list, including containers, before attempting another start. Keep one writer per data directory; stop the process holding the database before recovery. Rollback, snapshot restore, and reset commands change durable state and depend on the storage engine and release. Preserve a backup and use the recovery procedure for that exact node version. For validator recovery, preserve the existing signing state and confirm that only one signer is active. For a duplicate-signing alert, stop the affected signer and establish which instance owns signing before restarting. Retain the validator keys and signing history throughout recovery.

title: Prepare an actionable report
content: Node role, network identifiers, binary version and checksum, and startup command. Stalled or failing height and a comparison with a healthy node. At least the logs leading into the first failure, including the complete panic stack when present. Disk, memory, peer count, recent upgrade or restore activity, and snapshot checksum. The relevant configuration changes, with RPC credentials and signing material removed. Use Operators Guide for ongoing monitoring, Configuration for settings, and Run a Node for initial setup. Paxeer source: monorepo root — daemon/paxd/cmd/root.go (command registration), node/app.go (DefaultNodeHome), and consensus/internal/rpc/core/status.go (Status). Previous Operators Guide Next Configuration

title: Operators Guide
content: Manage Paxeer X node services, validator accounts, monitoring, and recovery. Manage Paxeer X node services, validator accounts, monitoring, and recovery. For stalled heights, peer failures, or state mismatches, start with Troubleshoot a Node . Record the binary revision and failing height before changing state.

title: Operate every Paxeer X plane
content: A Paxeer X deployment joins chain consensus, kernel execution, checkpoint finality, public ingress, discovery, and user services. Assign each role its own health checks, storage policy, credentials, and recovery procedure. Role Responsibility Operational evidence Chain node and validator Execute EVM and Cosmos transactions; enforce native custody, anchor, exchange, bridge, launchpad, and XWeb rules Chain identity, synchronization, peers, application hash, upgrade version, and RPC health Kernel sequencer Order signed activities, execute deterministic batches, and retain canonical logs and checkpoints Signed batch headers, state and receipt roots, durable activity history Authority replica Maintain the receipt-authority execution path and retained replica history Replica progress, verified receipts, and agreement with the sequencer Guarantor Independently retrieve and replay availability data, attest verified checkpoints, and submit settlement evidence Verified roots, bonded membership, certificate threshold, registration and finality Gateway and registry Verify public receipts, route requests, and publish discovery records Dependency readiness, receipt verification, registry identity, and routing health Agent and Human services Serve identity, delegated execution, owner approval, security, movement, and key-management boundaries Authorization outcomes, signed activity and receipt continuity, provider readiness Relay and archive Retired — see relay/archive status ; there is no installable relay/archive role — Public applications enter through the gateway. Core administration, signer channels, and provider internals stay inside their infrastructure boundary. Sequencing, custody release, and checkpoint authority remain distinct roles. See kernel execution , settlement , public APIs , and configuration .

title: Choose the Node Profile
content: Full nodes serve queries and retain recent history. Archive nodes preserve available historical state. Validators use a signing profile with public application APIs disabled, and seed nodes serve peer discovery. Hardware sizing depends on traffic, retained history, and the selected stores. Use Configuration to choose a node profile and its enabled services. Validator participation also depends on on-chain registration and the active set.

title: HPX Node Management
content: HPX manages a native paxd systemd service and verifies installation artifacts against its checksum manifest. The default distribution origin is https://node.hyperpaxeer.com . From the monorepo root, inspect and run the checked-out bootstrap script: less tools/hpx/get-hpx.sh sudo bash tools/hpx/get-hpx.sh HPX_TYPE=fullnode hpx setup Select HPX_TYPE=validator for the validator setup flow. The selected artifact set includes the binary, architecture-specific Wasm runtimes, genesis, and configuration. Use the selected mirror's manifest to confirm the release and artifact checksums. hpx # interactive menu hpx status hpx info hpx logs hpx start hpx stop hpx restart hpx peers show hpx statesync hpx validator keygen hpx validator stake hpx validator status hpx help hpx start|stop|restart control the systemd service. hpx validator keygen generates this node's operator account, hpx validator stake submits create-validator from the funded operator account, and hpx validator status reports validator state. hpx peers refresh changes the peer configuration (a peers-refresh systemd timer is also installed); hpx register announces the node to the registry. Use hpx update as a planned version change after checking network compatibility. Source: tools/hpx/get-hpx.sh , tools/hpx/hpx , tools/hpx/README.md .

title: Local Development Cluster
content: From the monorepo root: make docker-cluster-start make docker-cluster-start-monitoring The repository provides separate local cluster and monitoring targets. See Docker for compose services and generated paths.

title: Validator Accounts and Keys
content: The operator account submits staking and governance transactions. The consensus key signs blocks. Use an existing operator account, or create one with the following commands: paxd keys add operator paxd keys show operator -a paxd keys show operator --bech val -a paxd tendermint show-validator A pax1… account address, paxvaloper1… validator address, and consensus public key are distinct arguments. Use the form required by each command.

title: Register a Validator
content: After the node is synchronized and the operator is funded, register it with create-validator . This example uses one PAX in base units. Choose your stake, moniker, and commission settings, taking the network's active validator set into account. paxd tx staking create-validator \ --amount=1000000uhpx \ --pubkey="$(paxd tendermint show-validator)" \ --moniker="My Validator" \ --chain-id=hyperpax_125-1 \ --commission-rate="0.10" \ --commission-max-rate="0.20" \ --commission-max-change-rate="0.01" \ --min-self-delegation="1" \ --gas=auto \ --gas-adjustment=1.5 \ --gas-prices=0.02uhpx \ --from=operator --min-self-delegation is expressed in base units. Set gas prices for the connected network. Choose either --gas-prices with a gas limit or an explicit --fees amount.

title: Inspect Validator State
content: paxd query staking validator "$(paxd keys show operator --bech val -a)" paxd query staking delegations-to "$(paxd keys show operator --bech val -a)" paxd query slashing signing-info "$(paxd tendermint show-validator)" paxd query staking params paxd query slashing params The staking module also exposes edit-validator , delegate , redelegate , and unbond . paxd tx slashing unjail is subject to the keeper's eligibility checks; it cannot reverse permanent tombstoning. Source: sdk/x/staking/client/cli/tx.go , sdk/x/staking/client/cli/query.go , sdk/x/slashing/client/cli/query.go , sdk/client/tx/factory.go .

title: Monitoring
content: curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:26657/status | jq '.result.sync_info' curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:26657/net_info | jq '.result.n_peers' journalctl -u paxd -f Enable the configured Prometheus listener as shown in Configuration . Consensus metrics include block height, last-signed height, missed-block gauges, and syncing state. Build alerts from the emitted metric names and choose thresholds for your workload. Treat missed-block values as gauges.

title: Peer and Signer Configuration
content: Use bootstrap-peers , persistent-peers , and private-peer-ids under [p2p] . The peer ID can be read with paxd tendermint show-node-id . Keep signer access separate from public query services. Remote signers connect through the configured [priv-validator] socket or gRPC interface. For a hardware-backed signer, use an integration compatible with that interface and verify signing before activating the validator.

title: Backup and Recovery
content: Data Purpose config/priv_validator_key.json Consensus identity and signing key data/priv_validator_state.json Last signed height, round, step, and signature config/node_key.json Peer identity Selected keyring backend Operator account keys Genesis, TOML configuration, and configured stores Matching chain and state data Default paths are relative to ~/.paxeer and can be overridden. Stop the node before replacing its stores. Preserve the key and last-sign state together and ensure the original signer is offline before activating a replacement. Never start a second active signer with the same validator key. For snapshot recovery, verify the archive revision, checksum, backend, and layout before extraction. Reserve unsafe-reset-all for a planned state reset with complete backups. Use retention settings for routine pruning and paxd rollback for supported stopped-node state reconciliation. Source: consensus/config/config.go , consensus/privval/file.go , sdk/server/rollback.go , sdk/x/evidence/keeper/infraction.go .

title: Planned Upgrades
content: Match the network's upgrade plan and the release revision before replacing a binary. Record the installed version, preserve the previous binary and required state, stop the service, install the compatible release, and confirm synchronization after restart. Check the release's upgrade and snapshot compatibility requirements before installation. Governance upgrade proposals use the registered software-upgrade command. Expedited proposal support uses --is-expedited ; query current deposit and voting parameters before submitting. Previous Configuration Next Consensus

title: Oracles & Market Risk
content: Understand how Paxeer X accepts signed price observations, rejects stale or anomalous inputs, and applies market-specific risk limits. Understand how Paxeer X accepts signed price observations, rejects stale or anomalous inputs, and applies market-specific risk limits.

title: Prices enter the ledger as signed observations
content: Paxeer X carries external market data into deterministic execution through signed ORACLE_PUSH activities. Execution consumes accepted observations; it does not make an external network request to obtain a price. This gives replay the same ordered market input that original execution used. An observation identifies a market, observation sequence, unsigned integer price, observation timestamp, and source identifier. The signed transport appends a signature to the observation (see the format below); the signer key itself is checked against the market's permitted set rather than carried in the transport. A market defines the permitted keys, freshness window, minimum and maximum prices, and maximum deviation from its preceding accepted observation.

title: Price acceptance pipeline
content: Check Acceptance rule Refusal Canonical encoding The payload has the exact expected length and re-encodes to identical bytes. LXP_ERR_NON_CANONICAL Authorized signer The public key belongs to the market permission set and verifies the domain-separated observation signature. LXP_ERR_UNAUTHORIZED_ORACLE Freshness Observation time is no later than sealed batch time, and age does not exceed maximum staleness. LXP_ERR_TIMESTAMP_REGRESSION or LXP_ERR_ORACLE_STALE Price range The integer price lies between configured minimum and maximum, inclusive. LXP_ERR_ORACLE_BOUNDS Observation ordering The incoming sequence advances the accepted stream and satisfies timestamp ordering. LXP_ERR_ORACLE_SEQUENCE or LXP_ERR_TIMESTAMP_REGRESSION Deviation Absolute change does not exceed the prior accepted price multiplied by the deviation limit in basis points. LXP_ERR_ORACLE_DEVIATION The deviation allowance is rounded down in integer price units. The first accepted observation has no preceding observation for a relative-deviation comparison, but it must still satisfy authorization, freshness, encoding, and configured bounds.

title: Concrete acceptance example
content: Suppose the last accepted price is 100,000 integer units and the permitted deviation is 200 basis points. The next observation may differ by at most 2,000 units. A price of 101,500 satisfies that deviation check; 103,000 does not. If maximum staleness is 5,000 milliseconds, an observation aged exactly 5,000 milliseconds satisfies the freshness boundary, while 5,001 milliseconds fails it. These are example parameters, not network-wide defaults.

title: Canonical observation format
content: The unsigned canonical observation is 72 bytes ( LX_ORACLE_OBSERVATION_BYTES ). The signed transport submitted on the wire is 137 bytes ( LX_ORACLE_TRANSPORT_BYTES ): a 1-byte version ( LX_ORACLE_TRANSPORT_VERSION = 1), the 72-byte observation, and a 64-byte signature, decoded by lx_perps_oracle_transport_decode . The public key is not carried in the transport bytes; it is resolved from the market's permitted set. Integer fields use the canonical big-endian encoding; price uses unsigned 128-bit units. Signature verification binds the canonical payload to the LXP:ORACLE:OBSERVATION:v1 tag under the signature-preimage domain. market_id: 32 bytes observation_sequence: 8 bytes price: 16 bytes observed_at: 8 bytes source_identifier: 8 bytes Keep the market price scale with every decoded price. A source identifier describes the submitted observation; it does not replace signer authorization or make an unsigned price acceptable.

title: Risk limits are market-specific
content: Initial margin, maintenance margin, liquidation fees, funding caps, permitted oracle keys, and price acceptance bounds are explicit market parameters. A parameter version identifies the configuration revision. Market creation validates nonzero units and intervals, distinct system accounts, sorted unique permitted keys, and coherent margin and price bounds. Market halt state is an additional control. Risk-taking operations and funding execution enforce halt checks. Treat the halt flag as an operation-specific refusal boundary: an integration should inspect the receipt of each action rather than assume that all account or recovery operations have identical halt behavior.

title: What accepted data proves
content: An accepted observation proves that its canonical payload passed the configured signature and market checks at its place in execution. It does not prove the external source was economically correct, guarantee future prices, or remove liquidity and insurance constraints. Application risk policies can impose stricter freshness or exposure limits than the protocol minimums.

title: Integration workflow
content: Load the market identifier, price scale, parameter version, permitted signer set, and risk thresholds. Read the latest accepted observation with its sequence, timestamp, source identifier, and price. Display observation age and market status beside price-sensitive actions. Submit actions using canonical payloads and inspect execution receipts for price, margin, authorization, and halt refusals. On a stale, out-of-range, or deviation refusal, obtain a new accepted observation or reassess the request. Repeatedly submitting the same invalid observation cannot make it valid. Oracle intake records accepted observation data and its global sequence. Oracle ingestion may not mutate balances: value movements remain explicit ledger transfer sets performed by authorized modules. Keep observation acceptance and financial settlement as separate events in application accounting.

Platform APIs Application gateways, hosted services, webhooks and integration surfaces. EVM JSON-RPC Wallet integration, chain requests, contracts and transaction inspection. Operator guides Nodes, configuration, network services and settlement infrastructure. What is the difference between Paxeer X and LayerX? Paxeer X is the EVM chain supplying execution, custody and settlement. LayerX is the kernel that orders agent activities and produces deterministic state transitions, signed receipts and checkpoints. Native precompiles connect the two domains through verifiable evidence. Compare the domains Which chain ID and token does the network use? EVM chain ID 125 ( hyperpax_125-1 ) with native token PAX . Denominations, gas limits and endpoints are listed with the network parameters. Network parameters How does an agent get authority to spend? Through scoped, revocable delegation: primary and session keys, budget limits and mandates define exactly what an agent may do with money, and owners can revoke or rotate that authority. Agent budgets How do I verify a payment actually settled? Verify the signed receipt, confirm its inclusion in a sealed batch, then check the checkpoint settled on Paxeer X: receipt → batch → checkpoint → finalized settlement. Receipts and proofs Can I use my existing EVM tooling? Yes. Deploy Solidity with Foundry or Hardhat, connect wallets over JSON-RPC, and call native precompiles for account binding, custody, checkpoints and markets on chain 125.
