title: Paid APIs and x402
content: Monetize HTTP resources, agent tools, and recurring access with payment-required offers and receipt-verified fulfillment on Paxeer X. Monetize HTTP resources, agent tools, and recurring access with payment-required offers and receipt-verified fulfillment on Paxeer X. A Paxeer X paid endpoint advertises its price through x402 version 2. The buyer selects an accepted offer, authorizes payment, and retries with payment evidence. The seller releases the resource after verifying the receipt and required commitment. Exact, metered, and subscription schemes share this evidence-bound lifecycle.

title: The HTTP payment exchange
content: The buyer requests the resource without payment. The seller returns HTTP 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and matching JSON body. The buyer selects a supported scheme and network, verifies payee terms, and constructs a payment payload. The buyer retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE , preserving the accepted offer and required extensions. The seller verifies settlement and records fulfillment before returning the resource with PAYMENT-RESPONSE . The buyer independently verifies the response receipt and settlement reference. HTTP headers carry standard-base64 JSON. MCP and A2A bindings carry the corresponding JSON values. Settlement identity stays consistent across transports, so redelivering the same payment through another binding retains the same economic identity.

title: Define the offer
content: Field Contract x402Version 2 . resource HTTP(S) URL, with optional description, MIME type, service name, tags, and icon URL. accepts One to 32 offers; buyer selection follows seller order among supported scheme/network pairs. scheme , network exact , metered , or subscription , with the intended network identifier. amount Positive canonical decimal string, represented exactly as an unsigned 128-bit integer. asset , payTo 32-byte hexadecimal Asset and recipient identifiers. maxTimeoutSeconds Positive request timeout bound. extra.layerx Commitment, account reference, currency, and scheme-specific grant terms. For a layerx:* network, extra.layerx.account names the destination account, such as agent:<did>:main , and currency names its money currency. The offered payTo must derive from that account under a supported account-ID derivation. Buyers refuse a mismatched recipient.

title: Add seller middleware
content: The Node package @sidiora/layerx-seller-middleware exports SellerMiddleware , ReceiptPayloadAuthority , and the payment-header codecs. Supply a trusted authority resolver, payment requirements, and a durable fulfillment repository. The following handler is the resource-release pattern used by the paid API example; middleware is the configured seller instance. import { PAYMENT_SIGNATURE_HEADER } from "@sidiora/layerx-seller-middleware"; const header = request.headers[PAYMENT_SIGNATURE_HEADER.toLowerCase()]; const paymentHeader = Array.isArray(header) ? undefined : header; const decision = await middleware.handle( "public-paid-api", paymentHeader, async () => resourceBody, ); const headers = decision.kind === "payment-required" || decision.kind === "refused" || decision.kind === "released" ? decision.headers : { "retry-after": "1" }; response.writeHead(decision.status, { "content-type": "application/json", ...headers, }); response.end(JSON.stringify( decision.kind === "payment-required" ? decision.body : decision.kind === "released" ? decision.resource : { state: decision.kind }, )); The example serves GET /paid . Its configuration selects protocol version, network, price, Asset, recipient, account, currency, receipt authority, and fulfillment directory. Keep credentials in the configured environment variables. Set the resource URL to the externally reachable endpoint your customer requests.

title: Persist fulfillment
content: A fulfillment record binds the caller's idempotency key to the request digest, canonical receipt, authorized batch, and returned resource. Persist it durably and return the stored resource for a matching retry. Refuse reuse of the same key for a different request. The example writes an exclusive file, synchronizes it and its directory, and checks the existing record after a concurrent write.

title: Integrate the buyer
content: BuyerMiddleware accepts a production client, source account, protocol selection, supported scheme/network pairs, configured receipt authorities, and retry policy. prepare(paymentRequiredHeader, callerIdempotencyKey) parses the offer and prepares payment through the typed quote workflow. fetch drives the HTTP exchange, while captureSettlement verifies the result. Use fetchGrant and captureGrantSettlement for grant-backed receives. The buyer validates offered account and currency terms before quoting. Required extensions are echoed unchanged. Choose a stable caller idempotency key for one purchase and retain it with the accepted offer and activity identifier until the outcome is resolved.

title: Metered requests and subscriptions
content: A metered or subscription offer additionally commits to a nonzero payer and purpose hash. Subscription offers require a positive decimal-string windowSeconds below 2^64 ; metered offers omit the field. The payer signs a canonical 346-byte Asset ordinal-7 grant. The receiver submits a canonical 733-byte Asset ordinal-6 receive that embeds the grant and receiver authorization. Every metered request is one draw. Every subscription renewal uses a distinct signed receive and idempotency key; a recurring allowance alone does not establish one renewal per period. { "receive": "<733-byte canonical receive as hex>", "idempotencyKey": "<64-hex key>" } Validation binds the payer, recipient, Asset, amount, purpose, network, grant identity, allowance, per-draw maximum, expiry, controller, and signed context. Metered grants are non-recurring with a zero window. Unknown, paused, or unregistered Assets and changed payment facts are refused.

title: Select settlement assurance
content: Commitment Required evidence executed An authorized sequencer-signed successful receipt for the exact activity. batched Executed evidence plus receipt inclusion in the authorized signed batch header. finalised Batched evidence plus the guarantor checkpoint certificate for that batch. Set extra.layerx.commitment to the assurance your resource requires. Authority keys come from verifier configuration. Missing evidence keeps settlement pending or refused; it never silently lowers the requested assurance.

title: Receipt verification and capture
content: The seller verifies canonical receipt encoding, activity binding, successful result, protocol body, authorized sequencer signature, and the accepted Asset, amount, and recipient. The gateway records a receipt-verified settlement. Success returns transaction: "lxp:<receipt_digest>" . The buyer checks success , the layerx extension, verificationLevel: "sequencer-signed" , canonical receipt bytes, payer, network, Asset, recipient, and amount. It recomputes the receipt digest and requires both the declared digest and lxp: reference to match. An HTTP 200 or acknowledgement by itself does not establish settlement.

title: Recover uncertain payment outcomes
content: There is no public lx_* JSON-RPC transport in this checkout. The hosted gateway refuses every lx_* method name with JSON-RPC -32601 ( Method not found ), including lx_sendActivity , lx_getActivityStatus , lx_getReceipt , and lx_getProof . Do not build submission or recovery flows on those names. Recover through the identity you already hold: the purchase idempotency key, the accepted offer, and the original activity or transaction reference. Re-resolve the original payment through the SDK or buyer-middleware settlement capture, and use published hosted reads such as pax_sequencerReceipt where they apply. For batched assurance, require the recovered receipt evidence to verify against the authorized signed batch header before release. Verify recovered evidence before releasing or capturing the resource. Preserve payment identity throughout recovery; a replacement debit does not resolve the original purchase. Seller outcome HTTP Application action Payment required 402 Select and authorize an offered payment. Pending 202 Honor retry guidance and recover the same activity. Refused 402 Read settlement reason; correct the failed condition. Released 200 Verify PAYMENT-RESPONSE and consume the stored resource.

title: Facilitators and transport interoperability
content: The x402 facilitator exposes /supported , /verify , and /settle . Verification is read-only; settlement is state-changing and completes against verified canonical receipts. HTTP, MCP, and A2A share the same message semantics. An identical settlement identity and receipt digest recover the existing settlement; a swapped receipt for that identity is an idempotency conflict. Use service agreements for work that needs deadlines, delivered artifacts, review, and disputes. Continue with the SDK and native protocol modules for account, Asset, and activity integration.

title: Design for Parallel Execution
content: Reduce shared-state contention in Paxeer contracts, preserve on-chain invariants, and measure gas separately from throughput. Reduce shared-state contention in Paxeer contracts, preserve on-chain invariants, and measure gas separately from throughput. When the Giga executor is enabled, Paxeer executes transactions with optimistic concurrency control (OCC): independent work proceeds concurrently, while conflicting access is detected and resolved in a deterministic order. OCC runs only when giga_executor.enabled and giga_executor.occ_enabled are both set (both default to true ) and the block is not processed synchronously. Otherwise execution falls back to the V2 OCC path ( ProcessTXsWithOCCV2 ) or synchronous processing. Contract storage layout influences how much work is independent in any of these paths. See the execution engine and SDK integration .

title: Find the shared writes
content: Start by listing the state each entry point reads and writes, including state touched by external calls. Two different users can still conflict if both transactions update one total, one queue head, or the same pool. Pattern Contention source Design option Global counter on every update All writers touch the same slot Use per-user state when the aggregate is only needed for display One order book for all markets Unrelated markets share mutable state Partition by market where business rules allow Large push distribution One transaction writes many recipient balances Use bounded batches or independent claims Shared token or pool call External state reintroduces a common dependency Include the external call’s storage accesses in your design

title: Partition state by the unit of work
content: This small notes contract partitions quantities by caller and position ID, giving each pair its own storage entry. // SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT pragma solidity 0.8.28; contract PositionNotes { mapping(address => mapping(uint256 => int256)) public quantities; event QuantityChanged(address indexed owner, uint256 indexed id, int256 quantity); function setQuantity(uint256 id, int256 quantity) external { quantities[msg.sender][id] = quantity; emit QuantityChanged(msg.sender, id, quantity); } } Updates for different caller/ID pairs reach distinct mapping entries. Updates to the same entry still depend on one another. Calls from one sender also share nonce and balance state, so include sender distribution when measuring concurrency.

title: Keep invariants authoritative
content: Keep supply caps, collateral requirements, and conservation checks in on-chain state. These shared dependencies preserve the contract’s accounting rules. When an aggregate is used only for a dashboard, events can feed an indexer instead of requiring every transaction to update the same display counter. Preserve an explicit replay range and durable event cursor as described in Query the EVM .

title: Bound work and inspect packing
content: Bound arrays and loops that touch persistent storage; measure the largest permitted input. Calculate temporary values in memory and write only the final required state. Consider pull-based claims when recipients can act independently, while preserving authorization, funding, and reentrancy protections. Inspect packed fields before combining them: two logical values in one storage slot can introduce a shared write. Treat an external call as part of the access set, including shared token balances, allowances, and precompile-backed state.

title: Measure the actual workload
content: Use two workloads with the same contract and transaction shape: one distributes work across independent keys, and the other concentrates it on the same keys. Keep the binary revision, hardware, sender distribution, and submission rate fixed. Measure single-call gas with Foundry or Hardhat before changing storage layout. Run the workload against a Paxeer development cluster with the intended executor configuration. Record submitted, included, successful, and failed transactions separately. Compare throughput and latency percentiles at the same load, and inspect available conflict/re-execution diagnostics. Check the resulting state and invariants after every run, including retries and contention cases. forge test --gas-report forge snapshot Track gas per call and network throughput separately. Fewer conflicts can improve scheduling while the gas charged per transaction stays the same. Use the development-cluster workload to compare throughput and latency.

title: Review before adoption
content: Keep a storage-access sketch beside benchmark results: which keys are independent, which invariants require a shared dependency, and which external calls can serialize work. Compare each change against the same workload and check that the resulting state remains correct. Continue with transaction diagnostics to inspect execution failures and storage architecture for the underlying state engines. Paxeer source: Paxeer-X-Network/ — engine/executor/config/config.go (OCCEnabled), node/app.go (ProcessTXsWithOCCGiga), and modules/evm/types/params.go (DefaultPaxSstoreSetGasEIP2200). Previous Debug Transactions Next Troubleshoot a Node

title: Paxeer X and LayerX
content: One BFT network combines EVM smart contracts, autonomous agent execution, and programmable finance, with finality at block commit. One BFT network combines EVM smart contracts, autonomous agent execution, and programmable finance, with finality at block commit.

title: One Network, Kernel In-Process
content: Paxeer X is one BFT network with EVM chain ID 125 . paxd supplies the Cosmos SDK chain and native EVM. The LayerX kernel is embedded in the node through modules/lxphost and participates in block proposal and deterministic execution. node/sequencer supplies execution ordering within the node. Applications compose both through native EVM precompiles and protocol receipts. The names describe execution surfaces, not separate networks. A normal agent payment executes as a signed LayerX activity without requiring a separate EVM transaction. Its kernel state changes commit with the rest of the node's transaction state. A receipt is final once its block is committed. There is no later checkpoint or settlement step. Capability Paxeer surface LayerX surface Application execution Solidity contracts, native precompiles, Cosmos modules Signed activities, economic modules, deterministic WASM programs Identity EVM and Paxeer addresses Agent DIDs, sessions, scoped grants, recovery and revocation Money Native assets and bank balances Payments, holds, escrow, budgets, streams and protocol balances Markets perps at 0x1015 , pricefeed at 0x1020 , spot at 0x1021 – 0x1025 , launchpad at 0x1017 , bridge at 0x1016 Trading, positions, funding, and liquidation modules Evidence Committed blocks; pax_sequencerReceipt Signed receipts, ordered batches, state witnesses and replay Security authority Validators and governance under BFT consensus Actor authority, deterministic execution and independently replayed activity

title: Agent Businesses with Real Financial Controls
content: An agent operates through its own identity and bounded authority. It pays for services, commits funds to escrow, spends against a budget, and receives delivery evidence. Businesses issue assets and agents trade the resulting instruments. Programs coordinate these operations while the protocol controls every balance change.

title: Solidity Applications That Understand Agent Activity
content: A contract consumes a verified service receipt, proves a LayerX account balance, or checks a program result before applying its own rules. The merge precompiles at 0x101A – 0x101E and 0x0901 – 0x0908 expose ledger, payment, authorization, program, and tenant-domain surfaces. Select the interface for the upgrade active at the queried height.

title: Connected Markets and Assets
content: In the v6.12.0 set, perps is served at 0x1015 in place of the earlier layerxExchange . The same set serves the second-generation launchpad at 0x1017 , pricefeed at 0x1020 , and spot_pecor , spot_orders , spot_stoporders , spot_quoter and spot_vault at 0x1021 – 0x1025 . Registered external chains connect through layerxBridge at 0x1016 . Each path retains its own economic and verification rules.

title: A Shared Account, Explicit Authority
content: The address precompile binds an EVM address to a did:layerx identity with consent from both keys. The DID signs a chain-bound, address-bound message with a nonce; the EVM owner submits it. Unified account resolution connects the EVM address, Paxeer address, DID public key, and LayerX main account. Binding makes identity discoverable across surfaces. Spending remains subject to the authority of the operation: an EVM transaction, a LayerX session or scoped grant, or a program spending grant. Revocation and expiry constrain delegated actions.

title: Evidence and Finality
content: Execute payments, trades, deliveries, or program calls as signed activities or EVM transactions. Receive a signed execution receipt. pax_sequencerReceipt reports submitted , receipted , or committed . Treat the result as final only at committed , when the block covering its sequence batch has committed. The external checkpoint registry, bonded guarantor attestations, and L0–L4 settlement ladder are retired. The pre-merge layerxVerify ( 0x1012 ) and layerxCustody ( 0x1013 ) interfaces are retired at the merge. layerxAnchor ( 0x1014 ) rejects writes after the merge. These historical interfaces do not provide current funding or finality paths. The native asset pays EVM transaction gas. Its human-unit identifier in node parameters is hpx , with base unit uhpx . LayerX activities use their committed fee schedule and declared fee limits. Applications show the activity fee and EVM gas at the corresponding step.

title: Choose Your Starting Point
content: Read Unified Network Architecture for state, proof and authority boundaries. Build contracts with Foundry or Hardhat , then explore native precompiles . Explore protocol modules and the WASM runtime for programmable execution. Use Network Parameters for chain identity and Building a Frontend for wallet integration. Previous Introduction Next Unified Network

title: Your first payment
content: Quote, commit, and verify a Paxeer X payment using the application SDK or a native Asset transfer. Quote, commit, and verify a Paxeer X payment using the application SDK or a native Asset transfer.

title: Choose your integration
content: Use the application SDK when you want account-level payment journeys and bearer-token authentication. Use the native CLI when you control a signing identity and need explicit canonical activities, receipt policy, fee limits, and commitment selection. The LayerX package and command names are the integration interfaces of Paxeer X.

title: 1. Install the application packages
content: npm install @sidiora/layerx-sdk @sidiora/layerx-buyer-middleware Configure LAYERX_API_URL with your environment's API base URL and LAYERX_API_TOKEN with its account bearer token. Use HTTPS outside a loopback emulator. These credentials identify your API account; do not embed them in browser bundles or logs.

title: 2. Quote and commit the payment
content: This SDK integration accepts your typed source, destination, and money values. Choose paymentKey from a persistent order identifier or request digest and retain it before committing. import { LayerXPaymentHttpTransport } from "@sidiora/layerx-buyer-middleware"; import { ProductionClient, SecretBytes, idempotencyKey } from "@sidiora/layerx-sdk"; export const openLayerX = (apiUrl, apiToken) => new ProductionClient( new LayerXPaymentHttpTransport({ baseUrl: apiUrl, bearerToken: new SecretBytes(new TextEncoder().encode(apiToken)) }) ); export const pay = async (layerx, source, destination, money, paymentKey) => { const quote = await layerx.human("move.quote", { source, destination, money }); return layerx.human( "move.commit", { quote_id: quote.quote_id }, { idempotencyKey: idempotencyKey(paymentKey) } ); }; The quote establishes the payment terms, mechanism, fee ceiling, arrival expectation, and irreversible legs. Present these terms for approval before committing. An expired quote must be refreshed and approved again. Monetary quantities use integer base units rather than floating-point arithmetic.

title: 3. Follow the original journey
content: Store the returned journey identifier alongside the purchase key. Read its progress through journey.get and resolve evidence references through evidence.get . A layerx-receipt reference identifies canonical receipt evidence. Finish only when the journey reaches done or done-finalised with verified evidence. Observed outcome Next action waiting-for-you Obtain the requested decision before expiry. still-checking Track the existing journey; lock controls that could create a duplicate payment. refused Read refusal authority and money_left . done / done-finalised Verify evidence and record the settlement before fulfilment.

title: Native path: prepare a funded identity
content: The CLI uses your local key, a stored gateway credential, and a receipt policy supplied independently of the RPC response you verify. A policy binds protocol version, network, sequencer identity and key, permitted batches, and checkpoint context. Keep private seeds out of shell history. cargo build --manifest-path tools/platform/cli/Cargo.toml export PATH="$PWD/tools/platform/target/debug:$PATH" layerx key create alice layerx key default alice layerx wallet list export RPC_URL=https://api-mainnet-beta.paxeer.network/ export RECEIPT_POLICY=/absolute/path/to/receipt-policy.json export EVM_KEY_FILE=/absolute/path/to/evm-key-export export FEE_LIMIT='<maximum fee in base units>' export ASSET_ID='<64-hex Asset id>' export RECIPIENT_DID='<recipient DID>' Public JSON-RPC endpoints are HTTPS URLs at the root path. The old /rpc and /rpc/ws routes are retired. Note the current checkout still has CLI transport gaps: setting --rpc to a correct public root URL does not by itself make wallet commands work against a public node. Treat the native commands below as the command surface and verify connectivity in your environment before relying on them. The OS keyring stores keys by default; headless environments use the configured encrypted file store. The payer must already hold a spendable balance on the merged network before sending. Do not fund through the former custody precompile path: the custody module is retired, its keeper refuses deposits, and the precompile reverts. Confirm the account balance before spending.

title: Open the recipient account and send
content: Select the recipient wallet to open its account for the chosen Asset, then select the funded payer wallet to transfer. Identity sequence and source-account sequence are obtained separately. The signing flow discloses the debit authorization and outer activity, including recipient, amount, Asset, fee ceiling, expiry, network, and idempotency key. # Run with the recipient wallet selected. # open-account requires --evm-key-file, --receipt-policy, and --fee-limit. layerx --rpc "$RPC_URL" --gateway-credential beta wallet open-account \ --asset "$ASSET_ID" --evm-key-file "$EVM_KEY_FILE" \ --receipt-policy "$RECEIPT_POLICY" --fee-limit "$FEE_LIMIT" # Select the funded payer before sending. layerx key default alice layerx --rpc "$RPC_URL" --gateway-credential beta wallet send \ --to "$RECIPIENT_DID" --asset "$ASSET_ID" --amount 10 \ --wait executed --receipt-policy "$RECEIPT_POLICY" \ --fee-limit "$FEE_LIMIT" Choose executed for a verified execution receipt, batched for authenticated batch inclusion, or finalised for matching finalised checkpoint evidence. The exact wire spelling is finalised .

title: Recover a pending native payment
content: Each new CLI write creates a new idempotency key. If the first attempt times out, save its transaction hash and recover the original receipt instead of repeating wallet send . wallet receipt takes a transaction hash, with --wait and --receipt-policy as its options. layerx --rpc "$RPC_URL" --gateway-credential beta wallet receipt \ "$TX_HASH" --receipt-policy "$RECEIPT_POLICY" --wait finalised --timeout-seconds (1 to 300, default 60) belongs to wallet watch and to write commands such as wallet send , not to wallet receipt . Stream notifications are wake-ups: reconcile them with verified reads or a receipt verification.

title: Public JSON-RPC surface
content: The hosted gateway publishes px_* methods — including px_register , px_getAccount , px_getBalances , px_listAssets , and px_requestFunds — plus pax_sequencerReceipt . Every legacy lx_* method name is refused wholesale with JSON-RPC -32601 ( Method not found ). Do not build submission or recovery flows on lx_sendActivity , lx_getActivityStatus , lx_getReceipt , or lx_getProof ; no such public transport exists in this checkout. Use the SDK, the CLI, or the published px_* and node namespaces instead, and verify recovered evidence before treating a payment as settled.

title: Handle common failures
content: Code or condition Response idempotency-required Supply the persistent purchase key before committing. idempotency-conflict Resolve the original request; do not reuse its key for a different body. rate-limit Respect the carried retry timing. unknown-outcome Recover the original payment by key and evidence. budget-refusal Inspect the funded budget and approved spending limits. Invalid signature, stale sequence, missing scope, or evidence mismatch Resolve the specific refusal before preparing any new payment.

title: Next steps
content: Payment lifecycle and merchant workflows Create an Asset and manage accounts Funding and money movement Charge for HTTP resources Estimate fees and set limits Public payment API reference

title: Payments
content: Build transfers, paid APIs, merchant checkout, metered usage, and subscriptions on Paxeer X with explicit approval, bounded fees, and verifiable settlement. Build transfers, paid APIs, merchant checkout, metered usage, and subscriptions on Paxeer X with explicit approval, bounded fees, and verifiable settlement.

title: One payment lifecycle
content: Paxeer X combines native Asset settlement with the LayerX payment platform. Applications quote a move, commit the accepted quote under a stable idempotency key, and track a journey whose outcome is backed by evidence. Native integrations prepare canonical activities, disclose their exact terms, sign, submit, and verify the requested commitment. Quote: identify payer, recipient, Asset or currency, amount, mechanism, fee ceiling, expected arrival, and irreversible legs. Approve and commit: bind approval to those terms. An expired quote returns quote-expired rather than silently changing the payment. Track: retain the journey or activity identifier and idempotency key through interruptions. Verify and fulfil: validate canonical evidence and payment facts before delivering goods or releasing a protected resource.

title: Choose a payment experience
content: Experience Flow Settlement rule Wallet or application transfer Quote and commit a move, or sign a native Asset SEND Verify the receipt and selected commitment Paid HTTP resource x402 exact offer and receipt-backed retry Release only after the offer is paid and verified Merchant cart Catalog quote, persistent order, payment, fulfilment Bind order and settlement to the same request digest Metered usage Non-recurring grant and authorized receiver draws Validate purpose, allowance, expiry, and each receive Subscription Recurring grant with a declared billing window New receive and distinct period key for every renewal

title: Journey states
content: State Application behavior getting-ready The payment is accepted and its legs are being prepared. sending At least one leg is in flight. waiting-for-you Request the required human decision before its deterministic expiry. processing The payment is submitted and settling. still-checking The outcome is unknown. Keep duplicate-capable controls locked and resolve the original payment. done Settlement is backed by a verified receipt or finality proof. done-finalised The receipt-backed outcome has committed evidence, represented by checkpoint-finalised verification. This retained label is not required for every committed journey: EVM-intent and native journey projections render done and expose evidence separately. refused Inspect refused_by and money_left before reporting the result. awaiting-approval The native engine exposes its awaiting-approval leg phase while the journey awaits approval. It is not receipt-backed completion. closed Retained wallet-binding, deposit, withdraw, and exit history reads as closed. Closed history cannot resume signing or execution and does not assert a successful movement.

title: Merchant checkout
content: @sidiora/layerx-merchant-middleware prices catalog lines and creates a PAYMENT-REQUIRED offer. A cart contains at most 256 lines, with unique SKUs and positive integer quantities. All lines share one Asset, recipient, scheme, and network. Amount multiplication and summation use integer arithmetic within the 128-bit amount range. The order store opens the order before the seller decision. The quote digest binds its lines, total, Asset, recipient, scheme, network, and timeout. Repeating an unchanged checkout resolves the same order; a catalog price change produces a different digest. Store responses are checked for matching checkoutKey and requestDigest , with mismatches refused as order-conflict . Checkout result Action payment-required Return HTTP 402 with the decision headers. pending Preserve the order while settlement completes. refused Record the refused order and expose its refusal. paid The order is paid-verified and carries the receipt digest and transaction. Late settlement uses verified webhooks. The merchant checks signature, freshness, replay protection, order identifier and request digest, then resolves and verifies canonical receipt evidence. It recomputes the receipt digest before marking the order paid.

title: Buyer and HTTP payment flow
content: The seller responds with HTTP 402 and PAYMENT-REQUIRED . The buyer selects an offered requirement unchanged and checks supported scheme, network, Asset, recipient, amount, and commitment. The buyer pays under the purchase idempotency key and retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE . The seller verifies the payment before release and supplies PAYMENT-RESPONSE . The buyer verifies captured settlement against receipt evidence. @sidiora/layerx-buyer-middleware provides fetch(url, init) for the complete loop, plus parseOffer , prepare , and captureSettlement for custom workflows. Unsupported requirements fail before payment. The human-plane transport uses HTTPS, protects bearer tokens with SecretBytes , and carries Idempotency-Key on mutations.

title: Metered payments and subscriptions
content: A metered or subscription challenge binds extra.layerx.payer , purposeHash , and commitment ; subscriptions also bind windowSeconds . The payer signs an ordinal-7 grant. Each draw uses a receiver-signed ordinal-6 receive with its own idempotency key. Before submission, the seller checks payer, recipient, Asset, amount, purpose, grant limits, expiry, network, and receiver authority. Metered grants are non-recurring with a zero window. Subscription grants recur with the exact offered window. Every renewal uses current sequences and a distinct period key: an allowance alone does not establish one renewal per period. Pending draws return HTTP 202 without resource release; persistent draw recovery resolves the original activity identifier.

title: Commitments and evidence
content: Commitment Required evidence executed Verified canonical receipt for the submitted activity. batched Execution plus an authenticated receipt proof whose canonical value equals the receipt byte for byte. finalised Batch evidence plus finalised checkpoint evidence whose canonical header equals the proof's signed batch header. A stronger requested commitment is never downgraded to a weaker success. HTTP 202, admission acknowledgements, and activity identifiers alone do not establish execution. Successful x402 settlement references lxp:<receipt_digest> , with the digest computed from the canonical receipt and the protocol Merkle-leaf domain. Verify configured authority, protocol/network, receipt facts, and commitment evidence together.

title: Retries, sequences, and unknown outcomes
content: Choose one stable key per purchase or order. Repeating a human-plane mutation under that key returns its original journey; a different body under the same key is idempotency-conflict . Native activities also consume identity and account sequences, preventing replay. Retain signed bytes and the activity identifier when a response is lost. Resolve the original through receipt and status reads instead of generating another debit. On the human plane, retriabilities are retriable , retriable-after , structural , and final . The SDK ProductionClient reports its own retry classes: never , safe , after , and unknown-outcome . Map between the two vocabularies explicitly rather than treating them as one list. Respect carried rate-limit timing. An unknown-outcome result or human-plane still-checking requires tracking and evidence recovery, with duplicate controls locked.

title: Fees and refusal
content: The committed schedule prices activity type, encoded bytes, execution, storage, Asset operations, and module operations, then applies its basis-point multiplier with ceiling rounding. Fee estimates expose their schedule and snapshot but reserve nothing. Set an integer fee_limit and maintain spendable fee balance for that limit. An admission refusal consumes no sequence and charges no fee. An admitted activity that fails consumes its sequence, emits a failure receipt, rolls back module effects, and may charge up to the fee limit. Protocol fees go to system:fees ; Programs occupancy rent is a separate batch settlement.

title: Continue building
content: Make your first payment Assets and token accounts Public payment API x402 transport Fee schedules

title: Perpetual Futures
content: Trade long and short exposure with explicit margin accounts, deterministic funding, signed market prices, and accountable liquidation settlement. Trade long and short exposure with explicit margin accounts, deterministic funding, signed market prices, and accountable liquidation settlement.

title: A market is a complete risk configuration
content: Paxeer X perpetual markets combine an order book with position, margin, funding, insurance, and liquidation state. Every market identifies its quote asset, administrator, liquidity account, long and short funding accounts, and insurance account. Losses, fees, funding, and margin releases settle through conserved transfer legs in the shared ledger. Parameter group What it controls Contract size, tick size, lot size, price scale Contract units, valid price and quantity increments, and integer price interpretation. Initial and maintenance margin ratios Collateral required to open exposure and the threshold used by maintenance checks. Liquidation fee and liquidator share The fee charged during liquidation and its division between the liquidator and insurance. Funding interval and maximum rate Accrual cadence and the permitted funding-rate magnitude. Oracle keys, freshness, bounds, deviation Which signed observations are acceptable for the market. Parameter version and halt state The configuration revision and whether risk-taking operations are permitted. Initial margin must exceed maintenance margin. Market accounts are distinct, and the permitted oracle set contains up to eight canonical keys. Read the selected market configuration before sizing an order; ratios, intervals, and limits belong to the market rather than a universal exchange default.

title: Open, increase, and close exposure
content: Select a market and inspect its quote asset, price scale, lot size, margin ratios, oracle observation, and halt state. Fund your main account with the required quote asset and choose a dedicated margin account. Place a buy or sell order with a price and quantity, or submit a position-open activity with side, size, entry notional, and margin amount. Opening transfers posted margin from the owner main account into the position margin account. Increase an existing position with explicit size, notional, and margin deltas. Monitor accepted prices, accrued funding, margin, and the market maintenance threshold. Close the position to settle exposure and release eligible remaining margin. Buy positions express long exposure; sell positions express short exposure. Orders have explicit owner and order identifiers, and cancellations identify both the market and order. A rejected activity does not become an executed position: inspect its receipt before updating a trading interface.

title: Leverage and initial margin
content: Leverage is notional exposure divided by posted margin. A hypothetical market with a 1,000-basis-point initial margin ratio requires at least 1,000 quote units for 10,000 quote units of opening notional, corresponding to 10× exposure at that minimum. Posting 2,000 quote units lowers that ratio to 5×. These figures illustrate the calculation; the selected market defines the actual requirements.

title: Profit and loss
content: For a long position, price profit or loss follows (mark price − entry price) × size ÷ price scale ; the sign reverses for a short. Integer settlement rounds positive profit down and loss magnitude up when division leaves a remainder. A long with one normalized unit entered at 100 and marked at 105 has five quote units of price profit before funding and fees.

title: Funding follows sealed batch time
content: Funding ticks use the sealed batch timestamp. Only whole configured funding intervals accrue; a tick before the next complete interval is refused. The cumulative funding index advances by the rate multiplied by elapsed intervals, and a position records the index at entry so its accrued funding can be computed from the difference. The funding-rate calculation measures the signed difference between oracle and reference prices relative to the reference price, then caps its magnitude at the market maximum. Positive funding transfers from the long funding account to the short funding account; negative funding reverses that direction. At the position level, positive index movement makes longs pay and shorts receive. Funding payments are rounded conservatively when integer units leave a remainder. For example, 10,000 quote units of entry notional and a positive cumulative change of 20 basis points produce 20 quote units of funding owed by a long, before any rounding effects. The same index movement credits a short of equal entry notional.

title: Maintenance, liquidation, and insurance
content: The maintenance check computes mark notional from current price and size, rounds required maintenance collateral upward, and compares it with the supplied margin balance. A balance strictly below that requirement is liquidatable; equality satisfies that check. Applications should keep price P&L, funding, fees, and collateral accounting visible rather than inferring a liquidation price from leverage alone. Trading loss is paid from the position margin account to market liquidity, up to the available margin. A remaining trading-loss deficit draws on the market insurance account. The liquidation fee is limited by margin remaining after losses and split between the liquidator and insurance account. Any residual margin returns to the owner main account. Insurance is a funded account, not an unlimited guarantee. A liquidation whose deficit exceeds the available insurance balance is refused. Auto-deleveraging accepts an explicitly ordered list of position identifiers. The codec capacity is 128 ( LX_PERPS_ADL_CAPACITY ), but dispatch refuses more than LX_PERPS_DISPATCH_MAX_ADL (16) positions per activity; canonical sorted ordering makes processing deterministic.

title: Activity reference
content: Activity Purpose MARKET_CREATE / MARKET_HALT Create a market configuration or change its halt state. ORACLE_PUSH Submit a signed market price observation. ORDER_PLACE / ORDER_CANCEL Manage explicit buy and sell orders. POSITION_OPEN / POSITION_INCREASE / POSITION_CLOSE Manage exposure and its margin lifecycle. FUNDING_TICK Accrue completed funding intervals. LIQUIDATE / ADL Resolve undercollateralized exposure and ordered deleveraging. Perpetual activities use module identifier 6 and the 0x0006xxxx activity family: 0x00060001 – 0x0006000b for the activities above, plus LX_PERPS_MARGIN_REGISTER at 0x0006000c . A versioned 130-byte time-in-force order payload is also defined ( lx_perps_tif_module_iface ). Unknown ordinals, noncanonical payloads, zero amounts, insufficient margin, unauthorized debits, and halted markets produce explicit refusals.

title: Platform API
content: Accounts, balances, history, assets, registration, funding and consensus evidence over the hosted gateway, plus the Agent API for policy-governed writes. Accounts, balances, history, assets, registration, funding and consensus evidence over the hosted gateway, plus the Agent API for policy-governed writes.

title: Choose an interface
content: The canonical gateway origin is https://api-mainnet-beta.paxeer.network . Use the gateway px_ JSON-RPC methods for account, balance, asset, history and consensus reads, the EVM relay for chain transactions, and the Agent API for preparation, policy and tracking. EVM chain ID 125 identifies the EVM environment. Fetch GET /rpc/schema for the gateway's OpenRPC document ( LayerX public JSON-RPC , version 0.1.0), which is the method contract for the table below. Surface Transport Purpose Gateway RPC POST /rpc Seventeen px_ / pax_sequencerReceipt methods: accounts, balances, assets, history, registration, funding and consensus reads. EVM relay POST /rpc eth_ , net_ and web3_ methods relayed to the chain node, including eth_sendRawTransaction . See EVM JSON-RPC . Agent API Contract major 2, minor 0 Scoped identities, disclosures, approvals, budgets and event streams. The former lx_ native RPC namespace is switched off. Every lx_* method — including lx_getNodeInfo , lx_getAccount , lx_sendActivity and the lx_subscribe / lx_unsubscribe / lx_subscription WebSocket methods — returns -32601 Method not found . There is no gateway equivalent of lx_sendActivity , lx_estimateFee , lx_getProof or lx_getCheckpoint in the current catalogue; use the Agent API write pipeline for governed submission and the EVM relay for raw transactions.

title: Authentication and signing
content: Public gateway reads do not require a gateway key. State-changing JSON-RPC uses Authorization: LayerX-Key <key-id>:<key-secret> with activity:write . Hosted identity sessions use Authorization: Bearer <session-token> . The gateway credential admits an operation; a cryptographic activity signature authorizes the exact protocol action. Use scoped identities and credentials and budget controls .

title: Query gateway state
content: POST /rpc Content-Type: application/json {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"px_getNetwork","params":[]} Parameters are positional, in the order listed. The router recognises exactly the following seventeen methods; any other method returns -32601 . Batches may mix px_ and relayed EVM calls. Method Parameters Purpose px_getNetwork none Network handshake and heads for the unified endpoint. px_getAccount account Authenticated account object for one account. px_resolveAccount account Resolve an account reference to its account record. px_getBalances account Balances held by one account, read through the bank precompile. px_listAssets none Native asset list. px_register signer_public_key , registration_signature Self-registered identity principal. px_requestFunds did , signer_public_key One bounded testnet funding request, authenticated by identity session. pax_sequencerReceipt txHash The node's sequencer receipt and commitment rung, relayed unchanged. px_getCommit , px_getValidators , px_getSequenceBatch height Signed commit, validator set and sequence batch at one block height. px_getReceiptKeys none Published receipt signing keys for local receipt verification. px_getHistory , px_getUnifiedHistory account , optional cursor , limit , kind Paged account history from the indexer read API; the unified variant tags the side each record answers for. px_listHolderRecords address , kind , optional cursor , limit Paged holder records of one kind for one address. px_getCapabilities none Which product surfaces are currently available on this endpoint. px_getRouteCatalogue none Authenticated product route catalogue and dependency readiness. Node-side signing methods ( eth_accounts , eth_coinbase , eth_sendTransaction , eth_sign , eth_signTransaction , eth_signTypedData , eth_signTypedData_v4 , eth_mining ) and eth_subscribe / eth_unsubscribe are refused at the gateway rather than relayed. A raw transaction addressed to a precompile surface that px_getCapabilities reports false is refused with -32003 surface_unavailable ; check capabilities before submitting.

title: Submit through the Agent API
content: The gateway exposes no native activity-submission RPC. Governed writes go through the Agent API pipeline (prepare, sign, submit, track, wait) or the EVM relay as a signed raw transaction. The steps are: Verify the network with px_getNetwork and read the current account state. Prepare canonical activity bytes with an actor, authority, time bounds, fee limit, payload and stable idempotency key. Inspect the decoded disclosure and sign the exact signing preimage. Submit and retain the submission reference, transaction hash and receipt. Verify the evidence — receipt signature against px_getReceiptKeys , then commit and validator set at the landing height — before releasing goods, funds or dependent work.

title: Idempotency and uncertain outcomes
content: A timeout does not establish rejection. Reconcile the existing submission and reuse its idempotency key rather than creating a second payment. Agent mutations return the same result for the same body and key; a changed body under the same key returns IdempotencyConflict .

title: Follow activity
content: There is no gateway subscription RPC: the lx_ subscription methods answer method-not-found on WebSocket connections as well as HTTPS. Poll px_getHistory or px_getUnifiedHistory with a retained cursor for account activity, follow EVM heads and logs on the chain WebSocket endpoints , and use agent subscriptions for durable, acknowledged tenant-scoped streams.

title: Agent event streams
content: Agent subscriptions support create, list, health, acknowledge, pause, resume and delete. Their persisted cursor enables recovery. Scope evaluates tenant, capability, then filters for agents, accounts, activity types, modules, assets, counterparties and result classes. Delivery is at least once: deduplicate by deduplication_id and handle Event, Gap and Truncated variants.

title: Agent API pipeline
content: The wire envelope contains contract major and minor as big-endian u16, request ID as big-endian u64, operation as UTF-8 and a canonical-map payload. Amounts, sequences, limits and timestamps are decimal strings. Settlement domain is Paxeer. Operation Inputs and outcome prepare Actor, authority, account sequence, timestamp bound, idempotency key, fee limit, payload and payload hash produce unsigned canonical bytes, signing preimage, disclosure, preparation reference and expiry. sign , submit Preparation reference and signature bind the signed activity and tracked submission. track Submission reference returns state, evidence, rung and transitions. wait Submission reference, requested rung and deadline return the actual rung and whether the deadline elapsed. Reads read.balance , read.account , read.module_state , read.history , read.batch , read.checkpoint , read.proof_bundle . Availability and projection availability.fetch , export.offline , project . Projection is an estimate rather than a verified read. Submission progresses through Prepared, Signed, Queued, Submitted, Unknown, Executed, Committed, Failed and Expired. Unknown is a first-class pending state. On the wire, progress is reported as one of three rungs — submitted , receipted and committed — and a requested rung above the achieved rung is refused rather than downgraded. Finer internal verification ranks are not part of the Agent API vocabulary.

title: Errors and retries
content: Code Meaning Action -32600 Invalid request envelope. Correct the JSON-RPC framing. -32601 Method not found, including every switched-off lx_* method. Use the published px_ catalogue or the EVM relay. -32003 surface_unavailable : a raw transaction targets a precompile surface reported false by px_getCapabilities . Check capabilities; do not resubmit to a disabled surface. Agent errors distinguish TransportFailure, Deadline, ProtocolIncompatibility, UnavailableCapability, CoreRejection, VerificationFailure, PolicyRefusal, CapabilityRefusal, BudgetRefusal, RateLimit, IdempotencyConflict and InternalFault. Resolve authority and verification failures before retrying. Continue with CLI workflows , SDK integration and EVM JSON-RPC .

title: Precompiles
content: Call native Paxeer X capabilities from the EVM with the correct addresses, ABIs, permissions, and token units. Call native Paxeer X capabilities from the EVM with the correct addresses, ABIs, permissions, and token units. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/precompiles/setup.go and each precompile's abi.json and Go implementation.

title: Kernel and native application precompiles
content: Paxeer X extends the EVM with the LayerX kernel and native financial applications. These addresses share the same 20-byte padding convention as the chain interfaces above. Address Interface Operations 0x1012 LayerX verification verifyEd25519 , verifyReceipt , verifyReceiptInclusion , verifyStateProof , verifyDiscoveryProof 0x1013 Custody Native and token deposits, withdrawal requests and finalisation, deposit-root registration, nullifier queries, forced-exit requests and execution 0x1014 Anchor Checkpoint submission and finality, finalized roots, availability attestations, guarantor bonds, sequencer authorization, challenges, and equivocation evidence 0x1015 Perpetuals addCollateral , addSize , closePosition , executeOrder , cancelOrder , account, balance, and market queries; every method is nonpayable. From the v6.12.0 activation height this address serves the perpetuals venue; below that height it served the v6.9 exchange precompile, so bindings must match the height range they target 0x1016 Bridge bridgeIn , bridgeOut , getChain , getAttestors , getCap , isNullified , isPaused 0x1017 Launchpad Market creation, quotes, buys and sells, reserves and price snapshots, fee strategies, fee claims, burns, airdrops, and LP rewards 0x1018 Fee token setFeeDenom , getFeeDenom , clearFeeDenom select an approved fee denomination. Present only from the v6.7 upgrade 0x1019 XWeb request , fulfil , fulfilProgram , refund , getRequest , getResult , getProgramResult , getKernelNetworkId , attestors, threshold, fee, and parameters. Present only from the v6.8 upgrade 0x1020 Price feed getPrice , getPriceBySymbol , getPrices , market and observation queries, feed-key registration and revocation 0x1021 – 0x1025 Spot (PECOR) Market and swap rail ( 0x1021 ), limit orders ( 0x1022 ), stop orders ( 0x1023 ), read-only quoter ( 0x1024 ), and liquidity vault ( 0x1025 ); see the spot exchange guide

title: Merge and agent-function precompiles
content: The merge upgrade plan brings a further address range online. These entries are withheld below the plan's activation height, and an address with no registered constructor is not served. Address Interface 0x101a layerxledger 0x101b layerxpay 0x101c layerxauth 0x101d layerxprograms 0x101e layerxchains 0x0901 – 0x0908 Agent functions: orob , clearing , oracle aggregator , pofq , scheduler , streams , tee attestor , eip712 Use precompiles/<name>/abi.json and contracts/src/precompiles/ for exact tuple layouts, argument types, mutability, and events. docs/system/precompiles.md indexes the interfaces. A successful write transaction records an operation; check the corresponding checkpoint, claim, intent, or bridge lifecycle before treating it as finalized settlement.

title: One account across execution surfaces
content: The address precompile also exposes bindLayerX , unbindLayerX , layerXBindNonce , getLayerXDid , getEvmAddrByLayerX , and getUnifiedAccount . The unified account returns EVM, Cosmos, DID public key, and LayerX main account identifiers. Binding requires the account signature and current nonce; applications retain each identifier in its native encoding. Continue with XDK for client bindings, settlement for custody and finality, bridge transfers , and assets for denomination and pointer rules.

title: Fixed addresses and interfaces
content: Paxeer X implements precompiles natively in the node. Call them with their matching ABI rather than expecting deployed Solidity bytecode. Match your client bindings to the node revision you use. Address Capability Current interface 0x1001 Bank Native balances, metadata, supply, pointer-authorized sends, native value transfers 0x1002 CosmWasm instantiate , execute , execute_batch , query 0x1003 JSON Extract bytes, byte lists, unsigned integers, and array elements 0x1004 Address association getPaxAddr , getEvmAddr , associate , associatePubKey 0x1005 Staking Delegation and validator transactions, queries, pagination, pool, and parameters 0x1006 Governance vote , voteWeighted , deposit , submitProposal 0x1007 Distribution Reward queries, withdrawals, withdrawal address, and validator commission 0x1008 Oracle Registered, but both price-query methods revert as retired 0x1009 IBC transfer transfer , transferWithDefaultTimeout 0x100a Pointer lookup Native, CW20, CW721, and CW1155 pointer address, version, and existence 0x100b Pointer creation addNativePointer , addCW20Pointer , addCW721Pointer , addCW1155Pointer 0x100c Solo asset claims claim(bytes) , claimSpecific(bytes) using signed Cosmos transaction payloads 0x1011 P-256 signatures verify(bytes) Addresses in the table are shortened for readability. Pad them to 20 bytes, for example 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001001 . precompiles/common/ supplies shared gas, payment, ABI, and error handling; it is not another callable precompile.

title: Address association
content: getPaxAddr(address) resolves an existing EVM-to-Paxeer association. getEvmAddr(string) performs the reverse lookup. Account addresses use pax1 ; validator operator addresses use paxvaloper1 . These lookups can fail when no association exists; they are not interchangeable with a bech32 encoding of the same 20 bytes. The manual association methods derive both addresses from a public key or signature. Use the key belonging to the account being linked. Creating a new random wallet would associate a different account. Signature construction must match the exact message bytes expected by addr.go ; an application timestamp is not a replay-protection mechanism enforced by that method.

title: Bank balances and transfers
content: Bank amounts are integers in the supplied base denomination. The native bank denomination is uhpx : one PAX equals 1,000,000 uhpx , while EVM transaction value uses 10^18 wei per PAX. The internal human-unit identifier is hpx ; see network parameters for the unit mapping. // Minimal ABI for a read; use the full bank/abi.json for other methods. import { Contract, JsonRpcProvider, formatUnits } from 'ethers' const provider = new JsonRpcProvider(process.env.PAXEER_EVM_RPC_URL) if ((await provider.getNetwork()).chainId !== 125n) throw new Error('Wrong chain') const bank = new Contract( '0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001001', ['function balance(address,string) view returns (uint256)', 'function decimals(string) view returns (uint8)'], provider, ) const account = process.env.PAXEER_ACCOUNT_ADDRESS if (!account) throw new Error('Set PAXEER_ACCOUNT_ADDRESS') const amount = await bank.balance(account, 'uhpx') console.log('bank base units:', amount.toString()) console.log('PAX:', formatUnits(amount, 6)) console.log('bank denomination decimals:', await bank.decimals('uhpx')) // 0 bank.decimals(denom) returns 0 because the ABI represents base-denomination integers. It does not return the display exponent of PAX. The name and symbol methods require bank denomination metadata. send(address from, address to, string denom, uint256 amount) is nonpayable and restricted to the registered ERC-20 native pointer for that denomination. An arbitrary wrapper or wallet cannot call it successfully just by supplying a sender. sendNative(string toAddress) is payable, sends EVM value to a Paxeer bech32 recipient, and preserves both whole uhpx and the smaller wei remainder. The caller must be associated; delegatecall is rejected. all_balances(address) and supply(string) also expose base-denomination amounts.

title: Staking and distribution
content: Staking writes act for the immediate caller's associated account. A contract wrapper therefore controls its own position; querying its deployer's delegation does not inspect that position. Delegatecall is rejected. Payable staking methods receive EVM value and convert it into the native staking denomination; amount arguments and query results are denomination integers or fixed-point share and reward values whose exact scale is defined by each method's handler. Read the scale for a method in precompiles/staking/ and precompiles/distribution/ before converting a result for display, and keep delegation shares, pending rewards, and withdrawn amounts as separate quantities. The staking ABI also exposes validator creation and editing; validator, delegation, unbonding, and redelegation queries; historical information; pool ; and params . Read current parameters for unbonding time and entry limits. Paginated queries return a bytes cursor: with ethers, an empty cursor is 0x , whose JavaScript string length is two. Distribution supports setWithdrawAddress , withdrawDelegationRewards , withdrawMultipleDelegationRewards , withdrawValidatorCommission , and rewards . The withdrawal target must be associated. Some validator addresses are indexed strings in EVM events; an indexed string topic is a hash, not the original bech32 text.

title: Governance transactions
content: The governance ABI exposes writes only: vote , voteWeighted , deposit , and submitProposal . Use the native module query APIs to inspect proposals and live deposit or voting parameters. Take the exact argument and message shapes from precompiles/gov/abi.json and gov/handler.go for the node revision you target, and confirm a submission through the native governance queries rather than assuming a particular EVM event.

title: JSON extraction
content: The JSON ABI provides extractAsBytes(bytes,string) , extractAsBytesList(bytes,string) , extractAsUint256(bytes,string) , and extractAsBytesFromArray(bytes,uint16) . Keys select a literal top-level field. To read a nested field, first extract its containing object. Byte-list results preserve each element's JSON representation, including quotes around strings. Decode returned hex bytes before parsing JSON. Integer extraction accepts decimal integers and quoted integer strings, rejects negative or oversized values, and does not implement floating-point conversion. // With json connected to the current precompiles/json/abi.json: const document = toUtf8Bytes(JSON.stringify({ user: { count: '42' }, tags: ['one'] })) const user = await json.extractAsBytes(document, 'user') const count = await json.extractAsUint256(user, 'count') // 42n const tags = await json.extractAsBytesList(document, 'tags') const firstTag = JSON.parse(toUtf8String(tags[0])) // 'one' The helper functions toUtf8Bytes and toUtf8String above are ethers exports. The implementation charges 100 gas per ABI argument byte, excluding the selector; total transaction gas includes other execution and transaction costs.

title: P-256 signature verification
content: At 0x1011 , verify(bytes) takes exactly 160 payload bytes: a 32-byte digest followed by 32-byte r , s , public-key x , and public-key y . Valid signatures return ABI-encoded bytes containing a 32-byte word with value one. Invalid signatures return empty low-level call data rather than an ABI-encoded result; handle that case before decoding. Malformed payload length reverts. This is an ABI call with a dynamic bytes argument. The 160-byte payload occupies 224 argument bytes after its offset and length words, so the precompile charges 224 × 300 = 67,200 precompile execution gas, before other call or transaction costs. P-256 verification is one part of a passkey flow; challenge, origin, authenticator data, and replay handling belong to the complete application ceremony.

title: Cross-runtime and cross-chain calls
content: The CosmWasm guide covers matching the native coin list to payable EVM value. WASM bindings expose calls in the other direction. The IBC guide covers the transfer ABI, which does not expose channel queries. Pointer lookup returns the pointer address, a version, and an existence flag for one supplied native denomination or CosmWasm address. It does not provide a list-all query. Solo claims consume signed Cosmos transaction payloads; they are asset-claim operations rather than a general administrative interface.

title: Retired Oracle API
content: getExchangeRates and getOracleTwaps at 0x1008 revert with oracle precompile is retired; oracle data queries are disabled . See the Oracle module guide for native query interfaces.

title: ABI and failure handling
content: Use the matching precompiles/<name>/abi.json , simulate the real caller and value, and inspect revert data before sending a transaction. Most module precompiles meter native execution dynamically; sample gas figures are not fixed limits. An off-chain read needs no funded signer, while an on-chain call still consumes gas. In particular, address lookup is getPaxAddr in this tree. An SDK package targeting another chain can carry different selectors, chain IDs, prefixes, or addresses even when its API looks similar.
