title: Verify sequencer receipts against trusted keys
content: The platform verifiers take the signed receipt, the raw transaction, and independently trusted receipt keys (key ID, public key, and valid height range). They check the canonical encoding, the sequencer signature, and that the Keccak-256 hash of the raw transaction matches the receipt. Supplying keys from the same untrusted response as the receipt does not establish independent trust. The TypeScript Commitment type is "submitted" | "receipted" | "committed" . The values executed , batched , and finalised are retired and are rejected as invalid; the only verification rungs are receipted and committed . The Rust kernel-batch verifier above is the exception and follows its own AuthorizedBatch contract.

title: Programs terminal evidence
content: A Programs CALL receipt commits to one runtime terminal. Verify the receipt first, then check the terminal payload against its receipt commitments before acting on a program outcome. There is no public cross-SDK terminal-verifier function with a single shared name. The previously documented entry points ( decode_and_verify_program_terminal , decodeAndVerifyProgramTerminal , verifyProgramTerminal , ProgramsClient.verifyTerminal , ProgramsClient.VerifyTerminal , and Swift verifyTerminal ) are retired, unexported, package-private, private, or internal. On the JVM the public entry point is ProgramsClient.verifyTerminalV5 . In other languages, verify the sequencer receipt and the commitments it carries, and confirm any terminal-decoding helper in your SDK source before depending on it. Continue with XDK API families , Programs , and MCP tools .

title: Cosmos SDK Fork
content: Paxeer X’s in-tree Cosmos SDK fork with Paxeer X-specific modifications and extensions. Paxeer X’s in-tree Cosmos SDK fork with Paxeer X-specific modifications and extensions. Source: Paxeer-X-Network/sdk/

title: Choose the right development surface
content: Paxeer X has three complementary SDK surfaces. The in-tree Cosmos SDK powers paxd and native chain modules. The XDK provides application-facing clients for LayerX transactions, proofs, identity, exchange, bridge, launchpad, and native precompile calls. The platform API connects paid resources, merchant checkout, agent spending, receipts, and webhooks. Chain maintainers work in sdk/ , modules/ , and node/ . Application developers use services/agent/sdk/ (TypeScript, Python), services/agent/crates/layerx-sdk (Rust), sdk/platform/ (Go, JVM, Swift, .NET), and sdk/wallet . docs/system/sdk.md indexes exported SDK symbols and their source paths.

title: Cross-surface application lifecycle
content: Resolve the unified EVM, Cosmos, and LayerX identity and select the asset denomination or pointer. Use the matching client or native ABI to deposit custody funds, submit an intent, transfer an asset, or create a market. Track transaction receipts together with kernel receipts, checkpoint finality, and withdrawal or settlement status. Verify proofs against the appropriate finalized root before fulfilling a payment or releasing funds. The network overview explains how these execution surfaces compose. An EVM transaction receipt and a finalized kernel checkpoint represent different stages of an application lifecycle.

title: Overview
content: Paxeer X vendors a fork of the Cosmos SDK directly in the monorepo under Paxeer-X-Network/sdk/ . This is not a published Go module or npm package. It is an in-tree dependency for the paxd binary and Paxeer chain modules.

title: Why a Fork?
content: Paxeer X maintains a fork to support: Custom storage engines EVM integration and pointer contracts Fast iteration without waiting for upstream releases Paxeer X-specific consensus and execution optimizations Co-location with Paxeer modules and WASM runtime

title: Upstream Base
content: The fork is based on Cosmos SDK but diverges significantly. It is not compatible with upstream Cosmos SDK releases without careful rebasing and testing. Warning: Do not assume drop-in compatibility with standard Cosmos SDK tooling or libraries. Paxeer X’s SDK is a custom fork.

title: Directory Structure
content: Path Purpose baseapp/ Application framework (ABCI, routing, ante handlers) client/ CLI framework and transaction builders server/ Node server, gRPC, REST gateway types/ Core SDK types (messages, coins, errors, context) x/ Standard Cosmos modules (bank, auth, staking, gov, etc.) proto/ Protobuf definitions for SDK modules store/ State store abstraction and implementations storev2/ , codec/ , crypto/ Store v2, codec, and cryptography support platform/ , wallet/ , js/ Platform language SDKs, wallet, and JavaScript support

title: Key Modules
content: Paxeer X’s SDK includes standard Cosmos modules: Module Purpose x/auth Account authentication and transaction signing x/bank Token transfers and balance management x/staking Proof-of-Stake validator set and delegation x/distribution Staking rewards and fee distribution x/gov On-chain governance and proposals x/slashing Validator penalties for misbehavior x/authz , x/feegrant Authorization grants and fee grants x/capability , x/genutil , x/simulation Capability keeper, genesis utilities, and simulation x/evidence Double-sign evidence submission x/params Module parameter management x/upgrade Coordinated chain upgrades Plus Paxeer X-specific modules under Paxeer-X-Network/modules/ : evm — EVM execution and JSON-RPC epoch — Epoch tracking oracle , pricefeed — Price feeds tokenfactory — Custom token creation mint — Token minting launchpad , spot , perps , sequencer , store , xweb , lxphost layerxagent , layerxanchor , layerxauth , layerxbridge , layerxchains , layerxcustody , layerxexchange , layerxgov , layerxledger , layerxpay

title: BaseApp
content: The core application framework ( baseapp/ ) handles: ABCI interface to Tendermint consensus Message routing to module handlers Ante handlers (gas, signatures, nonces) Transaction execution and state commits Query routing Paxeer extends BaseApp for EVM transaction routing and concurrent execution (OCC).

title: Client & Server
content: The SDK provides: CLI: paxd command-line interface (transaction builders, queries) gRPC: Module query and transaction services REST: HTTP gateway (gRPC-Gateway) Tendermint RPC: Block and transaction queries See REST & gRPC for API documentation.

title: State Store
content: The SDK's store/ abstraction is implemented by Paxeer X’s custom storage engines. The engine implementations live under storage/ : Database engines under storage/db_engine/ : litt , pebbledb , rocksdb , and dbcache . See Storage for engine details.

title: Protobuf Definitions
content: SDK types are defined in sdk/proto/ . Regenerate Go code with: cd Paxeer-X-Network ./scripts/protoc.sh The script builds the pinned protoc-gen-gocosmos plugin and runs buf generate via go run github.com/bufbuild/buf/cmd/buf@v1.58.0 . See Paxeer-X-Network/api/README.md .

content: Paxeer modules import the SDK from the in-tree path: import ( sdk "github.com/Sidiora-Labs/Paxeer-X-Network/sdk/types" "github.com/Sidiora-Labs/Paxeer-X-Network/sdk/store" ) There is no sdk/go.mod : the SDK packages belong to the single root module github.com/Sidiora-Labs/Paxeer-X-Network , so no replacement directives are needed.

Test thoroughly: Edit code under sdk/ Rebuild paxd : make paxeer-build Run unit tests: make test Test with Docker cluster : make docker-cluster-start Run integration tests: make human-test-integration (there is no test-integration target)

title: Differences from Upstream Cosmos SDK
content: Paxeer X’s SDK fork diverges from upstream in several areas: Custom storage backends EVM module integration and pointer contracts Optimistic concurrency control (OCC) for parallel execution Receipt indexing and synthetic transactions Paxeer X-specific ante handlers and gas metering Chain-specific upgrade logic Do not assume compatibility with standard Cosmos SDK tooling (e.g., CosmJS, Keplr) without testing.

title: Security and trust boundaries
content: What signatures, replay, checkpoint settlement, custody controls, and authority services establish in Paxeer X. What signatures, replay, checkpoint settlement, custody controls, and authority services establish in Paxeer X. Paxeer X separates fast ordered execution from settlement and custody. A receipt establishes a specific execution claim; its inclusion evidence, sequencer authorization, guarantor certificate, and settlement state determine how that claim is verified. Applications preserve these distinctions when releasing goods, updating balances, or permitting withdrawals.

title: The trust boundaries
content: Boundary Verification responsibility Remaining dependency Actor to sequencer Canonical activity encoding, actor signature, authority scope, sequence, and fee rules. Key custody and correctly scoped delegation. Sequencer to client Authorized header signature, receipt inclusion, batch identity, and outcome. Sequencer availability and the requested evidence level. Sealed batch to guarantor Availability proofs, deterministic replay, and root comparison. Accessible batch data and eligible honest guarantors. Checkpoint to Paxeer Domain-bound eligible attestations and registry acceptance. Settlement-chain execution and configured challenge and withdrawal rules. Application to hosted authority Authenticated request and pinned identities; verify the resulting receipt facts. Authority and replica availability.

title: Evidence levels are consequential
content: Distinguish acceptance, execution, attestation, and settlement as separate evidence levels: acceptance is an ordering receipt, attestation adds bonded replay, and settlement registers the checkpoint on Paxeer. The gateway exposes executed-state handling; use the evidence level required by the application rather than interpreting every successful response as settlement. A canonical L0–L4 naming ladder and a complete commitment-level enum were not verified in source and are not asserted here. Custody remains on Paxeer. Guarantor bonds, challenge windows, withdrawal limits, and emergency exits bound settlement risk under their configured rules. The checkpoint path uses bonded re-execution and does not claim a SNARK or another validity proof.

title: Canonical execution and replay
content: The append-only activity log is the execution record. Indexes are derived views. Replay checks actor authority, receipts, state transitions, recovery metadata, and roots. Consensus execution excludes floating point, local-clock dependence, and unstable iteration so independent machines reproduce identical bytes. Program monetary effects are represented as transfer sets in the same history; they are not private balance writes outside the protocol. Storage occupancy is also replay-checkable. Missing availability data or inconsistent replay results prevent a guarantor from signing.

title: Verify hosted receipt authority
content: The hosted authority obtains a canonical receipt and requests evidence from a pinned replica. It checks the replica identity, pinned sequencer public key, signed header, Merkle inclusion, protocol version, sequence range, and re-derived execution batch identifier. Outcome verification then runs against these derived batch facts.

title: Authorized batch facts
content: The hosted authority references an authenticated authorized-batches route ( GET /v1/authorized-batches/by-activity/{activity_id} ) for derived batch facts. Its exact response schema was not verified in authority source (only README/test references were found) and is not specified here; read the deployed service's contract before depending on field names. Start with the exact activity identifier and the intended network and wire version. Retrieve the canonical receipt and authorized evidence through the configured authenticated service. Verify the receipt against the derived batch facts and the application's expected outcome. Require the appropriate checkpoint and settlement evidence for the action being authorized. A valid signature over a different batch does not establish inclusion for the requested activity. A root copied from an unverified response does not establish authorized execution.

title: Refusals and retry behavior
content: Treat authentication failures, unknown activities, refused evidence, and unavailable dependencies as distinct outcomes: fix credentials for the first, confirm the identifier for the second, do not retry refused evidence as if it were transient, and retry dependency outages with backoff. Exact status codes and error strings for the authorized-batches route were not verified in source and are not listed here. Service readiness probes the replica, and liveness reports process availability. Neither response certifies a particular activity or proves that the sequencer is reachable.

title: Keys, roles, and custody
content: Owner signatures, session grants, delegated capabilities, and budget allowances carry distinct authority scopes. Revocation and primary-key rotation are ordered governance events. Grant only the operations, assets, budgets, and lifetime the application needs, and verify recovery and signer history when evaluating authority. Guarantor membership, bond control, custody authority, checkpoint publication authority, and settlement submission are separate responsibilities. The live guarantor model is the Go layerxanchor Cosmos module (see Guarantors ), not a GuarantorBond contract. A funded submitter can publish an authorized certificate; funding does not give it the ability to manufacture eligible attestations or owner authorization.

title: Emergency response and upgrade control
content: Protocol emergency controls identify their scope, trigger, exit conditions, epoch, and ordered sequence. Settlement timelocks restrict proposers, executors, guardians, target selectors, call value, delays, and execution windows. Layer X component attestations identify role, configuration, release, and layout; upgrade authority follows the specific component or proxy path. During a stall, preserve the latest verified receipts, inclusion proofs, batch data, and checkpoint evidence. Determine the last established commitment level before proceeding with settlement or exit workflows. A loss of service availability must not be interpreted as a successful state transition.

title: Integration review
content: Pin network, protocol version, sequencer authorization, and settlement domain. Reject noncanonical encodings, unexpected response fields, and evidence bound to another activity or batch. Make retries idempotent and preserve the original activity identifier. Distinguish transport success, verified execution, checkpoint attestation, and settlement. Inspect deployed role assignments, thresholds, delays, and limits as part of the application's risk policy. Continue with Guarantors , Governance , and Finality .

title: Sequencing & Finality
content: Follow an activity from deterministic ordering into a sealed, signed batch, and request the evidence your application needs. Follow an activity from deterministic ordering into a sealed, signed batch, and request the evidence your application needs. Paxeer X combines the LayerX activity execution plane with Paxeer custody. Activities are ordered into signed batches and replicas preserve the sealed history for replay. A normal payment or agent action does not require a separate settlement-chain transaction. The layerx-merge upgrade ( v7.0 ) retired the separate sequencer, checkpoint, and guarantor settlement plane. The native sequencer recovery, equivocation, loss, and handover interfaces no longer exist in the kernel, and checkpoint submission to the Paxeer anchor returns a module-retired error. Sections below describe the live ordering and batch-evidence path; see Checkpoints for the retired anchor surface.

title: Global ordering and signed batches
content: Admitted activities receive contiguous global sequence numbers. A batch begins immediately after the previous batch’s last sequence and extends the state-root chain. A sequence gap, a reversed range, or a mismatched previous root refuses the batch. Account sequences enforce each actor’s own ordering alongside the network-wide sequence. Header commitment Fields Protocol and network protocol_version , network_id , epoch Ordered range batch_number , first_sequence , last_sequence State transition previous_state_root , resulting_state_root Execution evidence activity_merkle_root , receipt_merkle_root , event_merkle_root Reconstruction inputs data_availability_root , oracle_root Time and signer Batch timestamp and sequencer_id ; the native header stores time in timestamp_ms . The canonical header contains exactly these 15 fields, encodes to 354 bytes, and is signed by the key bound to the authorized sequencer identity. Batch time is the only time consulted during execution. Protocol-3 batches append an LXP/batch-maintenance/v1 receipt and an LXP/batch-maintenance-effects/v1 event leaf after activity leaves, including an empty effects frame when no maintenance module is enabled.

title: Evidence stages
content: Level Evidence Responsibility L0 · Accepted The ordered activity has a receipt chained to its state root. Inclusion and ordering. L1 · Sealed The signed batch fixes ordering and committed roots. Replica preservation of sealed bytes. L2 · Distributed The batch and availability bundle are retrievable for independent replay. Availability of the material needed for replay. Earlier designs extended this ladder with bonded guarantor attestation (L3) and checkpoint registration on Paxeer (L4). That settlement plane is retired: a receipt’s existence does not imply Paxeer checkpoint settlement, and applications must not wait for or require anchor registration. Certificates and attestations in historical data used the distinct domains LXP/v2/checkpoint-certificate and LXP/v2/guarantor-attestation , each with its terminating zero byte.

title: Replay
content: Retrieve the complete batch body: activities, receipts, events, oracle inputs, state-diff material, and recovery metadata. Verify actor, grant, oracle, and sequencer signatures. Replay from the previous state root using the committed protocol and parameters. Recompute every committed root and compare the canonical results byte for byte. Any disagreement stops acceptance of that replay. Deterministic execution excludes local clocks, floating point, and unstable iteration, so identical ordered input reproduces identical receipts and roots.

title: Public commitment levels
content: Submission uses the exact names executed , batched , and finalised . These are evidence requirements alongside the lifecycle stages. Requested level Required evidence executed A verified canonical receipt for the submitted activity. batched Execution evidence plus an authenticated receipt proof whose canonical value exactly matches the receipt. finalised Batch evidence plus finalised checkpoint evidence whose canonical header exactly matches the proof’s signed batch header. The gateway never downgrades the requested assurance. If its bounded wait cannot establish the requested commitment, it returns an error rather than a weaker success. Preserve the original signed activity and recover through lx_getActivityStatus , lx_getReceipt , and the required proof reads. An acknowledgement, HTTP 202, or activity identifier alone is not an executed receipt. The accepted spelling is finalised .

title: Data availability and recovery
content: A state root without its reconstruction material is insufficient. Retrieval must re-hash to the committed availability roots. Missing data prevents independent replay from accepting the batch. After a crash, recovery reads the durable log head, loads a usable snapshot, replays committed records, compares roots, and rebuilds disposable projections.

title: Equivocation
content: Two different signed batches at one batch number, or two activities at one global sequence, are conflicting histories. The later conflicting batch is refused. There is no native sequencer equivocation, loss, recovery, or handover interface in the current kernel; those entry points were retired with the separate sequencer plane.

title: The Paxeer custody boundary
content: Economic rules for orders, service delivery, escrow, and ordinary transfers execute in LayerX. Custody operations on Paxeer consume proven facts from the executed history. Deposits credit against proven custody facts. Withdrawals debit LayerX first and pay on Paxeer at most once. If Paxeer is unreachable, ordinary LayerX execution continues. Paxeer payouts wait for settlement connectivity. Applications should choose their commitment requirement according to the value and reversibility of the action they release.

title: Continue reading
content: Deterministic kernel execution Checkpoints (retired anchor) Data availability and reconstruction Deposits, withdrawals, and exits Receipt and proof verification Paxeer consensus

title: Services and agreements
content: Publish paid capabilities, agree on deliverables, attest execution, and resolve delivery through the Paxeer X service lifecycle. Publish paid capabilities, agree on deliverables, attest execution, and resolve delivery through the Paxeer X service lifecycle. Paxeer X turns a service into a verifiable agreement between a provider and a customer. An offer defines price, Asset, terms, deliverable specification, deadlines, and acceptance policy. Agreements bind those terms to an escrow; commitments and execution attestations establish the work performed; delivery records bind the resulting artifacts to their availability references.

title: Choose a service model
content: Model Use it for Completion evidence Deliverable agreement Research, generated assets, analysis, computation, and agent tasks. Commitments, signed tool execution, delivery hashes, acceptance or dispute ruling. Paid API Immediate access to a query result, data resource, or tool endpoint. Verified payment receipt and a durable fulfillment record. Metered or recurring API Usage draws and subscription periods authorized by a payer grant. A distinct signed receive activity for each draw or renewal. Use the service module for negotiated work with delivery and acceptance. Use paid API middleware for an HTTP resource that releases its response after receipt verification. Both use the native payment plane; the service module itself does not modify balances.

title: Register and discover an offer
content: Publish an offer with LX_SERVICE_OFFER_PUBLISH . Give customers the offer identifier and a human-readable description of its terms and deliverable specification. Content hashes commit to the exact documents; host the documents and artifacts where the customer can retrieve and verify them. Discovery identifies a suitable offer; the customer checks its Asset, price, expiry, and policy before proposing an agreement. Offer field Meaning offer_id , asset_id , price Nonzero offer identity, payment Asset identity, and positive integer price. terms_hash Commitment to the terms the customer accepts. deliverable_specification_hash Commitment to the expected result. delivery_deadline , offer_expiry Delivery limit and the offer validity boundary. acceptance_window , dispute_window Nonzero windows controlling review and disputes. default_outcome 1 accepts or 2 rejects when the review policy applies. Withdraw an offer with LX_SERVICE_OFFER_WITHDRAW . An unavailable offer or mismatched terms prevents a new agreement from proceeding.

title: From offer to invocation
content: Read the offer and verify the terms and deliverable documents against their hashes. Prepare payment escrow through the payment lifecycle and retain its identifier. Propose an agreement with agreement_id , offer_id , terms_hash , and escrow_id using LX_SERVICE_AGREEMENT_PROPOSE . The provider accepts with LX_SERVICE_AGREEMENT_ACCEPT . Commit a task using LX_SERVICE_COMMIT_TASK , binding its task hash, escrow, positive deadline, and resource bound. Execute the agreed capability, publish signed execution attestations, and report progress. Deliver artifacts for customer acceptance; resolve escrow through the payment lifecycle.

title: Commitments and execution attestations
content: A task commitment records commitment_id , agreement_id , task_hash , escrow_id , deadline , and resource_bound . An abandoned commitment carries an explicit reason through LX_SERVICE_COMMIT_ABANDON . LX_SERVICE_TOOL_EXEC_ATTEST records the tool identifier, input and output commitments, execution window, resource units, attestor identity, availability reference, public key, and signature. Verification checks the attestor; invalid signatures or execution evidence are refused as LXP_ERR_INVALID_ATTESTATION . LX_SERVICE_PROGRESS_REPORT binds a report and note hash to a commitment and availability reference. Progress is an integer from 1 through 10000 basis points. Progress cannot regress.

title: Deliver and review
content: LX_SERVICE_DELIVER carries one to sixteen artifacts. Each item contains a hash, a positive byte size, and a nonzero availability reference; a zero size or zero availability reference is refused as non-canonical. Every deliverable hash must equal the offer's deliverable_specification_hash , and delivery must arrive by the agreement deadline. Delivery is accepted from the committed state and again from the rejected state, which permits redelivery after rejection. Retain the bytes corresponding to every declared hash so the customer can verify the result. delivery_id32 || agreement_id32 || count:u8 || { hash32 || artifact_size:u64 || availability_reference32 } × count The customer accepts with LX_SERVICE_ACCEPT or rejects using LX_SERVICE_REJECT , a rejection reason, and contested hashes. Protocol batch maintenance applies the agreement's default review policy when the acceptance window ends.

title: Disputes and resolution
content: LX_SERVICE_DISPUTE_OPEN binds a dispute identifier and evidence hashes to the agreement. The agreement must be in the rejected state, the raiser must be the provider or the buyer, the escrow link must match the agreement, and the escrow must name a nonzero arbiter ( LXP_ERR_ARBITER_REQUIRED ); the dispute must open within its window. LX_SERVICE_DISPUTE_RESOLVE must come from that escrow arbiter ( LXP_ERR_UNAUTHORIZED_ARBITER for any other caller) and supplies a nonzero ruling, the provider's allocation in basis points, and the escrow resolution identifier. Allocation ranges from zero to 10000 .

title: Activity reference
content: The service module ID is 5 ; record version is 1 , encoded by the prefix bytes 00 01 . Identifiers and hashes are 32 bytes. Submit canonical activities through the native protocol path. Activity Type Payload bytes including version Offer publish / withdraw 0x00050001 / 0x00050002 179 / 34 Agreement propose / accept 0x00050003 / 0x00050004 130 / 34 Task commit / abandon 0x00050005 / 0x00050006 146 / 36 Tool execution attest / progress 0x00050007 / 0x00050008 Variable / 134 Deliver / accept 0x00050009 / 0x0005000a 67 + 72 per item / 34 Reject / dispute open 0x0005000b / 0x0005000c 37 + 32 per hash / 67 + 32 per hash Dispute resolve 0x0005000d 72

title: Handle refusals and retries
content: Preserve the agreement, commitment, activity, and escrow identifiers across retries. Check status before resubmission after a timeout. Sequence reuse, unauthorized debit, unavailable offers, terms mismatch, and invalid agreement state are distinct refusals; changing payment identity to escape uncertainty can create a second economic action. Delivery errors distinguish LXP_ERR_DELIVERABLE_MISMATCH (a hash that does not equal the specification hash), non-canonical zero sizes or availability references, and LXP_ERR_DELIVERY_DEADLINE_PASSED . Dispute errors distinguish an unauthorized actor from a closed window. Correct the refused condition before submitting a new action.

title: Continue building
content: Connect immediate resource access with paid APIs and x402 , explore SDK integrations , and inspect the protocol modules .

title: Checkpoint settlement & evidence
content: Follow LayerX activities from ordered receipts to bonded replay, finalized Paxeer checkpoints, and verifiable custody claims. Follow LayerX activities from ordered receipts to bonded replay, finalized Paxeer checkpoints, and verifiable custody claims.

title: Execution and settlement form one history
content: Paxeer X settles LayerX activity on EVM chain ID 125 . The sequencer orders activities; guarantors independently replay sealed batches; Paxeer records the resulting checkpoints and enforces custody releases. Payments, program calls, program-owned transfers, and storage occupancy charges participate in the same deterministic history. Level Evidence Meaning L0 · Accepted Sequencer receipt The activity is ordered in the current batch and bound to a state transition. L1 · Sealed Fixed batch history Ordering is fixed and the batch is ready for distribution. L2 · Distributed Batch and availability bundle Guarantors receive the material needed for independent replay. L3 · Attested Bonded guarantor certificate Guarantors attest byte-identical replay results. L4 · Settled Paxeer checkpoint Settlement custody enforces finality, challenge windows, withdrawal limits, and exits. A guarantor attestation is bonded re-execution evidence. Its security combines bonds, challenges, availability checks, and release limits. Applications retain the receipt for the fast path and follow the same activity into settlement evidence before presenting settled funds.

title: Native checkpoint anchor
content: The layerxanchor precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001014 records checkpoints, finality, availability attestations, and guarantor bonds. Anyone can submit a self-verifying checkpoint certificate. Finalization requires the configured threshold of active bonded guarantors, continuity with the finalized chain, no open challenge, and completion of the challenge window. Method Purpose submitCheckpoint(header, headerSignature, certificate) Admit a canonical 354-byte header, 64-byte sequencer signature, and guarantor certificate. submitAvailabilityAttestation(attestation) Record a 274-byte attestation for a known checkpoint. finalize(batchNumber) Finalize a checkpoint after its challenge conditions clear. latestFinalized() , checkpoint(batchNumber) Read finalized progress and full checkpoint metadata. finalizedStateRoot(batchNumber) , finalizedReceiptRoot(batchNumber) Retrieve roots together with their finality flags. openChallenge(batchNumber, kind, evidenceHash) Open a bonded fraud or data-availability challenge. submitEquivocation(evidenceA, evidenceB) Present conflicting guarantor attestations for slashing. Anchor status is 0 unknown, 1 submitted, or 2 final. Read the finality flag with a root; the existence of a root alone does not establish payout eligibility. The exact interface is precompiles/layerxanchor/LayerXAnchor.sol .

title: Deposit-root registration
content: The custody precompile ( ILayerXCustody ) records the deposit root of a finalized checkpoint with registerDepositRoot(registration, signature, leafOrdering) . Only the account that submitted the checkpoint to the anchor may call it. No settlement publication contract exposing an EVIDENCE_VERSION or withdrawal/balance witness vectors exists in the current contracts; do not build against one. Item Contents Commitment Deposit root registration Registration bytes, deposit-root authority signature, and positional leaf ordering. The ordering is committed to, not verified by the precompile. SHA256(abi.encode(uint16(2), registration, signature, leafOrdering)) , read back with depositRegistrationDigest(checkpointId) Registration records evidence; payout still requires the custody checks on the claim path. Use depositRootRegistered(checkpointId) and depositRootAuthority() to inspect registration state.

title: Independent signing roles
content: A separately configured Ed25519 deposit-root authority signs the registration. Guarantors attest replay. A guarantor key cannot substitute for the deposit-root authority. Deposit-root registration: "LX:PAXEER:DEPOSIT:ROOT:v1" || checkpoint_id32 || checkpoint_state_root32 || deposit_root32 || custody_reference32 || network_id:u32 (4 bytes) || protocol_version:u16 (2 bytes) The signature argument is the deposit-root authority's Ed25519 signature over those registration bytes. An Ed25519 public key is not converted into an EVM address.

title: Producer and consumer workflow
content: Replay native history independently and construct the deposit evidence for the checkpoint. Obtain the configured deposit-root authority's signature over the registration bytes. Submit and finalize the checkpoint at the anchor, then call registerDepositRoot from the checkpoint submitter account. Verify depositRootRegistered and depositRegistrationDigest before treating the deposit root as recorded. Apply claim-specific custody checks and verify the final payout on the custody path.

title: Verify the transport and the money
content: Settlement clients verify endpoint TLS trust and chain identity before consuming evidence. A healthy process or matching chain ID establishes connectivity, while finalized checkpoint evidence establishes the settlement claim. Do not elevate one finality level merely because an earlier stage succeeded. Continue with deposits, withdrawals, and emergency exits , Paxeer consensus , and native EVM interfaces .

title: Sidiora
content: The SID asset on Paxeer X: native balances, its stable ERC-20 address, bridge-controlled supply, and sponsored or native gas payments. The SID asset on Paxeer X: native balances, its stable ERC-20 address, bridge-controlled supply, and sponsored or native gas payments.

title: Asset Identity
content: Sidiora is the second official coin of Paxeer X. Its native denomination and ERC-20 interface represent one asset, giving wallets, contracts and Cosmos applications a consistent balance model. Property Value Symbol SID Decimals 6 ; one SID is 1,000,000 base units ERC-20 address 0x21f7b20a555199fa73A238B1a91FD0f549068fEe Native denom factory/pax1dzfx9mk4fl9kl2mysjmtvk2xp75ljumk6nynhf/usid Mint and burn authority The x/layerxbridge module account Proxy administration Governance through a restricted upgrade timelock PAX uses the base denom uhpx and eighteen decimals. Keep SID and PAX scaling separate in displays, approvals, transfer amounts, fee quotations and accounting. Read supply from the native bank state or ERC-20 totalSupply for a current value.

title: One Asset Across Native and EVM Interfaces
content: The native ERC-20 implementation reads balanceOf from the bank balance of the SID denom and totalSupply from its bank supply. Transfers move that denom through the bank precompile. A failed bank operation reverts the contract call. The pointer record resolves the denom to the same stable ERC-20 address. The proxy address remains constant through implementation upgrades. Native token metadata and allowances use an ERC-7201 storage namespace that preserves legacy implementation slots. Applications query current allowances before building spending transactions and request the approval required by the current interface.

title: Bridge-Controlled Supply
content: The bridge module account administers the tokenfactory denom. Attested bridge-in credits mint SID and bridge-out operations burn the departing amount. Denom creation verifies the bridge-derived creator, expected admin and remote asset mapping. Ordinary holders and application contracts have no minting authority.

title: Two Ways to Pay Gas in SID
content: Property Sponsored gas Native fee preference Execution EIP-7702 account batch and quote service Chain fee processing SID payment Atomic transfer to the sponsor inside the batch Fee debit in SID before execution Pricing Signed quote checked against the paymaster rate Governance-controlled conversion rate Replay protection Account batch nonce and sponsor quote nonce Normal transaction replay protection and account preference Unused gas Governed by the signed sponsorship quote Refunded in the selected fee denom PAX transaction value The account still supplies value it sends The account still supplies value it sends

title: Sponsored Transaction Workflow
content: Build the application calls and request a sponsor quote for the declared gas cost. Verify the configured sponsor, SID token, six-decimal units, chain ID, deadline, quoted amount and maximum. Sign the account batch, covering its nonce, calls hash and quote digest, and authorize the EIP-7702 execution. Execute through BatchCallAndSponsor ; the account runs the calls and repays the sponsor in SID in the same transaction. The sponsor signature binds chain ID, paymaster, sponsor, token, maximum amount, offered amount, deadline, quote nonce and declared gas cost. The account signature must recover to the account itself. Used quote nonces and account batch nonces prevent replay.

title: Pricing and Atomicity
content: The paymaster checks a positive, sufficiently fresh rate and requires the offered amount to fall within five percent of the amount implied by the declared gas cost. Expired quotes, zero amounts, an incorrect token or invalid sponsor are refused. A failed application call or SID repayment reverts the whole batch. Quote services apply their own budget and rate-freshness limits before signing a quote. Missing or invalid pricing inputs produce a refusal. Validate the returned quote and signatures locally before building executeSponsored .

title: Native Fee Preferences
content: The fee-token precompile at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001018 exposes the account preference: function setFeeDenom(string calldata denom) external; function getFeeDenom(address account) external view returns (string memory denom); function clearFeeDenom() external; Call setFeeDenom with the SID native denom to select it for the caller, query with getFeeDenom , or clear the preference to return to the network coin. Only allowed fee denoms can be selected. The precompile rejects value and delegatecall; static calls cannot change preferences.

title: Charging and Refunding
content: For EVM transactions, fee processing converts the maximum gas charge, including a blob fee when applicable, into the chosen denom. The account must have sufficient spendable SID for that charge and sufficient PAX for any transferred value. The fee debit replaces the PAX gas purchase. Unused gas returns in the same denom. Cosmos transactions can offer allowed fee denoms, whose governed conversion is used for minimum-gas-price checks.

title: Governed Rates and Fee Routing
content: Fee conversion uses a governance-controlled rate for each allowed denom. Only allowed fee denoms can be selected through the fee-token precompile. Applications read the current fee parameters before presenting a fee option, and re-estimate when a rate or policy changes. PAX fees keep their ordinary collection path through the fee collector.

title: Upgrade Authority
content: The Sidiora proxy timelock accepts only governance-scheduled upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes) operations targeting the proxy with zero value. The implementation must be a contract distinct from the proxy and timelock. Upgrade and initialization execute together. A designated executor runs an operation after its delay and within its grace period. A guardian can cancel before readiness. The handover governance proposal specifies a minimum delay of 172,800 seconds (two days), a delay floor of 86,400 seconds (one day) and an execution grace period of 604,800 seconds (one week). These delays are governance and constructor parameters, not constants in the token contract. These controls bound implementation changes while preserving the token address.

title: Integration Checklist
content: Use six-decimal SID amounts and query the current balance and allowance. Resolve the native denom and stable ERC-20 address as the same asset. Display the signed sponsorship amount or estimated native fee in SID before approval. Distinguish gas from PAX value sent by the transaction. Refresh rates and quotes before submission and preserve transaction evidence for accounting. Explore Unified Network , Contracts , Precompiles and xweb , which accepts SID for agent web requests.

title: Spot Exchange
content: Trade asset pairs on Paxeer X with deterministic order books, price-time matching, escrowed liquidity, and immediate two-leg settlement. Trade asset pairs on Paxeer X with deterministic order books, price-time matching, escrowed liquidity, and immediate two-leg settlement.

title: Markets and ownership
content: The LayerX spot module gives each market a base asset, quote asset, tick size, lot size, and administrator. A bid buys the base asset with quote units; an ask sells base units for quote units. Market identifiers, asset identifiers, account identifiers, and order identifiers are 32-byte values. Prices and quantities use unsigned 128-bit integer values: integrations apply the assets' unit conventions before constructing an activity. Spot runs in the LayerX execution kernel as module 10 . It settles through the asset module and uses the same deterministic price-time book engine as perpetuals. Native spot activities and the EVM exchange intent interface are distinct integration surfaces within Paxeer X. A separate Cosmos Go spot module ( modules/spot , with swap, vault, shares, stop-order, and TWAP keepers behind precompiles/spot ) is a third surface; this page covers the native kernel book and the EVM intent interface.

title: Choose an order
content: Order Price Time in force Remaining quantity Limit GTC Nonzero limit Good till cancelled Rests on the book with escrow after matching Limit IOC Nonzero limit Immediate or cancel Does not rest Market Zero in the payload Immediate or cancel Does not rest For native spot, side is bid or ask, kind is 1 for limit and 2 for market, and limit time in force is 1 for GTC or 2 for IOC. A market order executes against available opposing liquidity. Use a limit IOC when the strategy needs an explicit price boundary.

title: Matching and fills
content: The matching engine selects the best opposing price first, the earliest global sequence second, and the order identifier as the final deterministic tie breaker. Every fill uses the resting maker's price. Matching reduces the maker's remaining quantity and escrow; a completely filled maker leaves the book.

title: Worked example
content: An ask offers 5 base units at a price of 100 quote units per base unit. An incoming limit bid for 3 units at 105 crosses that ask. The trade executes at the maker price of 100: the buyer receives 3 base units, the seller receives 300 quote units, and the ask retains 2 units. This example uses whole units for readability; encoded values follow the market's asset-unit, tick, and lot conventions.

title: Escrow and settlement
content: A resting ask escrows its remaining base quantity. A resting bid escrows the quote amount required by its price and remaining quantity. Each fill settles the base transfer and quote transfer immediately as lxp_transfer_leg entries with reason LXP_REASON_ESCROW_CAPTURE ( 5 ); locking escrow uses LXP_REASON_ESCROW_LOCK ( 4 ) and refunds use LXP_REASON_ESCROW_RELEASE ( 6 ). Spot keeps no separate shadow balance: asset-module ownership, pause rules, account namespaces, and debit authorization apply to settlement. After cancellation or execution, reconcile the order's remaining quantity and the asset account state together. An accepted submission identifies an attempted activity; the resulting receipt and state establish the execution outcome. An agent should record its order identifier before submission and retain the corresponding activity and receipt evidence.

title: Native activity reference
content: Activity Type Canonical payload Create market 0x000A0001 Market, base asset, quote asset, tick size, lot size, administrator Place order 0x000A0002 Market, order, base account, quote account, side, kind, time in force, price, quantity Cancel order 0x000A0003 Market and order identifiers Halt market 0x000A0004 Market identifier Resume market 0x000A0005 Market identifier ORDER_PLACE: 163 bytes market_id[32] || order_id[32] || base_account_id[32] || quote_account_id[32] || side:u8 || kind:u8 || time_in_force:u8 || price:u128be || quantity:u128be ORDER_CANCEL: 64 bytes market_id[32] || order_id[32] Market creation uses a 160-byte payload; halt and resume use 32 bytes. Escrow identifiers are derived from the market and asset rather than supplied by the caller. Encode canonical big-endian integers and exact field widths.

title: Agent trading workflow
content: Resolve the market's base and quote assets, trading increments, and halted state. Check the strategy's authorized accounts and available asset balances. Choose a price boundary, quantity, order kind, and time in force; allocate and persist an order identifier. Submit the canonical native activity through the LayerX client and retain its activity identifier. Verify the receipt, account changes, fills, and residual order state before updating inventory. Cancel a residual quote using its market and order identifiers. Reconcile the cancellation result before treating its reserved inventory as available for another order. Market-making agents can quote both sides, cancel stale quotes, and adjust inventory using the same accounts and matching rules as other principals. Strategy decisions remain outside consensus; order authorization, matching, and settlement follow deterministic protocol rules.

title: EVM exchange intents
content: Contracts use ILayerXExchange at 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001015 to deposit or withdraw margin, place or cancel orders, request settlement, and inspect intents. These calls record pending exchange intents for LayerX routing. Their EVM events are submission evidence; LayerX executes the corresponding trading operation. The interface's state views require a batch number and native state witness. They verify the witness against the batch's finalized anchored state root. Its order interface uses its own time-in-force encoding: 0 GTC, 1 IOC, 2 fill or kill, and 3 post-only. Preserve each surface's encoding when building an adapter; do not copy native spot enum values into this ABI.

title: Capacity and operational refusals
content: The native module supports 64 markets and 256 resting orders per market. One activity produces at most 8 fills and 18 transfer legs. These are compile-time execution bounds: strategies split large operations and reconcile each result rather than assuming unlimited book traversal. A duplicate market returns LXP_ERR_MARKET_ALREADY_EXISTS ; order placement on a halted market returns LXP_ERR_MARKET_HALTED . Asset mismatch, paused assets, unauthorized debits, unknown account namespaces, sequence reuse, and noncanonical payloads also refuse execution. Correct the underlying account, market, or encoding condition before submitting a new operation.

title: Continue building
content: See Market Makers for quoting and ramp inventory workflows, Precompiles for contract integration, and Modules for execution capabilities. Protocol references: include/layerx/lx_spot.h , src/modules/spot/lx_spot_market.c , src/modules/spot/lx_spot_book.c , src/modules/spot/lx_spot_dispatch.c , and precompiles/layerxexchange/LayerXExchange.sol .

title: Bounded Storage Scans
content: Iterate Paxeer X program state with deterministic ordering, explicit page budgets, scope-bound continuation cursors, and metered canonical results. Iterate Paxeer X program state with deterministic ordering, explicit page budgets, scope-bound continuation cursors, and metered canonical results.

title: Read a namespace in bounded pages
content: The guest host function layerx_v2.storage_scan_scoped returns ordered key/value pairs matching a byte prefix. Every call declares an entry ceiling and a complete encoded-page byte ceiling. A portable continuation token resumes after the last returned key across activities without retaining a host iterator or allocator handle. This is a Candidate-V2 host function, validated through the candidate path; the frozen V1 ABI is unchanged. Confirm that your target admits layerx_v2 programs before depending on scans in production. Use scans for bounded indexes, application inventories, and paginated state processing. Design keys with stable prefixes and choose page sizes that fit the call's storage-read and output transport budgets. The function scans one authorized namespace, rather than exposing arbitrary kernel state.

title: Host-call contract
content: storage_scan_scoped( raw_selector: i32, prefix_pointer: i32, prefix_length: i32, cursor_pointer: i32, cursor_length: i32, max_entries: i32, max_bytes: i32, output_pointer: i32, output_capacity: i32 ) -> i32 Input Contract Selector 1 Principal-scoped namespace; requires StorageRead and the matching access declaration. Selector 2 Shared program namespace; requires SharedStorageRead and the matching access declaration. Prefix At most 256 bytes. An empty prefix selects all keys within the namespace. Cursor Empty starts a scan. A nonempty token must match the same namespace, prefix, and limits. Entry ceiling Between 1 and 64 entries per page. Page byte ceiling Between 5 and 67,126,228 complete encoded bytes. Output range A valid guest-memory buffer large enough for the encoded result. Return value Nonnegative encoded byte length on success; a negative host status on refusal. The host validates the output range before reading the prefix and cursor. It previews and encodes the page, checks output capacity, charges the storage-read meter, then copies bytes to guest memory. A negative length, invalid selector, out-of-memory range, or denied read is rejected before output is written.

title: Decode the canonical page
content: All lengths below are big-endian. Parse only the number of bytes returned by the host, validate each length against the remaining buffer, and require the cursor fields to agree. Field Width Entry count u16 For each entry: key length, key u16 followed by key bytes For each entry: value length, value u32 followed by value bytes Has-cursor flag u8: 0 or 1 Cursor length, cursor u16 followed by cursor bytes; zero length when no cursor # Empty terminal page: 5 bytes 00 00 00 00 00 # One entry, key "a", value "b", no continuation: 13 bytes 00 01 00 01 61 00 00 00 01 62 00 00 00 The complete encoding consumes the storage-read budget, including counts, lengths, cursor bytes, and the five-byte empty page. Allocate room for continuation metadata as well as the key/value content. A page with one short entry and a continuation can be larger than a terminal page with several short entries.

title: Resume without changing scan identity
content: The cursor binds version, canonical namespace, prefix, entry ceiling, byte ceiling, and the last returned key. Treat its bytes as an opaque continuation token in application code. Reuse them exactly with the same selector, program, principal where applicable, prefix, and both limits. Changing a limit to increase page size requires starting a new scan with an empty cursor. A principal cursor cannot resume in shared scope or under another program. Corrupted bytes, trailing bytes, empty last-key fields, and keys inconsistent with the prefix are invalid. The maximum encoded cursor size is 591 bytes.

title: Pagination workflow
content: Choose the authorized scope and stable prefix. Select both page ceilings and allocate a guest output buffer. Call with an empty cursor and check the signed return status before decoding memory. Decode the complete page, process its entries, and retain the exact continuation bytes. When a cursor is present, invoke again with unchanged scan identity and limits. Stop when the page has no continuation cursor. Each resumed activity reads its current authorized state. The cursor identifies a position and scan contract; it does not claim that all pages share a frozen historical state. For an application that needs a consistent export, bind the surrounding workflow to its own verified state and mutation policy.

title: Two independent page bounds
content: The scan stops before exceeding the entry count. It also checks the complete encoded size when adding each matching entry. If an entry would exceed the page-byte limit, it is removed and the preceding entries return with a cursor. If no entry can fit, the scan refuses with a bounds status rather than returning an ambiguous empty continuation. For the canonical short-key fixture, three pairs (a,a) , (b,b) , and (c,c) form a 29-byte terminal page. With a fourth pair and limits (64, 101) , the first page contains two entries plus continuation and occupies 101 bytes. A 100-byte limit yields one entry plus continuation at 93 bytes.

title: Refusals and unchanged output
content: Status Meaning Response -1 denied Missing matching read authority or access declaration. Supply the correct admitted grant and scope. -2 invalid Malformed input, invalid selector or limits, or a mismatched cursor. Correct the request; restart pagination if identity changes. -3 bounds Oversized prefix/cursor, invalid memory range, insufficient output capacity, or no entry fitting the page ceiling. Correct memory bounds or start a new scan with suitable limits. -4 meter Insufficient admitted storage-read budget for the encoded page. Increase the activity budget within admitted ceilings. Refusals before charging leave storage-read usage unchanged. A refused charge produces no partial page. The host writes output only after validation and metering succeed, so output bytes remain unchanged on these refusal paths. Never interpret preexisting buffer contents as a fresh page after a negative return.

title: Determinism, writes, and rollback
content: Storage is ordered by program, scope, and key. Within the chosen namespace, entries return in canonical key order independent of insertion order. Equivalent state and scan inputs produce equivalent pages, usage, and evidence. A scan sees writes already staged in the same activity because both use the activity's storage snapshot. A successful activity commits those writes. A later trap discards the staged mutation and returns the runtime-fault outcome without a successful response. Do not treat a page observed inside a failed guest execution as committed state. Read Programs for call budgets, response transport, and receipt verification, or the developer workspace for conformance and ABI checks. Technical references: Storage Scan protocol documentation; runtime host scan, storage scan, scoped storage authorization, and storage-scan conformance tests.

title: Storage
content: State commitment, historical queries, receipt retention, and backend configuration in Paxeer. State commitment, historical queries, receipt retention, and backend configuration in Paxeer.

title: Overview
content: Paxeer storage separates active state commitment from historical state queries and receipt storage. Each has its own configuration and retention behavior. The implementation is under Paxeer-X-Network/storage/ .

title: State Commitment
content: The state-commit layer under storage/state_db/sc/ includes MemIAVL, FlatKV, and a composite store that routes state operations. It participates in application commitment, snapshot import/export, and supported proof queries. The default write mode is memiavl_only . Other named modes support staged migration to FlatKV. Select routing modes according to the existing data layout and the chain's migration plan. # app.toml [state-commit] sc-enable = true sc-write-mode = "memiavl_only" Source: storage/config/sc_config.go , storage/config/write_mode.go , storage/state_db/sc/composite/store.go .

title: Historical State Store
content: The state-store layer maintains versioned key/value data for historical queries. Configure imported data and retention for the historical range you need. Commitment proofs also require the corresponding commitment-store history. # app.toml [state-store] ss-enable = true ss-backend = "pebbledb" ss-keep-recent = 100000 The default backend is Pebble and the default retention is 100,000 versions. ss-keep-recent = 0 retains all available versions. The config also supports a separate EVM historical store through evm-ss-split ; its data routing and missing-key behavior differ from the unsplit store. Source: storage/config/ss_config.go , storage/config/toml.go , storage/state_db/ss/ .

title: RocksDB Backend
content: The optional RocksDB backend uses user-defined timestamps and column families for versioned state. Build it from the Paxeer subtree: make build-rocksdb make install-rocksdb After installing the compatible binary, set ss-backend = "rocksdb" under [state-store] . When changing backends, import or restore data in the target backend's format. Compare backends with the same revision, hardware, retained history, and request workload. Measure historical-query latency, iteration time, disk usage, and write throughput for the operations your application uses. Source: chain.mk — build-rocksdb , install-rocksdb (the root Makefile delegates to chain.mk through PAXEER_MAKE ); storage/db_engine/rocksdb/mvcc/opts.go .

title: Receipts and Blocks
content: # app.toml: root setting must precede section headers min-retain-blocks = 100000 [receipt-store] rs-backend = "pebbledb" The receipt configuration accepts pebbledb or its pebble alias. Set receipt retention with the root min-retain-blocks setting and historical state retention with ss-keep-recent . --mode archive configures block and SS retention to zero, preserving imported history and subsequent state. Start with a dataset covering the historical range you plan to serve. Source: storage/config/receipt_config.go , node/params/config.go — setArchiveTypeAppConfig .

title: Snapshots and Recovery
content: Application snapshots, commitment-store snapshots, and filesystem backups are distinct. Use the mechanism and directory layout matching your build. Stop a node before replacing its data, preserve validator last-sign state, and keep a compatible copy of the configuration and genesis. Changelogs and write-ahead logs support storage replay and recovery. Follow the recovery procedure for the selected store, and preserve consensus signer state alongside the validator key. Source: storage/wal/ , storage/state_db/sc/composite/ , consensus/privval/file.go .

title: Inspection Tools
content: The separate PaxDB command provides storage inspection and benchmark operations. Build or run it from the Paxeer subtree, using its help to select the correct database path and height: go run ./storage/tools/cmd/paxdb --help go run ./storage/tools/cmd/paxdb dump-iavl --help go run ./storage/tools/cmd/paxdb dump-db --help Beyond inspection, paxdb provides dump-flatkv and import-flatkv-from-memiavl for FlatKV export and migration, migrate-evm-status for EVM status migration, prune for version pruning, and replay-changelog for changelog replay. Run these operations through paxdb . Use an offline copy when an operation needs exclusive database access. Source: storage/tools/cmd/paxdb/main.go , storage/tools/cmd/paxdb/operations/ .

title: Streaming Payments
content: Pay for elapsed time or verified usage with funded, capped streams, deterministic accrual, settlement, and cancellation. Pay for elapsed time or verified usage with funded, capped streams, deterministic accrual, settlement, and cancellation.

title: Continuous Commerce on Paxeer X
content: Streams turn ongoing work into incremental payment obligations. Time streams support service retainers, compute reservations, and recurring agent work. Metered streams pay for signed usage readings such as completed requests or consumed resources. Both use an isolated agent:<did>:stream:<id> account and settle through 402LXP transfer legs. Accrual and settlement are separate: accrual calculates how much the recipient has earned, while settlement transfers available funds. A stream has a lifetime cap and can be topped up, paused, resumed, or closed by its payer.

title: Choose a Payment Mode
content: Mode Accrual input Typical use Time ( 1 ) Elapsed batch time in milliseconds, bounded by the stream end time. Agent availability, access, subscriptions, reserved compute. Metered ( 2 ) Increase in a signed cumulative meter reading. API calls, work units, bandwidth, resource consumption.

title: Opening and Funding a Stream
content: Set the stream ID, dedicated account, recipient, asset, mode, rate, rate unit, start and end timestamps, total cap, and positive initial funding. Amounts and rates use integer asset base units. The payer supplies authorized funds; the stream account must differ from the recipient account. For time mode, rate_unit is a time interval in milliseconds. For metered mode, it is a quantity of meter units. A metered stream registers between one and eight authority keys in strictly increasing order. A time stream has no meter authorities.

title: Accrual Formula
content: new_amount = floor((rate × delta + remainder_carry) / rate_unit) new_amount = min(new_amount, total_cap - accrued_total) claimable = accrued_total - settled_total payment = min(claimable, stream_account_balance) The remainder carries across accrual calculations so frequent settlement does not repeatedly discard fractional base units. Batch timestamps provide a shared clock; regressing timestamps fail. Reaching the cap stops additional accrual.

title: Time Stream Example
content: Fund a stream with 600 base units and set a lifetime cap of 600. Set rate = 10 and rate_unit = 60000 , paying 10 base units per minute. After 15 active minutes, 150 units have accrued. Settle to pay those 150 to the named recipient. Pause for five minutes, then resume. The paused interval earns no additional time payment. Close after another 10 active minutes. With sufficient funding, closing pays the remaining 100 accrued units and refunds the unused 350 to the payer.

title: Metered Stream Workflow
content: A meter authority signs the stream ID, cumulative reading, and authority key under the LXP:STREAM:METER:v1 message tag. The stream verifies the Ed25519 signature and checks that the key belongs to its registered authority set. For a rate of 20 base units per 100 usage units, a reading increase from 1,000 to 1,250 accrues 50 base units. Readings cannot move backward. Repeating a reading produces no new accrual; multiple authority keys attest to the same cumulative meter rather than maintaining independent counters. Submit authenticated readings, then settle the accrued amount. Meter readings accepted while paused or underfunded advance the meter baseline without accruing payment, preventing that recorded usage from being charged retroactively when payment resumes.

title: Funding, Claims, and Cancellation
content: Action Behavior Top up Add authorized funds to an existing open stream. Funding does not increase its lifetime cap. Settle / claim Pay accrued, unsettled value to the fixed recipient, limited to the funded balance. Pause Payer checkpoints time accrual and stops further earning while paused. Resume Payer restarts from the current batch timestamp without charging paused time. Rate change Replace the rate for subsequent accrual under a fresh idempotency key, without reopening the stream. Close / cancel Payer settles payable accrued value, refunds the excess balance, and permanently closes the stream.

title: Underfunding
content: If settlement cannot cover all accrued value, it pays the available balance, resets accrued value to the settled total, and marks the stream underfunded. This does not preserve an unpaid debt balance. Accrual stops while underfunded. A top-up clears underfunding and starts the next time-accrual interval at the top-up timestamp. Maintain funding for continuous service. Monitor the stream balance, earned amount, cap, pause state, and underfunding state together. A payment cap limits earned value; a funded balance determines what settlement can actually pay.

title: Closing a Stream
content: Closing a funded active time stream first accounts for eligible elapsed time. It pays the recipient up to the available balance and returns the rest to the payer in the same transfer set. Closing is final: the stream cannot resume or receive further top-ups.

title: Protocol Reference
content: Streams are module 4 , with payload version 1 . The version prefix is two bytes, 00 01 . Activity Type Payload bytes LX_STREAM_OPEN 0x00040001 204 + 32 per authority LX_STREAM_TOP_UP 0x00040002 50 LX_STREAM_METER 0x00040003 138 LX_STREAM_SETTLE 0x00040004 66 LX_STREAM_PAUSE 0x00040005 34 LX_STREAM_RESUME 0x00040006 34 LX_STREAM_CLOSE 0x00040007 66 LX_STREAM_RATE_CHANGE 0x00040008 82 The rate-change payload carries the stream ID, a new rate as an unsigned 128-bit integer, and an idempotency key. It changes the rate applied to subsequent accrual; already-accrued and settled amounts are not recomputed.

title: Retries and Validation
content: Settle and close include a nonzero idempotency key. Retry the same economic operation with its original key and retain the result receipt. A key cannot identify a different stream or operation. Reject malformed versions, trailing payload bytes, meter regressions, unauthorized meters, and operations against a closed stream. Funding, draws, and refunds use published transfer assets and follow asset pause and asset-match rules. The stream account only permits its protocol-authorized draw and refund paths.
